## 2. ACCESSIBILITY — hard numbers

Ran Wix's official full-site accessibility scan.

| Metric | Result |
|---|---|
| Pages discovered | 51 |
| Pages scanned | 39 |
| **Pages that failed to analyze** | **12** |
| Total findings | **1,099** |
| Critical | **2** |
| Serious | 1,097 |
| Pages affected | 38 of 39 |

**By category:** screen reader 1,080 · alternative text 1,069 · color contrast 19 · heading structure 9 · keyboard 2

### 2.1 The two criticals

Both are `inaccessible-component` — a component that can't provide keyboard or assistive-tech behavior at all (WCAG 4.1.2, Level A).
- **Homepage** (element `comp-jqh1ozf6`)
- **Contact page**

### 2.2 Biggest concentration

**`/sermons` alone accounts for 1,031 of the 1,099 findings.** These are `media-alternatives` — video and audio with no captions, transcripts, or text alternative. 337 distinct media items.

### 2.3 Homepage heading structure

The homepage is flagged for **missing a main heading or skipping heading levels**. "WHO WE ARE" renders as an H2 with no H1 above it. This hurts screen readers *and* SEO.

### 2.4 The 12 pages that couldn't be scanned

`/ministries` · `/serve` · `/outreach` · `/previous-events-1` · `/tithes-and-offerings` · `/book-online` · `/booking-form` · `/cart-page` · `/payment-request-page` · `/s-projects-basic` · 2 booking service pages

Failure code: `ANALYSIS_FAILED`. This usually means the page is heavy or slow enough that the renderer timed out. **Worth treating as a performance red flag**, not just a scanner quirk — `/ministries` is one of your main pages.

---

## 3. CONTENT ERRORS

### 3.1 Leaders page — needs a full copy pass

**The meta description in Google right now literally reads:**
> "Recommended Meta Description for the Meet Our Leaders page: 'Meet the passionate pastors, ministers, and leaders of Arise Church…'"

The AI prompt label got pasted in with the answer. This is live in search results.

**Name mismatches:**
- Heading "Chad and Tabitha **Kerik**" → body says "Chad and Tabitha **Ker**"
- Heading "Will **Robinson**" → body says "Will **Robertson**"

**Truncated sentences (words missing mid-phrase):**
- "a source of ___ and strength for our community"
- "are truly remarkable ___ of our church community"
- "as one of our esteemed ___, leads with passion"
- "contributes to our community in ___ and impactful ways"
- "a committed member of ___ praise and worship team"
- "shine through in all ___ efforts"

**Tone inconsistency:** Bryant Sanders' bio is written in **second person** ("We are truly honored to have **you** lead us… **your** years of dedicated ministry"). Every other bio is third person. It reads like an appreciation card dropped into a staff directory.

**Layout:** Ethan Mayes has **no photo**. Vanessa Sanders' photo is 344×400; everyone else is 251×344.

**Titles:** Vanessa is called both "Pastor" and "Prophet" in one sentence. Bryant is "Apostle." Norman is "elder." No consistent title convention, and the top leader appears second in the list.

**Image filenames = alt text:** `image0 (2).png`, `image2.png`, `image3.png`, `image5.png`, `image6.png`, `image7.png`. Straight off a phone.

### 3.2 Ministries page

**Four of eight "Learn More" buttons are dead** — plain text, no link:
- Thrive For Young Adults
- Mvmt 6:14
- Worship Team
- In Edge / X Edge

Working: Lead Network (→ `/general-4`), Children's, Youth, Outreach.

**"Lead Network" points to `/general-4`** — a default Wix slug. Should be `/lead-network`.

**Image filenames leaking into URLs and alt text:**
- `ChatGPT Image May 14, 2025, 04_36_03 PM.png`
- `515499984_1033890948907446_8820358226701242830_n_edited_edited.jpg` (Facebook download)
- `Untitled design.png`
- `Pasted_Image_t1qdjcue.png`
- `Movment.PNG` — misspelled

### 3.3 Homepage

- Two missing periods: "join our vibrant community Here" and "…each person brings"
- No address, no "plan your visit," no next step for a first-time visitor.
- Prayer Request is a **`mailto:` link**. These fail silently on most phones, and you keep no record of the request.

**CORRECTION — service times.** My first pass said service times appear nowhere. **That was wrong.** They're in a custom-coded "Service Times ▾" dropdown, **top-right of the homepage hero, above the fold.** My method (reading server-rendered HTML) can't see client-side Velo output, so I reported an absence I hadn't established.

**Placement is good.** Above the fold, top-right is a conventional spot for utility info, and "Service Times" is the exact phrase visitors scan for. Three fixable things:

**1. Measured contrast failure.** Sampling the actual pixels of the button:

| Measurement | Ratio | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| White text vs. average panel color | **3.91:1** | Passes AA for large bold text (3.0) · **fails AA for normal text (4.5)** |
| White text vs. lightest 10% of panel | **2.18:1** | **Fails AA at any text size** |

The panel is translucent, so its color is whatever the hero image is behind it. Across that strip of the hero, background luminance ranges from 0.004 to 1.000 — **near the full possible range.** As the hero image changes, or on a different slide of that carousel, the text can land on near-white and become nearly unreadable. This is almost certainly among the 19 `color-contrast` findings in §2.

*Fix:* give the panel a solid or near-solid fill (85–100% opacity) instead of relying on the image behind it. That alone takes it well past 4.5:1 and makes it stable regardless of the background.

**2. It's collapsed by default.** The single most-searched fact about a church costs a click. Service times are 2–4 short lines — there's room to show them expanded. Keep the control for a full schedule, but let the core times render immediately.

**3. It's not in the server-rendered HTML.** The complete server-rendered text of the homepage is: nav → "WHO WE ARE" → welcome paragraph → prayer quote → footer. **No time strings anywhere.** Crawlers read that first; Google runs JavaScript on a slower, less reliable second pass, and collapsed content is deprioritized regardless. Third-party directories publishing invented hours is weak circumstantial support that they didn't see yours either.

*Fix:* keep the dropdown, and **also** emit the times as plain text plus JSON-LD (§12). Additive, not a redesign.

### 3.3b Homepage carousel is the critical accessibility failure

The critical finding `comp-jqh1ozf6` is a **stock Wix media Carousel rendered inside an iframe** (`Carousel.b605841e.html`) — not custom code. Carousels rendered that way can't expose keyboard or screen-reader behavior, which is why it trips WCAG 4.1.2 Level A.

### 3.3c Header branding

The header wordmark is **"# YouBelongHere"** — the church's name doesn't appear in the header at all. It's a strong tagline, but a first-time visitor landing from a search result has no name-level confirmation they're in the right place until they scroll to the logo in the hero.

### 3.4 Two campuses — the site never says so

**CORRECTION:** I flagged Pineville / Tioga / Alexandria as a three-town contradiction. It isn't. **Tioga is a town inside Pineville**, so "Impact Tioga" and the Pineville branding are consistent. And the two addresses are **two real campuses**:

| Campus | Address | Role |
|---|---|---|
| **Main** | 501 Ates Road, Pineville, LA 71360 | Primary |
| **Second** | 5305 North Blvd, Alexandria, LA 71301 | Second campus |

**The real problem is that a visitor can't tell any of this.** The Contact page has an **"Our Locations" heading with nothing under it**, then two bare addresses with no labels, no campus names, and no indication which is main. Nothing anywhere else on the site mentions being multi-campus.

A two-campus church needs this to be obvious — it changes where someone drives on Sunday. Recommended: a real **Locations** page (or a Locations section in the nav), each campus with its own name, address, map, times, and photo.

### 3.4b Confirmed service times

| When | What |
|---|---|
| **Sunday 10:30am** | Service |
| **Monday 7pm** | — |
| **Wednesday 7pm** | — |
| **Monday–Thursday 5am** | Corporate Prayer |

These now need to land in three places: the existing dropdown (already done), plain text in the page body, and JSON-LD structured data (§12). *Pending: whether both campuses share this schedule, and what the Monday/Wednesday 7pm gatherings are called.*

### 3.5 Contact info sprawl — four addresses

- `info.arisenow@gmail.com` — Wix site contact setting
- `arisenow.church@gmail.com` — Contact page
- `arisechurchprayer@gmail.com` — Prayer request
- `(318) 640-1865`

All gmail, on a premium plan with a custom domain. Also, the Contact page renders the email address **as an H2 heading**, which is semantically wrong.

### 3.6 Third-party listings are publishing confirmed misinformation

**Both of these are now confirmed wrong by Bradly:**

| Listings say | Reality |
|---|---|
| Lead Pastor **Chad Stecker** | **No longer connected to the church** |
| **Assemblies of God** | **Independent** — no longer affiliated |

This isn't a stale-data nitpick anymore. Directories with real search visibility are naming a former leader and a denomination you've left. Someone searching "Arise Church Pineville" can land on these before they ever reach your site.

Sites carrying it: JoinMyChurch, UnitedStatesChurches, YellowPages, FindOpen, Wikizer, PlaceDigger.

FindOpen also publishes hours you never set (Sun 9:00–13:00, Tue 18:30–20:00, Wed 18:30–20:30) — all wrong against the confirmed schedule in §3.4b.

**Priority: high.** Claim Google Business Profile first (it feeds many others), then work down the list. Both campuses need their own profile.

---

## 4. SEO

| Issue | Detail |
|---|---|
| Missing meta descriptions | `/contact`, `/arise-bible`, `/information-desk-registration` |
| Broken meta description | `/leaders` (contains the AI prompt label) |
| Weak title | "Contact \| arisechurch" — no city, no keywords |
| Brand inconsistency | Lowercase "arisechurch" in all titles |
| 404 in index | `/arise-team` needs a 301 redirect |
| No structured data | No Church / LocalBusiness JSON-LD found — this is what powers Google's service-times panel |
| Social links inconsistent | Homepage: FB, IG, Twitter. Contact: FB, Twitter, IG, YouTube. Twitter icons still branded Twitter, not X. |
| Thin homepage | Very little indexable text for your most important page |

---

## 5. UPGRADES & ENHANCEMENTS

### Tier 1 — fast, free, high impact
1. **Make the existing service times machine-readable.** Keep the dropdown; additionally emit the times as plain text in the page body (and in JSON-LD, §12) so crawlers and scrapers get them without a click. Adding the address alongside them is the natural pairing.
2. **"Plan Your Visit" page** — times, parking, what to wear, what happens with kids, who to look for.
3. Fix the 4 dead "Learn More" buttons.
4. Full copy pass on Leaders (names, truncated sentences, meta description, Ethan's photo).
5. 301 redirect `/arise-team`.
6. Delete Portfolio demo content and `/s-projects-basic`.
7. Fix the raw-URL link in the header.
8. Alt-text pass on the top 8 pages.

### Tier 2 — structural
9. Nav restructure (§1.7).
10. Surface the store, giving page, classes, and programs.
11. Move email to `@arisecenla.church` addresses.
12. **Add Church schema markup** — Velo is already enabled, so JSON-LD can be injected sitewide. This is what gets service times into Google's sidebar.
13. **Captions/transcripts on sermons** — YouTube auto-captions can be pulled and attached. Clears the majority of your 1,099 findings and makes sermons searchable.
14. Convert Prayer Request from `mailto:` to a real Wix Form.
15. Claim and correct Google Business Profile and the directory listings.
16. Investigate why 12 pages fail to render for the scanner.

### Tier 3 — bigger plays
17. Live-stream embed on the homepage that appears during service.
18. Sermon archive with notes, scripture references, and series grouping.
19. Wix Members Area is installed — is it doing anything?
20. Wix Multilingual is installed but the site is English-only. For a self-described multicultural church, Spanish is an obvious opportunity.
21. Wix Chat is installed — an unmonitored chat widget is worse than none.
22. Consolidate giving: one path, not two.

---

## 6. INSTALLED APPS — usage check

Installed: Promote SEO · Bookings · Chat · Events & Tickets · Forms · Forms & Payments · Groups · Invoices · Members Area · **Multilingual** · Online Programs · Pay Links · **Portfolio** · Stores · Video

Several look installed-but-idle (**Portfolio** is definitely just demo content). Every unused app adds page weight and clutter. Worth an audit of which ones earn their place.

# PAGE 1 — HOME
**Full build guide · Wix Editor (classic) · building directly on the live site**

Open `arise-homepage-redesign.html` in a second window and keep it beside the Editor. That's your visual target; this is the instruction set.

**Estimated time:** Step 0–1 about 40 minutes. Sections 2–10 about 2–3 hours, and you can stop after any section.

---

## STEP 0 — Safety net (2 minutes, do not skip)

1. Editor → top bar → **Site History**
2. Note the topmost entry — date and time. That's your restore point.
3. Close the panel.

If anything goes wrong at any stage: Site History → select that entry → **Restore**.

> Publish only when a section is finished and looks right. A half-built section left published is the one thing worth avoiding.

---

## STEP 1 — Global settings (~40 min, before any layout)

**Everything below inherits from these. Do them first or you'll rebuild the page.**

### 1a. Colors

**Site Design (paintbrush icon) → Color → Edit Colors**

| Slot | Set to | Where it's used |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `#FFFFFF` | Light sections |
| 2 | `#F4F2F0` | Alternating sections |
| 3 | `#0A0A0C` | Dark sections, header, footer |
| 4 | `#D6222D` | **Arise Red** — buttons, dashes, strips, badges |
| 5 | `#DB3F48` | Small red text **on dark only** |
| 6 | `#6A6A6E` | Body text on light backgrounds |

**Remove** the blue `#0088CB` and yellow `#FFCB05`. Your brand kit says Arise Red is the only accent.

| Theme | Font | Size | Settings |

| Heading 2 | Anton | 46px | UPPERCASE, letterspacing 6, line height 1.02 |
| Heading 3 | Anton | 22px | UPPERCASE, letterspacing 4 |
| Heading 4 | Oswald Medium | 13px | UPPERCASE, letterspacing 12 |
| Paragraph 1 | Oswald Light | 17px | line height 1.6 |
| Paragraph 2 | Oswald Light | 14.5px | line height 1.7 |

**Never set Anton below 18px.** It's designed for 148pt thumbnail headlines; small, it becomes an unreadable block.

# Batch 1 — Brand Alignment
**Arise Church · arisecenla.church**
Everything here is either a file you can use or a step you click. **I have changed nothing on your live site.**

---

## A note on what I can and can't do

I checked the Wix API surface directly: **Wix exposes no REST endpoint for site theme colors or typography.** Palette and font changes live in the Editor only. So Section 2 below is instructions for you, not something I can push.

What I *can* do through the API when you say go: SEO tags and meta descriptions, structured data, the Bookings cleanup (2022 conference, online class), and CMS work. That's Batch 2.

---

## 1. Logo files — ready to use

Your source was 304×274, RGB, white baked in. I un-matted it (proper alpha reconstruction, so the grunge texture and soft edges survive) and produced four files.

| File | Size | Use it for |
|---|---|---|
| `arise-logo-transparent@4x.png` | 1216×1096 | **Main file.** Header, hero, anywhere on light or dark |
| `arise-logo-transparent.png` | 304×274 | Native resolution, if you need the original size |
| `arise-logo-white@4x.png` | 1216×1096 | Solid white version for dark backgrounds and the near-black header |
| `arise-logo-brandred@4x.png` | 1216×1096 | Texture preserved, recolored to exactly **#D6222D** |

### How the "A" behaves — check `logo-preview.png`

The A is a **knockout** — an open counter, not a filled shape. It connects to the outside edge of the flame, so it takes on whatever is behind it:

- **On white** → A reads white. Correct.
- **On #0A0A0C near-black** → A goes dark. Still high contrast against the red. **Looks good** — see the preview.
- **On a busy photo** → the photo shows through the A. Avoid this; use the white version instead.

I could not auto-fill the A to solid white because it isn't an enclosed region. Filling it properly needs the vector source.

### The real fix

**304×274 is too small.** For a retina header you want 600px+ wide natively; for print or signage you need vector. My 4× files are resampled — sharper in use, but no new detail was invented.

**Ask whoever made the logo for the `.ai`, `.eps`, or `.svg`.** If nobody has it, it's worth paying someone to redraw it once. That single file solves the header, print, favicon, and social sizes permanently.

---

## 2. Wix Editor steps — colors and fonts

### 2a. Colors

**Editor → Site Design (paintbrush) → Color**

| Slot | Currently | Change to | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| `color_3` | `#ED1C24` | **`#D6222D`** | Brand kit is canonical |
| `color_2` | `#000000` | **`#0A0A0C`** | Brand near-black |
| `color_4` | `#0088CB` blue | retire | Kit: "Arise Red is the only accent" |
| `color_5` | `#FFCB05` yellow | retire | Same |

Leave whites alone. Retiring 4 and 5 means repointing anything using them to red, black, or grey — check as you go.

### 2b. Fonts

**Editor → Site Design → Text → Upload Fonts.** Anton, Oswald, and Bebas Neue are all free on Google Fonts.

| Style | Font | Treatment |
|---|---|---|
| Heading 1 / 2 | **Anton** | Uppercase always, letterspacing ~6 |
| Kicker / eyebrow | **Oswald Medium** | Uppercase, letterspacing ~14 |
| Body / buttons | **Oswald Regular** | Sentence case fine |
| Reserve | Bebas Neue | Alternate condensed display |

**One caution.** Anton is very heavy and very condensed. It's built for 148pt thumbnail headlines — at 24–32pt web subheads it gets dense fast. My suggestion: **Anton for H1 and hero only, Oswald for everything below.** Try one page before rolling it out site-wide.

### 2c. Service Times button

Same panel. Set the fill to **85–100% opacity** instead of translucent. Fixes the 2.18:1 contrast failure. Appearance otherwise unchanged.

---

## 3. Service times — corrected

Your brand kit says only *"Sundays 10:30 AM · Monday night Glory Nights."* That's incomplete. Actual:

| When | What | Where |
|---|---|---|
| **Sunday 10:30 AM** | Sunday Service | **Both campuses** |
| **Monday 7:00 PM** | **Glory Night** | Main campus |
| **Wednesday 7:00 PM** | Midweek Service | Main campus |
| **Mon–Thu 5:00 AM** | Corporate Prayer | Main campus |

Two things worth saying plainly: **"Glory Night" appears nowhere on your website** despite being a named format with its own YouTube playlist. And **Corporate Prayer at 5am, four mornings a week, is a genuine differentiator** — no other church in your comparison set offers anything like it.

---

## 4. Plan Your Visit — copy, ready to paste

Written in your brand voice: direct, warm, unhurried, specific. No hype.

---

### Plan Your Visit

**Sunday at 10:30 AM. Both campuses. Come as you are.**

**Where we meet**
Main Campus — 501 Ates Road, Pineville, LA 71360
Alexandria Campus — 5305 North Blvd, Alexandria, LA 71301

Sunday service runs at both. Everything during the week meets at the Main Campus.

**Parking**
Park wherever there's room. We have parking ushers on Sunday mornings — follow their direction and they'll get you where you need to be.

**What to wear**
There's no dress code. You'll see jeans and you'll see suits. Come as you are — we mean it.

**When to arrive**
If it's your first time, come a little early. It gives you room to park without rushing, find a seat you like, and meet somebody before the service starts.

**During the week**
Glory Night — Mondays at 7:00 PM
Midweek Service — Wednesdays at 7:00 PM
Corporate Prayer — 5:00 AM, Monday through Thursday

All at the Main Campus. Corporate Prayer is early and it's open to anyone.

**Who we are**
We're multiethnic and multigenerational. Our heart is to help you CONNECT with God and His family, GROW in God's character, SERVE in God's Church, and SHARE God's message.

---

## 5. Leaders page — corrected copy

Only the errors are fixed. Titles and names kept exactly as you confirmed.

**Chad and Tabitha Kerik** — *"Ker" → "Kerik", missing word restored*
> Chad and Tabitha Kerik not only serve as Elders, but they also take on the vital roles of our Youth Ministers and Leaders of Thrive for young adults. Their dedication and passion for youth and young adult ministry shine through in all their efforts. For more information about their ministries and how you can get involved, be sure to check out our Ministry section!

**Bryant Sanders** — *rewritten in third person, as you approved*
> Apostle Bryant Sanders leads Arise Church and serves as Leader of the Lead Network. His years of dedicated ministry and guidance shape the direction of this church, and his leadership is a source of strength for our community.

**Herbert and Erica Perry** — *two missing words restored*
> Herbert and Erica Perry are truly remarkable members of our church community. Their unwavering dedication and commitment inspire us all. Herbert, as one of our esteemed ministers, leads with passion and grace, setting a shining example for everyone. We are grateful for their contributions and the positive impact they have on our congregation.

**Will Robertson** — *heading corrected from "Robinson"; two missing words restored*

The heading said **Robinson**, the body said **Robertson**. These are two different people: **Kristina Robinson** is the Praise Team Leader; **Pastor Will Robertson** is a Minister. The heading had borrowed the wrong surname. The body was right all along.

> Will Robertson is an exceptional pastor and an even more extraordinary individual! As an essential member of our Pastoral Team, he contributes to our community in meaningful and impactful ways. His kindness and compassion shine through in all his efforts, positively influencing the lives of those he serves. We are truly fortunate to have him on our team!

**Ethan Mayes** — *missing word restored*
> Ethan Mayes is a committed member of our praise and worship team and is also one of our ministers. His passion and dedication to serving the community are inspiring. We are grateful for all the effort and love you bring to everything you do, Ethan! Thank you for your positive impact!

> **Worth flagging:** your brand kit says the voice is *direct, warm, unhurried, specific — no hype, no marketing voice.* These bios lean on "esteemed," "truly remarkable," "exceptional... and an even more extraordinary individual!" I've left that tone intact because you said the page was otherwise correct. If you want, I'll do a second pass rewriting all seven to match your own voice guide.

**Also still open:** Ethan has no image element on the live page, while all six others do. Worth opening that page in the Editor.

---

## 6. Meta description fix

Live on `/leaders` right now, visible in Google:

> "Recommended Meta Description for the Meet Our Leaders page: 'Meet the passionate pastors...'"

Replace with:

> Meet the pastors, ministers, and leaders of Arise Church in Pineville and Alexandria, LA — the team serving our multiethnic, multigenerational church family.

**I can push this one through the SEO API the moment you say go.**

---

## 7. Suggested order

1. Upload the transparent logo — immediate, visible, zero risk
2. Change `color_3` to `#D6222D` — one field
3. Service Times panel to solid fill — fixes the contrast failure
4. Load Anton + Oswald, test on **one page** before going site-wide
5. Paste the corrected Leaders copy
6. Tell me to push the meta description fix and the Bookings cleanup

---

## Open questions

1. **Will Robinson or Will Robertson?**
2. Anton on all headings, or Anton for H1/hero only and Oswald below?
3. Should **Glory Night** get its own page, or just a named line in the Service Times dropdown?
4. Do you want the full voice rewrite of all seven leader bios?
5. Does anyone have the logo vector (`.ai` / `.eps` / `.svg`)?
6. Green light to push the meta description + Bookings cleanup via API?
=== EMAIL-BUILD-SPEC ===
# Arise Church — Email Build Spec

For building the form emails in a drag-and-drop editor. Four emails, shared styling, exact values.

---

## Shared rules — apply to all four

### Colors

| Use | Hex |
|---|---|
| Brand red — bars, buttons, accents | **`#D6222D`** |
| Light red — small red text **on black only** | **`#DB3F48`** |
| Near-black — headers, footers | **`#0A0A0C`** |
| Bone — quote blocks, page background | **`#F4F2F0`** |
| Body text on white | **`#4A4A4E`** |
| Headings / strong text on white | **`#0A0A0C`** |
| Muted text on black | **`#8D8D92`** |

> **Never put `#D6222D` text on black** — it fails contrast at small sizes. Use `#DB3F48` there.

### Font

**Arial** (or Helvetica) throughout. Not Anton, not Oswald.

Email clients don't load web fonts — the site's fonts would silently fall back and look broken. Bold Arial with wide letterspacing gets close enough.

| Element | Size | Weight | Letterspacing | Case |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Big headline | 34px | Bold | 1px | UPPERCASE |
| Section heading | 27px | Bold | 1px | UPPERCASE |
| Small red label | 11px | Bold | **3px** | UPPERCASE |
| Field label | 11px | Bold | **2px** | UPPERCASE |
| Body | 16px | Regular | 0 | Sentence |
| Greeting | 17px | Regular | 0 | Sentence |
| Button | 12px | Bold | **3px** | UPPERCASE |
| Footer small | 13px | Regular | 0 | Sentence |

**The wide letterspacing is the signature.** If the builder won't do letterspacing, use bold uppercase and accept it.

### Layout

- Width **600px**, centred, on a `#F4F2F0` background
- Content padding **32px** left and right
- Line height **1.7** on body text

### Buttons

Rectangular, **no rounded corners**. Fill `#D6222D`, white bold text, padding **15px vertical / 32px horizontal**.

### The red double-dash

Appears above the small red label in every header. Two red rectangles, **34×5px**, **12px apart**, `#D6222D`.

If the builder can't do that, use a single **80×5px** red bar instead.

---

# EMAIL A — Staff alert

**Trigger:** `formSubmission` → arisenow.church@gmail.com
**Subject:** `New {{formType}} submission from {{name}}`

| # | Block | Content |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Divider | Solid `#D6222D`, 6px tall, full width |
| 2 | Header — bg `#0A0A0C`, padding 28/32 | Double-dash · label **NEW SUBMISSION** in `#DB3F48` 11px · heading **{{formType}} FORM** white 27px |
| 3 | Detail rows — white bg | Five rows, thin `#E6E4E2` line between each |
| 4 | Quote block | bg `#F4F2F0`, **5px `#D6222D` left border**, padding 22/24 |
| 5 | Button | **REPLY TO {{name}}** → `mailto:{{email}}` |
| 6 | Footer — bg `#0A0A0C` | "Sent from the website form · also saved in CMS › Form Submissions" in `#8D8D92` 12px |

**Detail rows** — label left (110px wide, `#D6222D`, 11px bold, 2px spacing), value right (`#0A0A0C`, 16px):

`NAME` {{name}} · `EMAIL` {{email}} · `PHONE` {{phone}} · `SUBJECT` {{subject}} · `POSITION` {{position}}

**Quote block:** label `MESSAGE` in `#D6222D`, then {{message}} at 16px.

---

# EMAIL B — Contact confirmation

**Trigger:** `formReceived` where `formType` = **contact**
**Subject:** `We got your message`

| # | Block | Content |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Divider | `#D6222D`, 6px |
| 2 | Hero — bg `#0A0A0C`, padding 40/32 | Double-dash · **ARISE CHURCH** in `#DB3F48` · headline **WE GOT YOUR MESSAGE.** white 34px — **the full stop in `#D6222D`** |
| 3 | Body — white | See copy below |
| 4 | Quote block | bg `#F4F2F0`, 5px red left border. Label `WHAT YOU SENT`, then {{message}} |
| 5 | Line | One sentence, see below |
| 6 | Times row | Thin lines above and below. Left: **Sunday Service** / 10:30 AM · both campuses. Right: **Glory Night** / Mondays 7:00 PM |
| 7 | Button | **PLAN YOUR VISIT** → `https://www.arisecenla.church/contact` |
| 8 | Footer | Standard, below |

**Body copy:**

> Hi {{name}},
>
> Thanks for reaching out to Arise Church. We've got your message and someone will get back to you soon.
>
> If you need to add anything, just reply to this email.

**Block 5:**

> We'd love to see you on a Sunday — and you're welcome exactly as you are.

---

# EMAIL C — Serve confirmation

**Trigger:** `formReceived` where `formType` = **serve**
**Subject:** `Thanks for signing up to serve`

Same structure as B, with these changes:

**Hero:** label **SERVE WITH US** · headline **THANKS FOR STEPPING UP.**

**Body copy:**

> Hi {{name}},
>
> We've got your sign-up, and someone from that team will reach out about next steps.
>
> You don't need experience — just a willingness to show up. We'll take it from there.

**Quote block** — label `YOU SIGNED UP FOR`, then:
- **{{position}}** on its own line, **19px bold `#0A0A0C`**
- then {{message}} at 15px in `#4A4A4E`

**Block 5:** "Questions before then? Just reply to this email."

**Button:** **SEE ALL MINISTRIES** → `https://www.arisecenla.church/ministries`

---

# EMAIL D — Prayer confirmation

**Trigger:** `formReceived` where `formType` = **prayer**
**Subject:** `We're praying with you`

**Deliberately quieter than the others.** No button, no service-times row, no invitation push. Someone sending a prayer request is in a different frame of mind, and a marketing email would land badly.

| # | Block | Content |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Divider | `#D6222D`, 6px |
| 2 | Hero | Double-dash · **PRAYER REQUEST** in `#DB3F48` · headline **WE'RE PRAYING WITH YOU.** — full stop in `#D6222D` |
| 3 | Body | See below |
| 4 | Quote block | Label `YOUR REQUEST`, then {{message}} |
| 5 | Thin line, then one sentence | See below |
| 6 | One more line | See below |
| 7 | Footer | **Main Campus address only**, no second campus |

**Body copy:**

> Hi {{name}},
>
> Thank you for trusting us with this. Our prayer team has your request, and we're praying.
>
> You're not carrying it alone.

**Block 5:** "If there's more you'd like us to know, just reply to this email."

**Block 6:** "Corporate Prayer meets Monday to Thursday at 5:00 AM at the Main Campus. You're welcome any morning."

---

## Footer — B and C

Background `#0A0A0C`, padding 28/32.

- **ARISE CHURCH** — white 13px bold, 2px letterspacing, uppercase
- 501 Ates Road, Pineville, LA 71360 — `#8D8D92` 13px
- 5305 North Blvd, Alexandria, LA 71301 — `#8D8D92` 13px
- **arisecenla.church** — `#DB3F48` 12px bold, 2px spacing, uppercase, links to the site
- "This is an automatic confirmation — a real person will reply separately." — `#6A6A6E` 11px

**Email D:** same, but Main Campus address only and no website link.

**No phone number in any of them.**

---

## Variables

`formType` · `name` · `email` · `phone` · `subject` · `position` · `message`

Insert with the builder's variable picker, not by typing `{{name}}`.

---

## If the builder can't branch on formType

Use **Email B** for all three confirmations. It reads fine across the board.

Better a working general email than a clever broken one — but if branching is available, **D is worth having separately.** The tone difference matters most there.

---

## Before going live

Send yourself one of each and **open them on your phone in Gmail.** That's where most people will read them, and it's the fastest way to catch anything that didn't survive the builder.

# Arise Church — Email Build Spec

For building the form emails in a drag-and-drop editor. Four emails, shared styling, exact values.

---

## Shared rules — apply to all four

### Colors

| Use | Hex |
|---|---|
| Brand red — bars, buttons, accents | **`#D6222D`** |
| Light red — small red text **on black only** | **`#DB3F48`** |
| Near-black — headers, footers | **`#0A0A0C`** |
| Bone — quote blocks, page background | **`#F4F2F0`** |
| Body text on white | **`#4A4A4E`** |
| Headings / strong text on white | **`#0A0A0C`** |
| Muted text on black | **`#8D8D92`** |

> **Never put `#D6222D` text on black** — it fails contrast at small sizes. Use `#DB3F48` there.

### Font

**Arial** (or Helvetica) throughout. Not Anton, not Oswald.

Email clients don't load web fonts — the site's fonts would silently fall back and look broken. Bold Arial with wide letterspacing gets close enough.

| Element | Size | Weight | Letterspacing | Case |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Big headline | 34px | Bold | 1px | UPPERCASE |
| Section heading | 27px | Bold | 1px | UPPERCASE |
| Small red label | 11px | Bold | **3px** | UPPERCASE |
| Field label | 11px | Bold | **2px** | UPPERCASE |
| Body | 16px | Regular | 0 | Sentence |
| Greeting | 17px | Regular | 0 | Sentence |
| Button | 12px | Bold | **3px** | UPPERCASE |
| Footer small | 13px | Regular | 0 | Sentence |

**The wide letterspacing is the signature.** If the builder won't do letterspacing, use bold uppercase and accept it.

### Layout

- Width **600px**, centred, on a `#F4F2F0` background
- Content padding **32px** left and right
- Line height **1.7** on body text

### Buttons

Rectangular, **no rounded corners**. Fill `#D6222D`, white bold text, padding **15px vertical / 32px horizontal**.

### The red double-dash

Appears above the small red label in every header. Two red rectangles, **34×5px**, **12px apart**, `#D6222D`.

If the builder can't do that, use a single **80×5px** red bar instead.

---

# EMAIL A — Staff alert

**Trigger:** `formSubmission` → arisenow.church@gmail.com
**Subject:** `New {{formType}} submission from {{name}}`

| # | Block | Content |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Divider | Solid `#D6222D`, 6px tall, full width |
| 2 | Header — bg `#0A0A0C`, padding 28/32 | Double-dash · label **NEW SUBMISSION** in `#DB3F48` 11px · heading **{{formType}} FORM** white 27px |
| 3 | Detail rows — white bg | Five rows, thin `#E6E4E2` line between each |
| 4 | Quote block | bg `#F4F2F0`, **5px `#D6222D` left border**, padding 22/24 |
| 5 | Button | **REPLY TO {{name}}** → `mailto:{{email}}` |
| 6 | Footer — bg `#0A0A0C` | "Sent from the website form · also saved in CMS › Form Submissions" in `#8D8D92` 12px |

**Detail rows** — label left (110px wide, `#D6222D`, 11px bold, 2px spacing), value right (`#0A0A0C`, 16px):

`NAME` {{name}} · `EMAIL` {{email}} · `PHONE` {{phone}} · `SUBJECT` {{subject}} · `POSITION` {{position}}

**Quote block:** label `MESSAGE` in `#D6222D`, then {{message}} at 16px.

---

# EMAIL B — Contact confirmation

**Trigger:** `formReceived` where `formType` = **contact**
**Subject:** `We got your message`

| # | Block | Content |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Divider | `#D6222D`, 6px |
| 2 | Hero — bg `#0A0A0C`, padding 40/32 | Double-dash · **ARISE CHURCH** in `#DB3F48` · headline **WE GOT YOUR MESSAGE.** white 34px — **the full stop in `#D6222D`** |
| 3 | Body — white | See copy below |
| 4 | Quote block | bg `#F4F2F0`, 5px red left border. Label `WHAT YOU SENT`, then {{message}} |
| 5 | Line | One sentence, see below |
| 6 | Times row | Thin lines above and below. Left: **Sunday Service** / 10:30 AM · both campuses. Right: **Glory Night** / Mondays 7:00 PM |
| 7 | Button | **PLAN YOUR VISIT** → `https://www.arisecenla.church/contact` |
| 8 | Footer | Standard, below |

**Body copy:**

> Hi {{name}},
>
> Thanks for reaching out to Arise Church. We've got your message and someone will get back to you soon.
>
> If you need to add anything, just reply to this email.

**Block 5:**

> We'd love to see you on a Sunday — and you're welcome exactly as you are.

---

# EMAIL C — Serve confirmation

**Trigger:** `formReceived` where `formType` = **serve**
**Subject:** `Thanks for signing up to serve`

Same structure as B, with these changes:

**Hero:** label **SERVE WITH US** · headline **THANKS FOR STEPPING UP.**

**Body copy:**

> Hi {{name}},
>
> We've got your sign-up, and someone from that team will reach out about next steps.
>
> You don't need experience — just a willingness to show up. We'll take it from there.

**Quote block** — label `YOU SIGNED UP FOR`, then:
- **{{position}}** on its own line, **19px bold `#0A0A0C`**
- then {{message}} at 15px in `#4A4A4E`

**Block 5:** "Questions before then? Just reply to this email."

**Button:** **SEE ALL MINISTRIES** → `https://www.arisecenla.church/ministries`

---

# EMAIL D — Prayer confirmation

**Trigger:** `formReceived` where `formType` = **prayer**
**Subject:** `We're praying with you`

**Deliberately quieter than the others.** No button, no service-times row, no invitation push. Someone sending a prayer request is in a different frame of mind, and a marketing email would land badly.

| # | Block | Content |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Divider | `#D6222D`, 6px |
| 2 | Hero | Double-dash · **PRAYER REQUEST** in `#DB3F48` · headline **WE'RE PRAYING WITH YOU.** — full stop in `#D6222D` |
| 3 | Body | See below |
| 4 | Quote block | Label `YOUR REQUEST`, then {{message}} |
| 5 | Thin line, then one sentence | See below |
| 6 | One more line | See below |
| 7 | Footer | **Main Campus address only**, no second campus |

**Body copy:**

> Hi {{name}},
>
> Thank you for trusting us with this. Our prayer team has your request, and we're praying.
>
> You're not carrying it alone.

**Block 5:** "If there's more you'd like us to know, just reply to this email."

**Block 6:** "Corporate Prayer meets Monday to Thursday at 5:00 AM at the Main Campus. You're welcome any morning."

---

## Footer — B and C

Background `#0A0A0C`, padding 28/32.

- **ARISE CHURCH** — white 13px bold, 2px letterspacing, uppercase
- 501 Ates Road, Pineville, LA 71360 — `#8D8D92` 13px
- 5305 North Blvd, Alexandria, LA 71301 — `#8D8D92` 13px
- **arisecenla.church** — `#DB3F48` 12px bold, 2px spacing, uppercase, links to the site
- "This is an automatic confirmation — a real person will reply separately." — `#6A6A6E` 11px

**Email D:** same, but Main Campus address only and no website link.

**No phone number in any of them.**

---

## Variables

`formType` · `name` · `email` · `phone` · `subject` · `position` · `message`

Insert with the builder's variable picker, not by typing `{{name}}`.

---

## If the builder can't branch on formType

Use **Email B** for all three confirmations. It reads fine across the board.

Better a working general email than a clever broken one — but if branching is available, **D is worth having separately.** The tone difference matters most there.

---

## Before going live

Send yourself one of each and **open them on your phone in Gmail.** That's where most people will read them, and it's the fastest way to catch anything that didn't survive the builder.

   A Wix "Embed HTML" element is an <iframe>. Nothing inside an iframe can

   WHY THIS INSTEAD OF THE HTML EMBED
   ----------------------------------
   A Wix "Embed HTML" element is an <iframe>. Nothing inside an iframe can
   paint outside it — not with position:fixed, not with overflow:visible, not
   with any z-index. Bringing it to front doesn't help, because the limit is
   the iframe's own edge, not stacking order. That's why the expanded panel
   stops dead at the box boundary.

   A Custom Element renders into the REAL page DOM. No iframe, no boundary.

   This build goes one step further: when you open it, the panel is appended
   to document.body and positioned with fixed coordinates measured from the
   button. That means it escapes not just the iframe (gone) but also any
   Wix strip or section with overflow:hidden. It will overlap anything.
--- arise-service-times-v2.js ---

1	=================== FORMS-SETUP.md ===================
2	# Forms — built into the layout
3	
4	**Yes, the forms can live inside the elements and route themselves.**
5	
6	I was wrong earlier when I said they couldn't. Custom elements can't call Velo *backend modules* — but they **can** fetch a **Velo HTTP Function**, which is a real URL on your own site. Same origin, no auth, no page code.
7	
8	One element, three forms, one backend file.
9	
10	---
11	
12	## How it works
13	
14	```
15	arise-form element  →  POST /_functions/ariseForm  →  http-functions.js
16	                                                         ├── saves to Form Submissions (CMS)
17	                                                         └── emails the right address
18	```
19	
20	Which form appears is set by an attribute in the Editor:
21	
22	| Page | Attribute | Fields | Goes to |
23	|---|---|---|---|
24	| Contact | `data-form="contact"` | Name, Email, Phone, Subject, Message | arisenow.church@gmail.com |
25	| Serve | `data-form="serve"` | Name, Email, Phone, Position, Notes | arisenow.church@gmail.com |
26	| Anywhere | `data-form="prayer"` | Name, Email, Prayer Request | arisechurchprayer@gmail.com |
27	
28	The **Serve** form's Position dropdown is your five real roles: Children's Department, Outreach, Media/Social Media, Edge/X Edge, Maintenance.
29	
30	---
31	
32	## 1. Backend — `backend/http-functions.js`
33	
34	Velo sidebar → **Backend** → the file must be named exactly `http-functions.js`.
35	
36	```javascript
37	import { ok, badRequest, serverError } from 'wix-http-functions';
38	import wixData from 'wix-data';
39	import { triggeredEmails } from 'wix-crm-backend';
40	
41	// Where each form goes. Change these addresses if routing changes.
42	const ROUTES = {
43	  contact: 'arisenow.church@gmail.com',
44	  serve:   'arisenow.church@gmail.com',
45	  prayer:  'arisechurchprayer@gmail.com'
46	};
47	
48	function clean(v, max) {
49	  return String(v == null ? '' : v).trim().slice(0, max || 2000);
50	}
51	
52	export async function post_ariseForm(request) {
53	  try {
54	    const body = await request.body.json();
55	
56	    const formType = clean(body.formType, 40).toLowerCase();
57	    if (!ROUTES[formType]) return badRequest({ body: { error: 'unknown form' } });
58	
59	    const name    = clean(body.name, 120);
60	    const email   = clean(body.email, 200);
61	    const message = clean(body.message, 4000);
62	
63	    if (!name || !email) return badRequest({ body: { error: 'name and email required' } });
64	    if (!/^[^\s@]+@[^\s@]+\.[^\s@]+$/.test(email)) {
65	      return badRequest({ body: { error: 'invalid email' } });
66	    }
67	
68	    const record = {
69	      formType,
70	      name,
71	      email,
72	      phone:    clean(body.phone, 60),
73	      subject:  clean(body.subject, 200),
74	      position: clean(body.position, 120),
75	      message,
76	      handled:  false
77	    };
78	
79	    // 1. Always store it — nothing is lost even if email fails.
80	    await wixData.insert('FormSubmissions', record, { suppressAuth: true });
81	
82	    // 2. Notify. Requires a triggered email named "formSubmission" — see below.
83	    try {
84	      await triggeredEmails.emailContact('formSubmission', ROUTES[formType], {
85	        variables: {
86	          formType, name, email,
87	          phone: record.phone || '-',
88	          subject: record.subject || '-',
89	          position: record.position || '-',
90	          message: message || '-'
91	        }
92	      });
93	    } catch (mailErr) {
94	      console.error('Form email failed (submission still saved):', mailErr);
95	    }
96	
97	    return ok({ body: { ok: true } });
98	
99	  } catch (err) {
100	    console.error('ariseForm failed:', err);
101	    return serverError({ body: { error: 'server error' } });
102	  }
103	}
104	```
105	
106	---
107	
108	## 2. The element
109	
110	Paste `arise-form.js` into `public/custom-elements/`.
111	
112	Then on each page: **Add → Embed Code → Custom Element → Choose Source → Velo file → `arise-form.js`**, tag name **`arise-form`**.
113	
114	**Then set the attribute.** In the element's settings there's a place to add custom attributes:
115	
116	```
117	name:   data-form
118	value:  contact        (or serve, or prayer)
119	```
120	
121	Stretch it full width. That's the whole setup — same element on every page, different attribute.
122	
123	---
124	
125	## 3. Email notifications — one dashboard step
126	
127	The backend saves every submission to the CMS regardless. For email on top:
128	
129	**Dashboard → Automations → New Automation**
130	- Trigger: **Velo code trigger** (or Triggered Email)
131	- Name the trigger exactly: **`formSubmission`**
132	- Action: **Send an email**
133	- Available variables: `formType` `name` `email` `phone` `subject` `position` `message`
134	
135	**If you skip this**, submissions still save — you'd just check the CMS instead of your inbox. Nothing is lost either way.
136	
137	---
138	
139	## Where submissions live
140	
141	**CMS → Form Submissions.** Every entry has the form type, all fields, and a `handled` checkbox so you can track what's been answered.
142	
143	That's better than Wix Forms in one respect: **you own the data**, and it's queryable.
144	
145	---
146	
147	## What the visitor sees
148	
149	Required fields marked in red. Inline validation before anything is sent — empty required fields and malformed emails are caught in the browser. The email format is checked again on the server, so it can't be bypassed.
150	
151	On success, the form is replaced by a thank-you panel. On failure, an error appears **with your email address as a fallback**, so a broken form never means a lost visitor.
152	
153	---
154	
155	## Two honest notes
156	
157	**Test on the published site.** `/_functions/` URLs don't resolve in Preview.
158	
159	**This replaces the Wix form on Contact.** Once it's working, remove the old one — otherwise you have two forms doing the same job and submissions split between two places.
160	
161	=================== EVENTS-SETUP.md ===================
162	# Events — automatic from Wix Events
163	
164	Two files. Once they're in, **every event you create in Wix Events appears on the page by itself** — with its own uploaded image, the right button, and a link to its own registration page.
165	
166	Nothing to edit in code when you add an event.
167	
168	---
169	
170	## What the button says
171	
172	Read straight from each event's registration settings:
173	
174	| Event setup | Button |
175	|---|---|
176	| RSVP, open | **RSVP** |
177	| Ticketed, open | **Get Tickets** |
178	| Sold out | **Sold Out** — greyed, not clickable |
179	| Closed or ended | **View Event** |
180	| External registration | **Register** |
181	| No registration | **View Event** |
182	
183	---
184	
185	## 1. Backend — `backend/events.jsw`
186	
187	```javascript
188	import { events } from 'wix-events.v2';
189	import { elevate } from 'wix-auth';
190	
191	const elevatedQuery = elevate(events.queryEvents);
192	
193	function ctaFor(ev) {
194	  const reg = ev.registration || {};
195	  const type = reg.type;
196	  const status = reg.status || '';
197	
198	  if (reg.registrationDisabled) return { cta: 'View Event', ctaEnabled: true };
199	
200	  if (type === 'TICKETING') {
201	    if (reg.tickets && reg.tickets.soldOut) return { cta: 'Sold Out', ctaEnabled: false };
202	    if (status.indexOf('OPEN') === 0) return { cta: 'Get Tickets', ctaEnabled: true };
203	    return { cta: 'View Event', ctaEnabled: true };
204	  }
205	  if (type === 'RSVP') {
206	    if (status === 'OPEN_RSVP_WAITLIST') return { cta: 'Join Waitlist', ctaEnabled: true };
207	    if (status.indexOf('OPEN') === 0) return { cta: 'RSVP', ctaEnabled: true };
208	    return { cta: 'View Event', ctaEnabled: true };
209	  }
210	  if (type === 'EXTERNAL') return { cta: 'Register', ctaEnabled: true };
211	  return { cta: 'View Event', ctaEnabled: true };
212	}
213	
214	function shape(ev) {
215	  const dt = ev.dateAndTimeSettings || {};
216	  const f  = dt.formatted || {};
217	  const start = dt.startDate ? new Date(dt.startDate) : null;
218	  const loc = ev.location || {};
219	  const addr = (loc.address && loc.address.formatted) || '';
220	
221	  return Object.assign({
222	    id: ev._id || ev.id,
223	    title: ev.title || '',
224	    shortDescription: ev.shortDescription || '',
225	    image: (ev.mainImage && (ev.mainImage.url || ev.mainImage)) || '',
226	    dateLine: f.dateAndTime || '',
227	    startDate: f.startDate || '',
228	    startMonth: start ? start.toLocaleString('en-US', { month: 'short' }) : '',
229	    startDay: start ? String(start.getDate()) : '',
230	    location: addr || loc.name || '',
231	    url: (ev.eventPageUrl && ev.eventPageUrl.path) || ''
232	  }, ctaFor(ev));
233	}
234	
235	/**
236	 * Upcoming events (soonest first) and past events (most recent first).
237	 */
238	export async function getEvents() {
239	  try {
240	    const res = await elevatedQuery({ fields: ['DETAILS', 'TEXTS', 'REGISTRATION', 'URLS'] })
241	      .ne('status', 'CANCELED')
242	      .limit(50)
243	      .find();
244	
245	    const all = (res.items || []).map(shape);
246	    const raw = res.items || [];
247	
248	    const upcoming = [], past = [];
249	    raw.forEach((ev, i) => {
250	      const s = all[i];
251	      if (!s.url) return;
252	      if (ev.status === 'UPCOMING' || ev.status === 'STARTED') upcoming.push(s);
253	      else if (ev.status === 'ENDED') past.push(s);
254	    });
255	
256	    upcoming.sort((a, b) => (a.dateLine > b.dateLine ? 1 : -1));
257	    past.reverse();
258	
259	    return { upcoming, past: past.slice(0, 8) };
260	  } catch (err) {
261	    console.error('getEvents failed:', err);
262	    return { upcoming: [], past: [] };
263	  }
264	}
265	```
266	
267	---
268	
269	## 2. Events page code
270	
271	```javascript
272	import { getEvents } from 'backend/events.jsw';
273	
274	// Right-click the custom element -> View Properties to confirm this ID.
275	const EL = '#customElement1';
276	
277	$w.onReady(async () => {
278	  if (!$w(EL).length) {
279	    console.warn('Events: custom element ' + EL + ' not found.');
280	    return;
281	  }
282	
283	  try {
284	    const data = await getEvents();
285	    if (data && (data.upcoming.length || data.past.length)) {
286	      $w(EL).setAttribute('data-events', JSON.stringify(data));
287	      console.log('Events loaded:', data.upcoming.length, 'upcoming,', data.past.length, 'past');
288	    }
289	  } catch (err) {
290	    console.error('Events load failed:', err);
291	    // element keeps its built-in fallback
292	  }
293	});
294	```
295	
296	---
297	
298	## What the page becomes
299	
300	**Featured** — your next upcoming event, using its own uploaded poster, with the date block, time, location, and the correct button.
301	
302	**Also Coming Up** — every other upcoming event as a card.
303	
304	**Previous Events** — your past events with their real images, most recent first, capped at eight. That section was an empty placeholder before.
305	
306	You have **13 events** in Wix Events right now, so the past grid fills immediately.
307	
308	---
309	
310	## Adding a new event
311	
312	Create it in Wix Events as normal. Nothing else. The site picks up its image, dates, location, registration type and link on the next page load.
313	
314	**The image is whatever you upload as the event's main image** — so make it a good one. It's the biggest thing on the page.
315	
316	---
317	
318	## If the backend import fails
319	
320	Some sites expose the events module differently. If `wix-events.v2` errors, try:
321	
322	```javascript
323	import { events } from 'wix-events-backend';
324	```
325	
326	and drop the `elevate` wrapper — `queryEvents` on that module runs with site permissions already.
327	
328	Everything else stays the same. Tell me which one your site accepts and I'll lock the file to it.

330	=================== SERMONS-LIVE-SETUP.md ===================
331	# Sermons — Automatic Live Stream Detection
332	
333	Two files. Once these are in, the featured player switches to your live stream on its own — Sunday mornings, Monday Glory Nights, and any other time you go live.
334	
335	**No API key. No cost. Nothing to remember on a Sunday.**
336	
337	---
338	
339	## What happens
340	
341	| State | Player shows | Badge |
342	|---|---|---|
343	| **You're streaming** | The live stream | **LIVE NOW** — red, pulsing dot |
344	| Not streaming | Your most recent livestream | **Latest Service** |
345	
346	The page also **re-checks every 60 seconds**. So if a visitor opens the page five minutes before service and you start streaming, it switches over for them without a refresh.
347	
348	---
349	
350	## 1. Backend — `backend/youtube.jsw`
351	
352	Velo sidebar → **Backend** → new file named exactly `youtube.jsw`.
353	
354	```javascript
355	import { fetch } from 'wix-fetch';
356	
357	const CHANNEL_ID = 'UCGS9j7B_prcJkbTNgzlGrKg';
358	
359	// Short cache so a busy Sunday doesn't hammer YouTube.
360	let cache = { value: null, at: 0 };
361	const CACHE_MS = 45000;
362	
363	/**
364	 * Returns the videoId of the current live stream, or null when not streaming.
365	 * Reads YouTube's public /live page — no API key needed.
366	 */
367	export async function getLiveVideoId() {
368	  const now = Date.now();
369	  if (now - cache.at < CACHE_MS) return cache.value;
370	
371	  let result = null;
372	
373	  try {
374	    const res = await fetch(
375	      `https://www.youtube.com/channel/${CHANNEL_ID}/live`,
376	      { method: 'get', headers: { 'User-Agent': 'Mozilla/5.0 (compatible)' } }
377	    );
378	
379	    if (res.ok) {
380	      const html = await res.text();
381	
382	      // Signal 1 — when live, the canonical link is a watch URL.
383	      const canonical = html.match(/<link rel="canonical" href="([^"]+)"/);
384	      if (canonical && canonical[1].includes('/watch?v=')) {
385	        const id = canonical[1].split('/watch?v=')[1].split('&')[0];
386	        if (/^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{11}$/.test(id)) result = id;
387	      }
388	
389	      // Signal 2 — fallback if the canonical is missing.
390	      if (!result && html.includes('"isLive":true')) {
391	        const vid = html.match(/"videoId":"([A-Za-z0-9_-]{11})"/);
392	        if (vid) result = vid[1];
393	      }
394	    }
395	  } catch (err) {
396	    console.error('Live check failed:', err);
397	    result = null;           // fail quiet — player keeps the latest stream
398	  }
399	
400	  cache = { value: result, at: now };
401	  return result;
402	}
403	```
404	
405	---
406	
407	## 2. Past Sermons page code
408	
409	Pages → **Past Sermons** → ⋮ → Page Code.
410	
411	```javascript
412	import { getLiveVideoId } from 'backend/youtube.jsw';
413	
414	// Rename this if your element's ID differs.
415	// Right-click the custom element -> View Properties to check.
416	const ELEMENT_ID = '#customElement1';
417	
418	$w.onReady(() => {
419	  if (!$w(ELEMENT_ID).length) {
420	    console.warn('Sermons: custom element ' + ELEMENT_ID + ' not found.');
421	    return;
422	  }
423	
424	  let current = null;
425	
426	  async function check() {
427	    try {
428	      const liveId = await getLiveVideoId();
429	      if (liveId === current) return;      // nothing changed
430	      current = liveId;
431	
432	      if (liveId) {
433	        $w(ELEMENT_ID).setAttribute('data-live-video', liveId);
434	        console.log('Live stream detected:', liveId);
435	      } else {
436	        $w(ELEMENT_ID).setAttribute('data-live-video', '');
437	      }
438	    } catch (err) {
439	      console.error('Live check failed:', err);
440	    }
441	  }
442	
443	  check();                        // on load
444	  setInterval(check, 60000);      // and every 60 seconds after
445	});
446	```
447	
448	**Check the element's ID before you paste.** Right-click the custom element → View Properties. Wix usually names it `#customElement1`, but not always — and a wrong ID here fails silently.
449	
450	---
451	
452	## How the detection works
453	
454	YouTube's `/live` URL gives it away without any API:
455	
456	- **Streaming** → its canonical link points at a `watch?v=` URL
457	- **Not streaming** → it points back at the channel
458	
459	I tested this against your channel. It correctly reported not-live, and returned the channel canonical exactly as expected.
460	
461	There's a second check on `"isLive":true` in case the canonical is ever missing.
462	
463	---
464	
465	## The featured playlist
466	
467	Separately from live detection, the player's default is your **live streams playlist**:
468	
469	| Prefix | Contains |
470	|---|---|
471	| `UU` | All uploads, Shorts included |
472	| `UULF` | Long-form only |
473	| **`UULV`** | **Live streams only** ← the player uses this |
474	| `UUSH` | Shorts only |
475	
476	```
477	Channel:      UCGS9j7B_prcJkbTNgzlGrKg
478	Live streams: UULVGS9j7B_prcJkbTNgzlGrKg
479	```
480	
481	Verified — its first entry matches the newest video on your `/streams` tab.
482	
483	---
484	
485	## Testing it
486	
487	**Best test is a real one.** Next time you go live, open the Sermons page and watch the badge turn red.
488	
489	**Before then**, open the browser console on the published page. You should see the check running with no errors. When live, it logs `Live stream detected: <videoId>`.
490	
491	---
492	
493	## Honest caveat
494	
495	This reads YouTube's public HTML rather than an official API. It works today and needs no key, but YouTube could change their markup without warning.
496	
497	**If that ever happens, the page doesn't break** — it falls back to showing your most recent livestream, which during a service is usually that same stream anyway. You'd lose the LIVE badge, not the video.
498	
499	If you'd rather have something contract-backed, the official YouTube Data API does this properly with a free key. Say the word and I'll write that version instead.
500	
501	=================== SERMONS-SERIES-AUTO.md ===================
502	# Sermons — Automatic Series Detection
503	
504	The site reads your YouTube playlists and uses the most recent one as the Current Series band.
505	
506	**The habit:** when a series starts, make a YouTube playlist named after it and add the messages as you go. That's useful on YouTube anyway — and it's how the website finds out.
507	
508	---
509	
510	## How it decides — your own naming convention
511	
512	You have twelve playlists, and four already say **"Series"** in the name:
513	
514	- Fruit of the Spirit **(Series)**
515	- No Killer, No King **(Series)**
516	- The Believers Authority **(Series)**
517	- Sermon **Series**: This Is Us (2019)
518	
519	So that's the rule: **a playlist is the current series if its name contains "series".**
520	
521	Opt-in, unambiguous, nothing to maintain — and it's already how you name them. Glory Nights, Sunday Sermons, Conferences & Special Events and the rest are simply never candidates.
522	
523	An ignore list stays as a backstop in case an evergreen playlist ever gets an awkward name:
524	
525	```javascript
526	const IGNORE = ['sunday sermons', 'lead network', 'iserve september',
527	                'glory nights | arise church', 'conferences & special events',
528	                'apostle bryant sanders — messages'];
529	```
530	
531	> **Name your series playlists with "(Series)".** One word, and the website updates itself.
532	
533	---
534	
535	## Order of precedence
536	
537	1. **Manual override** — if `seriesActive` is ticked in **CMS → Site Settings**, that wins. Always.
538	2. **Auto-detect** — otherwise, the newest playlist not on the ignore list.
539	3. **Nothing** — if neither applies, the band hides itself.
540	
541	So you can always overrule it, and between series the band simply disappears.
542	
543	---
544	
545	## 1. Backend — add to `backend/youtube.jsw`
546	
547	```javascript
548	/* ---- Current series, read from the channel's playlists ---------------- */
549	
550	const IGNORE = ['sunday sermons', 'lead network', 'iserve september'];
551	
552	let seriesCache = { value: null, at: 0 };
553	const SERIES_CACHE_MS = 600000;   // 10 minutes
554	
555	/**
556	 * Returns { title, url } for the newest playlist that isn't on the ignore
557	 * list, or null. Playlists appear newest-first on the channel's tab.
558	 */
559	export async function getCurrentSeries() {
560	  const now = Date.now();
561	  if (now - seriesCache.at < SERIES_CACHE_MS) return seriesCache.value;
562	
563	  let result = null;
564	
565	  try {
566	    const res = await fetch(
567	      `https://www.youtube.com/channel/${CHANNEL_ID}/playlists`,
568	      { method: 'get', headers: { 'User-Agent': 'Mozilla/5.0 (compatible)' } }
569	    );
570	
571	    if (res.ok) {
572	      const html = await res.text();
573	      const seen = new Set();
574	
575	      // NOTE: playlist IDs come in two lengths — 13 and 34 characters.
576	      // Matching {16,} silently misses most of them.
577	      const re = /"playlistId":"(PL[A-Za-z0-9_-]{10,})"/g;
578	      let m;
579	      while ((m = re.exec(html)) !== null) {
580	        const pid = m[1];
581	        if (seen.has(pid)) continue;
582	        seen.add(pid);
583	
584	        // title sits near the id in the same block
585	        const seg = html.slice(m.index, m.index + 3000);
586	        const t = seg.match(/"title":\{"runs":\[\{"text":"([^"]{2,90})"/) ||
587	                  seg.match(/"title":\{"simpleText":"([^"]{2,90})"/);
588	        if (!t) continue;
589	
590	        const title = t[1].trim();
591	        const lower = title.toLowerCase();
592	
593	        if (IGNORE.includes(lower)) continue;
594	        if (!lower.includes('series')) continue;   // opt-in by name
595	
596	        result = {
597	          // drop a trailing "(Series)" so the heading reads cleanly
598	          title: title.replace(/\s*\(series\)\s*$/i, '').trim(),
599	          url: `https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=${pid}`
600	        };
601	        break;                       // first non-ignored = newest
602	      }
603	    }
604	  } catch (err) {
605	    console.error('Series lookup failed:', err);
606	    result = null;
607	  }
608	
609	  seriesCache = { value: result, at: now };
610	  return result;
611	}

694	## Using it day to day
695	
696	**New series starts** — make the playlist with **"(Series)"** in the name. The site picks it up within ten minutes.
697	
698	**Series ends, nothing new** — rename the playlist to drop "Series", or set the CMS override. Band disappears.
699	
700	**Want to override** — tick `seriesActive` in CMS → Site Settings and set the title. Manual always beats automatic.
701	
702	**Playlist name is the heading**, so name it the way you want it read on the site. "The Kingdom Culture of Giving" reads better than "kingdom giving series 2026".
703	
704	---
705	
706	## Two honest caveats
707	
708	**Playlist name = series name.** Whatever you type on YouTube appears on the site, "(Series)" included — so write it the way you want it read. The code strips a trailing "(Series)" for you, but nothing else.
709	
710	**This reads YouTube's public HTML**, not an official API. It works today, needs no key, and is cached for ten minutes. If YouTube changes their markup, detection stops and the band falls back to your CMS setting — or hides. **It degrades quietly; it doesn't break the page.**
711	
712	If you'd rather have something contract-backed, the official YouTube Data API does playlists properly with a free key. Say the word.

# Arise Church website — facts sheet for audit agents

Project root: `D:\projects\Arise Church Website`
Live site: https://www.arisecenla.church (Wix classic Editor, Velo enabled). Site ID `5fff0585-70f7-4075-9289-b6e4e3d38059`.
Today: 2026-09-13.

## Which files are current

- **CANONICAL element set (21 files):** `files2/arise-fixed-2026-08-23/*.js`. These supersede the same-named files in `files/`.
  13 differ from `files/` (about, childrens, connect, contact, events, footer, form, header, home, leadnetwork, outreach, serve, service-times-final, youth); 8 are byte-identical (alexandria, bible, classes, creatives, leaders, ministries, sermons + one more).
- **LEGACY / superseded (in `files/` only):** `arise-pages.js` (one file defining arise-leaders/ministries/about/contact tags — older), `arise-hero.js`, `arise-events-sermons.js`, `arise-service-times.js`, `arise-service-times-v2.js`.
- **HTML mockups** in `files/*.html` are design references (FINAL-PREVIEW.html, arise-homepage-redesign.html, page-0x-*.html, pages-05-11.html, pages-ministries-leaders.html, arise-design-system.html, service-times-*.html, EMAIL-TEMPLATES.html). They are not deployed code.
- **Docs:** `files/*.md` (setup guides, build plans) and `files2/ARISE-HANDOFF.md` (newest, Aug 23 2026), `files2/AUDIT-REPORT.md` (Aug 23 2026 audit that produced the fixed set), `files/arisecenla-audit.md` (Aug 17 2026 live-site audit).
- **CSV:** `files/PageContent.csv` (CMS PageContent seed: contentKey,page,label,text,imageUrl,image,where). `files/ArchivedFormSubmissions.csv` contains 50 real people's contact details — do NOT quote its rows.
- **Backend code (Velo `backend/`) exists ONLY as code blocks inside the .md docs** — there are no backend .js/.jsw files in the zips. Versions appear in: FORMS-SETUP.md, CONNECT-SETUP.md, ARISE-HANDOFF.md §5a (http-functions.js); EVENTS-SETUP.md (`events.jsw`) vs ARISE-HANDOFF.md §5b (`events.web.js`); CMS-SETUP.md, CONNECT-SETUP.md, CREATIVES-SETUP.md, SERVE-SETUP.md, HOME-VIDEO-SETUP.md, PAGECONTENT-SETUP.md, ALEXANDRIA-SETUP.md (content.web.js pieces — note PAGECONTENT-SETUP and ALEXANDRIA-SETUP give two DIFFERENT `getPageContent` implementations); CLASSES-SETUP.md + GALLERY-SETUP.md (gallery.web.js, page code); SERMONS-LIVE-SETUP.md + SERMONS-SERIES-AUTO.md (youtube.jsw + page code).

## Architecture (from ARISE-HANDOFF.md)

CMS collection → backend web module → page code (`$w.onReady`, sets `data-*` attribute with JSON.stringify) → custom element reads attribute and renders. Custom elements cannot call backend modules; forms `fetch('/_functions/ariseForm')` (Velo HTTP function `post_ariseForm`). Element files live in `public/custom-elements/`. Elements render in an iframe in Editor/Preview; only the published site is real. Custom-element text is invisible to Google.

Element → attributes it observes:
- arise-home: data-photos, data-news, data-culture, data-content
- arise-header / arise-footer / arise-about / arise-contact / arise-alexandria / arise-bible: data-content only
- arise-leaders: data-leaders; arise-ministries: data-ministries; arise-events: data-events ({upcoming,past}); arise-serve: data-positions; arise-connect: data-groups; arise-classes: data-classes; arise-creatives: data-depts, data-members, data-dept; galleries (childrens/youth/outreach/leadnetwork): data-photos; arise-sermons: data-live-video, data-series-active/title/line/link/button; arise-form: data-form (contact|serve|prayer); arise-service-times: none.
- `data-content` shape expected by applyContent(): `{ "<contentKey>": { text: string, image: string } }`; keys are matched to `data-ck` (text), `data-ci` (image), `data-ckrow` (unhide row when text exists).

## Canonical facts (ARISE-HANDOFF.md §9, DESIGN-BRIEF.md)

- Always write **"Arise Church"**, never bare "Arise" (standing rule 2). (AUDIT-REPORT flagged "This Is Arise" heading as the one known exception awaiting the owner's decision.)
- Service times: Sunday 10:30 AM (both campuses) · Monday 7:00 PM **Glory Night** (Main) · Wednesday 7:00 PM Midweek (Main) · Corporate Prayer 5:00 AM **Monday–Thursday** (Main). Note: `PageContent.csv` row `site.times.sunday.second` says "Sunday 10:00 AM" for Alexandria and `arise-alexandria.js` FALLBACK also says 10:00 AM — this conflicts with DESIGN-BRIEF/FINAL-BUILD-PLAN/HANDOFF (10:30 both). For query and search endpoints: each endpoint declares which fields it can filter and sort by, and with which operators. Do not import Node.js built-ins such as `fs`, `path`, or `node:*`, and do not try to write files from this code; ExecuteWixAPI only returns data from the function. ## analytics

### [Query Site Analytics](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/business-management/analytics/skills/query-site-analytics)
**Technical:** Retrieve a Wix site's analytics through the Semantic Model API. Covers listing semantic models, inspecting a model's schema (measures, dimensions, parameters), and querying model data with a required time interval, filters, sorting, paging, and human-readable formatting.

### [Analytics Dashboard Navigation](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/business-management/analytics/skills/analytics-dashboard-navigation)
**Technical:** Builds direct links to Wix Analytics dashboard pages on manage.wix.com — highlights, reports, per-domain overviews (traffic, behavior, sales, marketing), and performance insights/benchmarks. Pairs analytics data with its read API so you can answer a question via API and hand back a 'see it in your dashboard' link. Use when the user asks where something is in the Wix dashboard, wants a direct link to a dashboard page, or you need a dashboard URL to include with the result of an API operation.

## app-installation

### [List Installed Apps](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/business-management/app-installation/skills/list-installed-apps)
**Technical:** Lists all apps installed on a site using Apps Installer API. Useful for verifying app installations before making API calls and diagnosing authorization errors.

### [Install Wix Apps](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/business-management/app-installation/skills/install-wix-apps)
**Technical:** Installs Wix apps on a site using Apps Installer API. Covers enabling Velo (Wix Code), app installation, and common app definition IDs.

### [App Management Dashboard Navigation](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/business-management/app-installation/skills/app-management-dashboard-navigation)
**Technical:** Builds direct links to the app-management dashboard pages on manage.wix.com — the App Market and the installed-apps management page. Pairs installed apps with the List Installed Apps read API. Use when the user asks where something is in the Wix dashboard, wants a direct link to a dashboard page, or you need a dashboard URL to include with the result of an API operation.

---

## aria

### [Scan a Wix Site for Accessibility Issues](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/site/accessibility/skills/scan-a-wix-site-for-accessibility-issues)
**Technical:** Run a Wix accessibility scan for a full site, one page, or every page in any supported page collection, including products, blog posts, booking services, events, and restaurant pages. Poll the asynchronous scan to completion, report failed pages separately, retrieve prioritized findings, and use the returned fix guidance to help the user resolve and verify issues.

---

## blog

### [How to Create Blog Posts](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/business-solutions/blog/skills/how-to-create-blog-posts)
**Technical:** Creates and publishes blog posts using Blog Posts API. Covers resolving the required author memberId (including creating an author member when the site has none), Ricos rich content format, image upload via Media Manager, category/tag assignment, and bulk post creation.

### [Blog Dashboard Navigation](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/business-solutions/blog/skills/blog-dashboard-navigation)
**Technical:** Builds direct links to Wix Blog dashboard pages on manage.wix.com — posts list (published and draft tabs), categories, tags, writers, comment moderation, blog analytics, monetization, and settings. Pairs each main Blog entity with its read API so you can fetch an entity and hand back a 'view it in your dashboard' link. Use when the user asks where something is in the Wix dashboard, wants a direct link to a dashboard page, or you need a dashboard URL to include with the result of an API operation.

---

## bookings

### [External Calendar Integration](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/business-solutions/bookings/skills/external-calendar-integration)
**Technical:** OAuth-based integration with Google Calendar, Microsoft Outlook, and Apple Calendar. Covers authentication flows, sync configuration, and bidirectional event management.

### [End-to-End Booking Flow](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/business-solutions/bookings/skills/end-to-end-booking-flow)
**Technical:** Complete booking flow from service discovery to payment. Query services, check availability with Time Slots V2, create bookings, and process payment via eCommerce checkout.

### [Create and Update Booking Services](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/business-solutions/bookings/skills/create-and-update-booking-services)
**Technical:** Full CRUD operations for Wix Bookings services using Services API. Covers service types (APPOINTMENT, CLASS, COURSE), pricing configuration, location setup, and schedule management.

### [Multi-Resource Service Creation](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/business-solutions/bookings/skills/multi-resource-service-creation)
**Technical:** Creates resource types and individual resources using Resources API. Enables services that require multiple resources (rooms + equipment + staff) with automatic allocation.

### [Booking Service Policy Setup](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/business-solutions/bookings/skills/booking-service-policy-setup)
**Technical:** Sets up booking policies, cancellation rules, and waitlist configuration using the Booking Policies API (query, then PATCH the bookingPolicy entity with its revision). Covers cancellationPolicy, reschedulePolicy, booking-notice limits, waitlistPolicy, and participants limits — e.g. "customers can cancel up to 24 hours before".

### [Booking System Integration Gaps](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/business-solutions/bookings/skills/booking-system-integration-gaps)
**Technical:** Documents undocumented API patterns for booking payments. Covers Bookings→Ecommerce integration, booking ID transformation to catalog items, and async payment confirmation flows.

### [Bookings Staff Setup](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/business-solutions/bookings/skills/bookings-staff-setup)
**Technical:** Creates staff members and configures custom working hours using Staff API + Calendar Events API. Critical two-step process: create staff → assign schedule → create working hours events.

### [Create Class Service](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/business-solutions/bookings/skills/create-class-service)
**Technical:** Create a class booking service — e.g. 'create a yoga class for $50', 'set up a pilates class', 'add a group fitness session', 'create a weekly meditation class'. Handles group capacity, recurring session defaults, and pricing via bulkCreateServices API. Staff assignment is not used for classes.

### [Create Course Service](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/business-solutions/bookings/skills/create-course-service)
**Technical:** Create a course booking service — e.g. 'create a 6-week photography workshop', 'set up a training program', 'add a bootcamp course for $300', 'create a hidden free test course with 8 sessions'. Handles group capacity, full-course pricing, bulkCreateServices, and separate course session events via bulkCreateEvents. Staff assignment is not used for courses.

### [Create Appointment Service](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/business-solutions/bookings/skills/create-appointment-service)

### [Manage a Campaign Success Guide](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/business-management/marketing/ads/google-ads/skills/manage-a-campaign-success-guide)
**Technical:** Retrieves and manages the campaign success guide for an existing Wix Google Ads Performance Max Leads campaign. Offer it after creating a supported campaign, even while it is learning or has no metrics; that proactive offer requires approval before retrieval. A direct request to improve a campaign, see what to fix next, or show the guide is already approval to retrieve it. Also use when a user reports completing or wants to reopen a guide item. Treat a clear completion report as an actionable update request even when phrased as a statement. Covers campaign selection, prioritized guide retrieval, and suggestion status updates without redundant confirmation. REST base https://www.wixapis.com/pa-platform/suggestions/v1.

### [Generate a Marketing Plan and Schedule Its Posts](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/business-management/marketing/skills/generate-a-marketing-plan-and-schedule-its-posts)
**Technical:** End-to-end flow to generate an AI-powered social media marketing plan for a site and schedule its generated posts for publishing, using the Wix Marketing Plan API. Recommends configuring marketing settings (goal, tone, cadence, content pillars) before the first generation, generates the plan asynchronously, polls until it's ready, then schedules the DRAFT posts. Includes generating posts for additional activities. Use for 'generate a marketing plan', 'create a social media plan/calendar', or 'schedule my plan's posts' requests.

### [Create and Publish a Social Media Post (with AI generation)](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/business-management/marketing/skills/create-and-publish-a-social-media-post-with-ai-generation)
**Technical:** End-to-end flow to create a social media post, optionally generating it with AI, and publish or schedule it to a site's connected channel (Instagram, Facebook, LinkedIn, X/Twitter, TikTok, Pinterest, YouTube, Google Business Profile) using the Wix Publisher API. Can generate a full per-channel post from a free-text idea or from the site's own assets (products, blog posts, events, bookings, coupons, categories), generate caption/title suggestions, and edit an existing image with AI. Settles the post content with you first, then confirms the channel is connected, checks premium quota, creates a draft, and publishes now or schedules it. Use for 'create a post', 'generate a post from my product/idea', 'write a caption', 'caption ideas/suggestions', 'edit a post image with AI', 'post to Instagram/Facebook/TikTok', 'connect my Instagram/Pinterest/LinkedIn', or 'schedule a post'.

### [Marketing Dashboard Navigation](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/business-management/marketing/skills/marketing-dashboard-navigation)
**Technical:** Builds direct links to Wix marketing dashboard pages on manage.wix.com — the social posts hub (drafts, scheduled and published posts across connected channels), post design templates, saved designs, and the email marketing pages (campaigns list, campaign templates, campaign analytics). Pairs each main marketing entity (social post item, connected social account, marketing-plan post, email campaign) with its read API so you can fetch an entity and hand back a 'view it in your dashboard' link. Pairs each main Stores/eCommerce entity with its read API so you can fetch an entity and hand back a 'view it in your dashboard' link. **Technical:** Mandatory first recipe for every Wix Stores Catalog V3 create-product request. Before any mutation, require an explicit name and price for every product; an absent price is never 0. If no product is identified, offer both image-upload and text-description paths and stop. If name or price is missing, ask or offer a suggestion and stop. When both are present, create from the supplied details without requiring optional enrichment. Covers single/bulk creation, inventory, physical/digital products, images, options, variants, SKUs, and validation.
