### Query existing items with filter, sort, paging, projection and total count calculation
```javascript
curl -X POST \
'https://www.wixapis.com/wix-data/v2/items/query' \
-H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
-H 'Authorization: <AUTH>' \
-d '{
    "dataCollectionId": "cities",
    "query": {
        "filter": {
            "state": "California"
        },
        "sort": [
            {
                "fieldName": "population",
                "order": "ASC"
            }
        ],
        "paging": {
            "limit": 2
        },
        "fields": ["population"]
    },
    "returnTotalCount": true
}'
```
--- Method Response Shape ---

## Method Response Shape

```json
{
  "dataItems": [
    "object"
  ],
  "pagingMetadata": {
    "count": "integer<int32>",
    "offset": "integer<int32>",
    "total": "integer<int32>",
    "tooManyToCount": "boolean",
    "cursors": "object"
  }
}
```
--- Code Example: Query existing items ---

### Query existing items
```javascript
curl -X POST \
'https://www.wixapis.com/wix-data/v2/items/query' \
-H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
-H 'Authorization: <AUTH>' \
-d '{
    "dataCollectionId": "cities",
    "query": {
        "filter": {
            "state": "California"
        },
        "paging": {
            "limit": 2
        }
    }
}'
```
--- Method Description ---
## Method Description:
Retrieves a list of items, on the basis of the filtering, sorting, and paging preferences you provide.

Choose between offset and cursor paging:

- Use `query.paging` (offset) when each request needs its own `filter` or `sort`, or when you need `returnTotalCount`.
- Use `query.cursorPaging` to continue an existing result set by reusing the cursor returned in `pagingMetadata.cursors`. Define `filter` and `sort` on the first request only — follow-up cursor requests should pass only the returned cursor, because `filter` and `sort` are ignored on subsequent cursor requests.

For date and datetime fields, write filter values as `{"$date":"2026-05-05T00:00:00.000Z"}` (plain ISO 8601 strings are also accepted).

To inline related items in each result, set `includeReferences`. If a reference or multi-reference field can contain more items than you want to inline, page the base query first and then call [Query Referenced Data Items](https://dev.wix.com/docs/rest/business-solutions/cms/data-items/query-referenced-data-items) for the specific item and field you want to expand.

Learn more about [API Query Language](https://dev.wix.com/api/rest/getting-started/api-query-language).
## Method Permissions:
WIX_DATA.QUERY
## Method Permissions Scopes:
Read Data Items: SCOPE.DC-DATA.READ

--- Method Description ---
## Method Description:
Searches for items in a collection on the basis of the filtering, sorting, searching, and paging preferences you provide.

Learn more about [API Query Language](https://dev.wix.com/api/rest/getting-started/api-query-language).

> **Notes:**
> - You can only search collections [created in the CMS](https://support.wix.com/en/article/cms-formerly-content-manager-creating-a-collection) or with the [Data Collections API](https://dev.wix.com/docs/rest/business-solutions/cms/data-collections/introduction). Searching isn't currently supported for [Wix app collections](https://support.wix.com/en/article/cms-formerly-content-manager-working-with-wix-app-collections), [external collections](https://dev.wix.com/docs/develop-websites/articles/databases/external-databases/overview/integrating-external-databases-with-your-wix-site) or [Wix Blocks](https://dev.wix.com/docs/build-apps/develop-your-app/frameworks/wix-blocks/about-wix-blocks).
> - Filtering is only supported for fields explicitly defined in the [data collection structure](https://dev.wix.com/docs/rest/business-solutions/cms/data-collections/introduction#data-collections-and-their-structure). Fields not defined in the collection structure cannot be used for filtering.
> - Searching for data items is always [eventually consistent](https://dev.wix.com/docs/rest/business-solutions/cms/eventual-consistency).

### Supported filter operators by field type

# About the Wix Data APIs

> **Note for app developers:** Wix Data APIs require the site's [code editor](https://dev.wix.com/docs/develop-websites/articles/get-started/development-environments) to be enabled. If you are building a Wix app, add a [data collections extension](https://dev.wix.com/docs/build-apps/develop-your-app/extensions/backend-extensions/data-collections/about-data-collections-extensions) to automatically enable the code editor and create data collections when your app is installed on a site.

The Wix Data APIs provide a complete solution for accessing, organizing, configuring, and managing data stored in a Wix site's database.

## Wix Data APIs

Wix Data APIs include:
- **[Data items](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/business-solutions/cms/data-items/introduction):** Access, manage, and perform aggregations on data items stored in a site's existing data collections.
- **[Collection management](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/business-solutions/cms/collection-management/introduction):** Create and configure data collections, manage access permissions, and organize a site's data structure.
- **[Operations](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/business-solutions/cms/operations/introduction):** Manage background processes and maintenance tasks for a site's data.
- **[External databases](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/business-solutions/cms/external-databases/introduction):** Connect external databases to a Wix site, allowing you to manage and query external data as if it were stored in native Wix collections.

## Before you begin

It's important to note the following points before starting to code:

- A Wix site's database can hold up to 1,000 data collections.
- The maximum size of an item you can save to a collection is 500 kb.
- When naming fields in data collections, we recommend avoiding special characters. You can do this by using field names that match this regex pattern: `[a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_-]{0,63}`.
- Each data collection defines a schema of fields for the items it contains. However, this schema isn't enforced. This means that if you add or update an item containing a field or data type that doesn't match the collection's schema specification, your data is stored anyway.

# Querying Indexed Data

Indexes accelerate filtering and sorting queries of certain types. Data queries are carried out by calling [Query Data Items](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/business-solutions/cms/data-items/query-data-items). For details of the query language used in data queries, see [API Query Language](https://dev.wix.com/api/rest/getting-started/api-query-language).

## Filtering

Indexes accelerate queries based on equality operators, such as `eq` and `in`. They also accelerate queries based on range operators, such as `gt`, `gte`, `lt`, and `lte` under certain circumstances. Indexes don't accelerate queries based on the case insensitive `startsWith` operator.

The order of fields in an index determines when and how filter queries use the index to save time.

For example, consider a collection containing information about paintings. The collection has an index for fields called `artist` (in ascending order), `dateCompleted` (in ascending order), and `title` (in ascending order), respectively.

Queries that filter based on the fields in the following orders can use the index to find the resulting entries more quickly:
- `artist` alone.
- `artist` and `dateCompleted`.
- `artist`, `dateCompleted`, and `title`.

A query that filters based on the `dateCompleted` field or the `title` field first doesn't use the index and will iterate through all items in the collection.

A query based on `artist` and `title` uses the index for looking up values in the `artist` field, but then iterates through all of the resulting items for the query of the `title` field. The index thus improves the speed of this query, but only partially.

Note that queries can use an index to accelerate a range filter (such as `gt`, `gte`, `lt`, or `lte`) only if it is the last filtering action of the query. | Boolean | `$eq`, `$ne`, `$exists` |
| Array of strings | `$hasSome`, `$hasAll`, `$exists` |
| Array, Document Array, Object, Any, Media Gallery | `$exists` |

# About the Wix Data APIs

> **Note for app developers:** Wix Data APIs require the site's [code editor](https://dev.wix.com/docs/develop-websites/articles/get-started/development-environments) to be enabled. If you are building a Wix app, add a [data collections extension](https://dev.wix.com/docs/build-apps/develop-your-app/extensions/backend-extensions/data-collections/about-data-collections-extensions) to automatically enable the code editor and create data collections when your app is installed on a site.

The Wix Data APIs provide a complete solution for accessing, organizing, configuring, and managing data stored in a Wix site's database.

## Wix Data APIs

Wix Data APIs include:
- **[Data items](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/business-solutions/cms/data-items/introduction):** Access, manage, and perform aggregations on data items stored in a site's existing data collections.
- **[Collection management](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/business-solutions/cms/collection-management/introduction):** Create and configure data collections, manage access permissions, and organize a site's data structure.
- **[Operations](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/business-solutions/cms/operations/introduction):** Manage background processes and maintenance tasks for a site's data.
- **[External databases](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/business-solutions/cms/external-databases/introduction):** Connect external databases to a Wix site, allowing you to manage and query external data as if it were stored in native Wix collections.

## Before you begin

It's important to note the following points before starting to code:

- A Wix site's database can hold up to 1,000 data collections.
- The maximum size of an item you can save to a collection is 500 kb.
- When naming fields in data collections, we recommend avoiding special characters. You can do this by using field names that match this regex pattern: `[a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_-]{0,63}`.
- Each data collection defines a schema of fields for the items it contains. However, this schema isn't enforced. This means that if you add or update an item containing a field or data type that doesn't match the collection's schema specification, your data is stored anyway.

The Data Items API allows you to access and manage items in a Wix site's data collections.

With the Data Items API, you can:

- Create and manage data items in a site's collections.
- Publish and unpublish data items through an editorial draft lifecycle.
- Retrieve data items from a collection individually or with filtering and sorting queries.
- Create and manage reference fields.
- Update or remove many items asynchronously by filter.
- Perform aggregations and calculations on data in collections.
- Run advanced aggregation pipelines for complex data transformations.
- Truncate a data collection, removing all its contents.

The Data Items API only works with existing collections. To create and manage data collections, use the [Data Collections API](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/business-solutions/cms/collection-management/data-collections).

# Querying Indexed Data

Indexes accelerate filtering and sorting queries of certain types. Data queries are carried out by calling [Query Data Items](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/business-solutions/cms/data-items/query-data-items). For details of the query language used in data queries, see [API Query Language](https://dev.wix.com/api/rest/getting-started/api-query-language).

## Filtering

Indexes accelerate queries based on equality operators, such as `eq` and `in`. They also accelerate queries based on range operators, such as `gt`, `gte`, `lt`, and `lte` under certain circumstances. Indexes don't accelerate queries based on the case insensitive `startsWith` operator.

The order of fields in an index determines when and how filter queries use the index to save time.

For example, consider a collection containing information about paintings. The collection has an index for fields called `artist` (in ascending order), `dateCompleted` (in ascending order), and `title` (in ascending order), respectively.

Queries that filter based on the fields in the following orders can use the index to find the resulting entries more quickly:
- `artist` alone.
- `artist` and `dateCompleted`.
- `artist`, `dateCompleted`, and `title`.

A query that filters based on the `dateCompleted` field or the `title` field first doesn't use the index and will iterate through all items in the collection.

A query based on `artist` and `title` uses the index for looking up values in the `artist` field, but then iterates through all of the resulting items for the query of the `title` field. The index thus improves the speed of this query, but only partially.

Note that queries can use an index to accelerate a range filter (such as `gt`, `gte`, `lt`, or `lte`) only if it is the last filtering action of the query. ---

Arise Church, Pineville LA — multicultural, multiethnic, multigenerational; independent (no longer Assemblies of God; former pastor Chad Stecker is not connected — third-party directories still list both, wrongly). Led by Apostle Bryant Sanders and Pastor Vanessa Sanders (she is also called "Prophet" in some copy; unresolved which title is public).

- **Main Campus:** 501 Ates Road, Pineville, LA 71360 (Tioga is a town inside Pineville; "Impact Tioga" is the outreach brand). **Second Campus:** 5305 North Blvd, Alexandria, LA 71301, lead pastor Sheron Turner (since 2024). Sunday service at both; everything else at Main.
- **Service times:** Sunday 10:30 AM both campuses per the design brief/handoff — BUT the CMS PageContent row `site.times.sunday.second` and `arise-alexandria.js` say **10:00 AM** for Alexandria (unresolved as of 2026-09-13). Monday 7 PM = **Glory Night** (Main). Wednesday 7 PM midweek (Main). Corporate Prayer 5 AM **Mon–Thu** (Main). Service END times are unknown (needed for JSON-LD).
- **Contact:** (318) 640-1865 · arisenow.church@gmail.com (contact/serve/connect) · arisechurchprayer@gmail.com (prayer) · Wix account contact email is a third address, info.arisenow@gmail.com. Tagline `#YouBelongHere`. Mission verbs: CONNECT · GROW · SERVE · SHARE.
- **Leaders (6 CMS rows):** Bryant & Vanessa Sanders (featured); Norman & Margie Youngblood (elder; Margie on praise team); Chad & Tabitha **Kerik** (not "Ker"; elders, youth ministers, Thrive); Herbert & Erica Perry (minister); Will **Robertson** (pastor — NOT "Robinson"); Ethan Mayes (minister, worship). Kristina Robinson = Praise Team Leader (a different person, not in Leaders). Lead Network ministers: Carlos & Melissa Austin, Derrick & Pamla Calloway.
- **Ministries:** Lead Network, Children's, Youth (In Edge / X Edge), Outreach live; Thrive (young adults), Mvmt 6:14, Worship Team flagged coming-soon. Creative Arts departments: Praise & Worship, Musicians, Production, Sound, Media (Bradly), Social Media & Content.

name: arise-site-architecture
description: How arisecenla.church is built on Wix — Velo custom-element architecture, which local files are canonical, CMS collections, backend modules, page slugs, gotchas, and the local sample site
metadata:
  type: project
---

Wix classic Editor + Velo. Wix has no REST API for layout, so whole pages ship as **Velo custom elements** in `public/custom-elements/`. Pattern: CMS collection → backend web module (`content.web.js` etc.) → page code (`$w.onReady`, retry-until-ready, sets a `data-*` attribute with `JSON.stringify`) → element reads the attribute and renders. Forms in the elements POST to `/_functions/ariseForm` (`backend/http-functions.js` → `FormSubmissions` collection first, then email/automation).

- **Local project:** `D:\projects\Arise Church Website` (not a git repo). `files.zip` = everything to Aug 2026 (75 files: docs, mockups, images, CSVs, element JS); `files2.zip` = `ARISE-HANDOFF.md` (newest, Aug 23 2026), `AUDIT-REPORT.md`, and `arise-fixed-2026-08-23.zip`. Both were extracted on 2026-09-13 into `files/` and `files2/`.
- **CANONICAL element set = `files2/arise-fixed-2026-08-23/*.js` (21 files).** The same-named files in `files/` are older (13 differ). Legacy files that also define the same tags and must not be installed: `arise-pages.js`, `arise-hero.js`, `arise-events-sermons.js`, `arise-service-times.js`, `arise-service-times-v2.js` (canonical is `arise-service-times-final.js`).
- **Backend code exists only as code blocks inside the `*-SETUP.md` docs** (no `.jsw`/`.web.js` files in the zips), and the docs disagree: `events.jsw` (EVENTS-SETUP) vs `events.web.js` (handoff); two different `getPageContent` implementations (PAGECONTENT-SETUP returns `{text,image}`, ALEXANDRIA-SETUP returns string|`{text,imageUrl}`); INSTALL-ORDER still says Serve uses `arise-form.js` while SERVE-SETUP/handoff use `arise-serve.js`; FORMS-SETUP's `http-functions.js` uses `triggeredEmails.emailContact` with an email address instead of a contactId.
- **Elements → pages:** arise-header + arise-footer sitewide; arise-home `/` (+ arise-service-times placed top-right of the hero, 360×80); arise-about `/about`; arise-leaders `/leaders`; arise-ministries `/ministries`; arise-sermons `/sermons`; arise-events `/events`; arise-contact `/contact`; arise-bible `/arise-bible` (calls bible-api.com directly; 16 translations, no NIV/ESV); arise-serve `/serve`; arise-connect `/connect-groups`; arise-creatives `/creative-arts` + `/praise-worship /musicians /production /sound /media-team /content` via `data-dept`; arise-classes `/classes`; galleries arise-childrens `/childrens`, arise-youth `/youth`, arise-outreach `/outreach`, arise-leadnetwork `/lead-network` (Portfolio projects → `data-photos`); arise-alexandria `/arise-alexandria` (NOT `/alexandria`); arise-form reusable (`data-form=contact|serve|prayer`).
- **CMS collections:** Leaders(6), Ministries(8), Studies(2, video links blank), PastEvents(empty), FormSubmissions(admin-only), PageContent (contentKey → text / imageUrl / image; keys `site.times.*`, `site.campus.*`, `home.*`, `connect.season.*`, `serve/connect/creatives/classes.hero.body`, `alexandria.*`), ConnectGroups, ServePositions(7), CreativeDepartments(6), CreativeMembers(15), HomeSettings(`churchCulture`), SiteSettings(`sermonSeries`). Portfolio project IDs feed the galleries (GALLERY-SETUP.md).
- **Gotchas:** custom elements render in an iframe in Editor/Preview — only Published is real; `/_functions/` don't work in Preview; element code pasted into page code/masterPage throws "document is not defined"; check the element ID per page (Classes was `#customElement5`); custom-element text is invisible to Google — homepage still has no native H1/meta description (2026-09-13); Wix classic has no text-transform control; header `NAV` array is hardcoded; Wix serves each element file in its own module scope.
- **Local sample site (built 2026-09-13):** `sample-site/` — `node sample-site/server.js` → http://localhost:4173/_sample (hub listing every route); `.claude/launch.json` config `arise-sample`; pages generated by `build.js`, fixtures by `make-fixtures.js` (reads `files/PageContent.csv`, merges `fixtures-cms.json` if present); mock `/_functions/ariseForm` mirrors the handoff backend. Elements are copied from the canonical set.

Standing rules from `ARISE-HANDOFF.md` §1 ("these never change") and this session (2026-09-13: "IF ANYTHING IS BROKEN let me know and I'll tell you to fix it"):

1. **No design or code change without explicit permission.** Audit, report with evidence, wait for "fix it". Ask questions first.
2. **Always write "Arise Church"**, never bare "Arise" (the collage heading "This Is Arise" is the one known exception awaiting the user's call).
3. **Use the text already live on the site.** Do not invent marketing copy.
4. **One page at a time**, mockup for approval before implementing.
5. **The site must stay functional** as a church website throughout; nothing gets dropped — every page reachable from any menu keeps a home.
6. **The user reviews on an iPhone in the Facebook in-app browser in dark mode** — every mockup needs `color-scheme: light only`, explicit background on every surface, and a test at 390px with dark forced.
7. Test rendered output, not source (screenshots); never infer image-to-person mapping from DOM order on Wix; re-download files after every fix (stale copies were opened before); verify live URLs by fetching, not by trusting an API response; publish, not save, is what ships a custom element.

**Why:** the user maintains a live church site and has been burned by unrequested changes, invented copy, stale file copies, a doc slug (`/alexandria`) that was wrong versus the live site, and dark-mode rendering bugs invisible to CSS analysis.

**How to apply:** report findings with file/line evidence and wait for the go-ahead; keep the naming rule; build samples that mirror the published composition (header + page element + footer); check dark mode at 390px; prefer the newest doc (the handoff) when docs conflict, and prefer the live site over any doc.

content.content: total distinct: 65 1. [bug] arise-contact.js:292 docs-mismatch — When the documented PageContent map is applied, both Sunday rows render the word "Sunday" twice ("Sunday Sunday 10:30 AM") because the CMS seed text for the two Sunday keys already contains the day name that the markup also prints as the row label. 2. [bug] arise-contact.js:368 escaping — CMS text from data-content is written with innerHTML and the file has no escape helper, so any '<' or unclosed tag typed into a Page Content row is parsed as markup and silently drops text. 3. [bug] arise-form.js:248 a11y — Form status is never exposed to assistive tech: the success panel replaces the DOM (focus drops to , nothing is announced), the 'Sending…'/error note is not a live region, and inline 'Required' hints are not associated with their fields — WCAG 2.1 AA SC 4.1.3 Status Messages is not met. 4. [bug] arise-header.js:325 escaping — applyContent writes CMS text straight into innerHTML without the file's ahdEsc helper, so an angle bracket or ampersand typed into the PageContent 'text' column is parsed as markup instead of shown. 5. [bug] arise-leaders.js:296 escaping — Values parsed from the data-leaders JSON (photo, role, name, bio) are concatenated raw into innerHTML and into src/alt attribute values; the file has no escape helper at all, so a stray quote or angle bracket in a CMS Leaders row breaks the card markup. 6. [warning] ALL-PAGE-CODE.md:78 stale-file — ALL-PAGE-CODE.md §3 supplies Leaders page code that drives a Wix repeater (#leaderRepeater, #featName…) and never sets data-leaders; pasting it instead of CMS-SETUP.md §2 leaves the custom element on its hardcoded fallback with no error, so CMS edits silently never appear. 7. [warning] arise-about.js:318 fact-conflict — The Visit CTA states Alexandria meets at 10:00 AM, which contradicts DESIGN-BRIEF.md and ARISE-HANDOFF.md (10:30 AM at both campuses) while agreeing with PageContent.csv and arise-alexandria.js (10:00 AM); the sources disagree and no one has resolved it. 8. [warning] arise-contact.js:305 wrong-fact — The Alexandria campus Sunday fallback time (10:00 AM) conflicts with the brand/build documents, which say 10:30 AM at both campuses; the sources disagree and the owner has not settled it. 14. [warning] arise-creatives.js:103 brand-typography — Anton is set below the 18px brand floor in three places: the tile number badge (13px), the department switcher (14px), and every h3 (member names, tile names) which clamps down to 16px on any viewport under ~941px. 17. [warning] arise-youth.js:321 accessibility — Lightbox has no role="dialog"/aria-modal, no focus trap and no focus return on close (shared lightbox code, same defect as arise-childrens.js line 359). 62. [warning] arise-youth.js:351 escaping — p.videoId from data-photos is concatenated raw into the lightbox attribute (shared lightbox code, same defect as arise-childrens.js line 389). 63. [warning] CLASSES-SETUP.md:0 element-id-assumption — Section '2. Classes page code' hardcodes '#customElement1' with no retry and no 'check the ID' note, while the handoff records that the Classes element is customElement5 and CMS-SETUP says the retry loop is required because of this exact page. 64. [warning] CLASSES-SETUP.md:0 contract — The two docs disagree about which backend module exports getPrograms: CLASSES-SETUP.md puts it in gallery.web.js and imports from 'backend/gallery.web', while ARISE-HANDOFF.md §4 lists it in a separate classes.web.js; the page code import will fail with 'module not found' if the installer follows one doc for the backend and the other for the page. 65. [warning] CLASSES-SETUP.md:68 contract — Documented Classes page code targets #customElement1, but the handoff records that the Classes element is customElement5; pasting the doc as-is makes setAttribute a no-op so data-classes is never set and the element renders an empty list area (items()===null path) instead of even the 'Classes are coming' panel. 66. [warning] CMS-SETUP.md:0 velo-api-misuse — The content.web.js getters return CMS image fields raw (photo, image, flyer, groupPhoto), i.e. wix:image:// strings, which the custom elements drop straight into ; only PAGECONTENT/ALEXANDRIA convert via the (undefined) imgUrl -- so leaders/ministries/serve/connect/creatives images will be broken unless the rows happen to hold https URLs (medium confidence -- depends on how the rows were seeded). 67. [warning] files.zip:0 privacy — ArchivedFormSubmissions.csv, containing 50 real people's names, emails, phone numbers and addresses, is packaged inside the shared files.zip. 68. [warning] GALLERY-SETUP.md:0 contract — No page code anywhere sets `data-news`; the only doc mention of the Exciting News feed (GALLERY-SETUP.md 'Your projects' table) routes it through gallery page code that emits `data-photos` with a different shape, so the hero news panel stays hidden. 69. [warning] INSTALL-ORDER.md:0 install-contradiction — Step 4 row 9 installs Serve as `arise-form.js` + data-form="serve", contradicting SERVE-SETUP.md (element arise-serve.js / tag arise-serve, CMS positions, page code), and the Quick reference counts '11 elements. 3 backend files. 2 page-code files.' against a canonical set of 21 elements, content.web.js, and page code on most pages. 71. [blocker] CONNECT-SETUP.md:0 backend-conflict — Section '4. Allow the two form types' tells the installer to add `const ALLOWED = [...]` to http-functions.js, but the only full http-functions.js (FORMS-SETUP.md '1. Backend') gates on a `ROUTES` object with no connect keys, so every connect-host / connect-join submission is rejected with 400 'unknown form'. 6 2. [bug] ALEXANDRIA-SETUP.md:0 backend-conflict — Section '2. Backend' supplies a second `export const getPageContent` for content.web.js that returns a different shape (string | {text,imageUrl}) from PAGECONTENT-SETUP.md ({text,image}); pasting both is a duplicate-export SyntaxError, and if the Alexandria version wins, every element except arise-alexandria drops all string-valued keys. 7 3. [bug] arise-connect.js:38 facts — Host sign-up deadline 'September 2' is already past (today 2026-09-14) yet is shown as the urgent 'Host sign-up closes' card, in the Host tab label, and the Host tab is still open by default. 8 4. [bug] arise-connect.js:38 stale-content — Connect Groups page tells visitors on 2026-09-14 that host sign-up closes 'September 2' (12 days ago) and the same stale date is in the CMS seed, so the CMS override cannot fix it. 9 5. [bug] arise-connect.js:178 contrast — Placeholder text (e.g. '7:00 PM', 'Pineville, Alexandria, Tioga...', 'Any group works') is rgba(255,255,255,.34) on the #0A0A0C panel — 3.01:1, below AA 4.5:1 for normal text. 10 6. [bug] arise-connect.js:433 data-contract — Group flyer is written straight into but the documented backend returns the raw Wix Image field value (wix:image://v1/...), which browsers cannot load — every group card with a flyer will show a broken image. 11 7. [bug] arise-home.js:429 contract — CMS Home Settings `heading`/`kicker` fields are documented as editable but the element hardcodes both and never reads cfg.heading/cfg.kicker. 12 8. [bug] arise-leadnetwork.js:322 lifecycle — Same misplaced-call defect: fillGallery()/applyContent() sit inside the TEACHINGS.map callback after `return`, so the Camp Meetings gallery and the leadnetwork.austin.photo / leadnetwork.calloway.photo CMS images are never rendered on first build when the attributes arrive before upgrade. 13 9. [bug] arise-outreach.js:251 lifecycle — The initial fillGallery()/applyContent() calls were pasted inside the CLIPS.map callback after its return statement, so they are unreachable and connectedCallback never renders the gallery or applies CMS content on first build. 14 10. [bug] arise-sermons.js:389 lifecycle — applyLive() reassigns the featured iframe src unconditionally on every data-live-video change; the documented page code re-sets that attribute every 60 s, so the YouTube player reloads (and any playback restarts) once a minute. 15 11. [bug] CLASSES-SETUP.md:0 missing-import — Section '1. Add to backend/gallery.web.js' uses auth.elevate, webMethod and Permissions but only tells the installer to import `programs`; no doc ever creates gallery.web.js or its header, so `auth`, `webMethod` and `Permissions` are all undefined and the module fails to load. 16 12. [bug] CLASSES-SETUP.md:0 links — Documented backend builds every View Class link as /classes/{slug}, but /classes is the static custom-element page and the Online Programs app page on the live site is /class-detail, so every card button the element renders (arise-classes.js line 227-228) would point at a non-existent sub-path. 17 13. input.content:
# Arise Church — local sample site

A local render of the Velo custom elements in `files2/arise-fixed-2026-08-23/`
(the canonical set), composed the way the published Wix site composes them:
header element + one page element + footer element.

## Run it

```bash
node sample-site/server.js
```

Then open **http://localhost:4173/_sample** — the hub lists every page.

Clean URLs work exactly like the live site (`/about`, `/leaders`, `/creative-arts`,
`/praise-worship` …). `/tithes-and-offerings` and `/podcast` stop at a stand-in page
instead of redirecting off-site. Anything else that would be a Wix app page
(`/events-1/...`, `/classes/...`) shows a stand-in too.

## What feeds the elements

- `fixtures-cms.json` — real rows read from the live Wix CMS on 2026-09-13
  (Leaders, Ministries, PageContent, ServePositions, CreativeDepartments,
  CreativeMembers, HomeSettings, SiteSettings, Studies). Image URLs are exactly
  what the CMS holds, including the `c3b2d0_…` ones the CDN answers 403.
- `fixtures-data.js` — sample data for things the CMS does not have yet
  (connect groups, class rows, gallery photos, news items, past events). Every
  sample string says "Sample" so it cannot be mistaken for real content.
- `make-fixtures.js` merges both (plus `files/PageContent.csv`) into `fixtures.js`.
- `mock-page-code.js` plays the role of the Velo page code: it waits for the
  element, then sets the `data-*` attributes 350 ms later, as production does.

Main routes get **only what the live site's page code would send today**
(no `data-events` because the events backend is not installed, empty galleries
because Portfolio has no items, etc.). Routes under `/_sample/` feed the same
elements sample data so every feature can be seen.

## Forms

The elements POST to `/_functions/ariseForm`. `server.js` mocks that endpoint
with the same validation as the handoff's `http-functions.js` (ALLOWED list,
email regex, required fields). Submissions are printed to the console and
listed at `/_sample/submissions.json`. Nothing is emailed or saved.

## Rebuild after editing

```bash
node sample-site/build.js && node sample-site/make-fixtures.js
```

`assets/audit.js` is a dev helper (`window.__audit()`) used for the render
audit; it is not part of the site.

content.content: Launching skill: artifact-design

content.text:
Approach this as the design lead at a small studio known for their versatility, giving every client a visual identity pitched at the treatment the task actually calls for. Make deliberate choices about palette, typography, and layout that are specific to this subject, and avoid templated designs.

## Read the request first

Calibrate treatment, not whether to design. A doc deserves the same craft as a landing page - what changes is the treatment that craft is delivered in. Format is not part of this read: author HTML, and publish Markdown only when a loaded skill explicitly instructs it - a Markdown publish keeps its filename as its title and takes almost none of the craft below, and is never a way to save time.

Many requests call for a more utilitarian treatment: a plan, a memo, a demo. Make it polished: include real typographic hierarchy, considered spacing, and a proper palette, but avoid over-designing. Most pages do not need a flashy, gigantic hero. Keep flourishes tasteful and limited.

Some requests call for an editorial treatment: a landing page, a game, an app or tool they'll keep or share.

When unsure: a well-composed page is never the wrong answer; an over-designed visual identity sometimes is.

Fundamentals below apply to everything. The editorial process after that runs only when the read above says so.

## Fundamentals for every artifact

**Honor what's already there** Look for an existing design system first - CLAUDE.md, a tokens or theme file, existing component styles. When one exists, apply it; everything below fills gaps and never overrides. Precedence is always: the user's own words, then the project's existing system, then your choices.

**Ground it in the subject.** If the subject isn't already clear, pin it: one concrete subject, its audience, and the page's single job. The subject's own world - its materials, instruments, vernacular - is where distinctive choices come from. Whatever the treatment, carry at least one detail only this subject would have - its real units and scales, its document conventions, its terms of art - as content, not ornament; it costs a plain page nothing. Build with real content throughout, never lorem.

**Pair typefaces** Typography carries the page even when the page isn't about typography. Google Fonts is the one font host the Artifact CSP admits - link it directly (`<link rel="stylesheet" href="https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=...&display=swap">`); a face from anywhere else must be inlined as a @font-face data URI or it falls back silently. Either way, declare a real fallback stack. Keep running text near 65 characters wide; set a type scale and stay on it; give headings `text-wrap: balance`, body text room to breathe, and uppercase labels a touch of letter-spacing.

**Load libraries, don't paste them.** When the page genuinely needs a library - React, a charting or highlighting package - load its UMD build from cdnjs (only the script - a library's stylesheet still has to be inlined) with one pinned `<script src="https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/...">` placed before the inline script that uses its global, instead of inlining the library's source or hand-writing a stand-in; the Artifact tool's description lists the few other script hosts the CSP admits. The page's own CSS and JS, its images and its data ship with the page. Most pages need no library at all - reach for one only when it carries real weight.

**Choose neutrals, don't default to them.** A pure mid-grey reads as unconsidered; a grey with a slight hue bias toward the page's accent reads as chosen. Pure white and near-black are fine grounds when they suit the subject - the point is that the neutral was picked, not inherited.

**Design both themes.** The page renders in the viewer's theme, and the viewer has three states, not two: an explicit choice stamps `data-theme="dark"` / `data-theme="light"` on the root element, and the default "system" setting stamps *nothing* - most viewers see the un-stamped document, where only `prefers-color-scheme` separates light from dark. Structure the CSS token-level for all three: the bare `:root` block defines the complete light palette (for a deliberately dark-first design, swap light and dark consistently through this whole pattern); `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)` redefines only the tokens, guarded as `:root:not([data-theme="light"])` so an explicit light choice beats a dark OS; `:root[data-theme="dark"]` redefines them again so the toggle also wins in the other direction. Style components through the tokens, never directly inside a media or `[data-theme]` block - a color whose only definition sits behind `[data-theme]` never applies in the un-stamped state, and the page renders one theme's text on the other theme's ground. Two more rules keep each theme resolving as a set: the artifact composites over a ground the viewer paints in *its* theme, so `body` must set an explicit `background` from a token - a transparent body silently borrows the host's ground; and every element that sets a color takes it from the same token set as the surface behind it, never a literal that only works in one theme. Declare every token in the bare `:root` block before any media or `[data-theme]` block redefines it - a color that exists only inside one of those blocks is the classic unreadable-artifact bug. Give the second theme the same care as the first - don't naively invert; keep contrast legible and the accent working on both grounds. A design that deliberately commits to one visual world (a neon arcade screen, a letterpress invitation) may stay single-theme - then skip the media query and stamps entirely but still paint the background and every color explicitly, so the page holds on either host ground; make it a choice, not an omission.

**Let layout do the spacing.** Lay out sibling groups with flex or grid and `gap`, not per-element margins that silently collapse or double. Keep a side gutter of at least 16px at every width - set once as side padding on `body` or one outer wrapper, whose vertical padding uses `padding-block`, never a `padding` shorthand that zeroes the sides - and let rows wrap or stack to one column at phone width (~400px). Images and any `aspect-ratio` box get `max-width: 100%`, and nothing gets a `min-width` wider than the screen; only wide tables, code and diagrams may run past it - each gets `overflow-x: auto` on its own container so the page body never scrolls sideways. Reach for `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` wherever digits line up in columns.

**Compose repeated things as one object.** Cards in a row, label/value pairs down a list, badges on siblings: same edges, baselines and inner padding from one to the next, and a recurring element sits in the same place on each. Let content set a container's height and pick a column count the items fill, so nothing stretches over dead space or sits alone in a row. Text that can outgrow its track wraps or scrolls in its own container; clipped text is a bug.

**Not everything is a card.** Border, fill, radius and shadow each say "separate object" - spend them by role, lifting the one thing that needs it, instead of one radius and one shadow stamped on every block, which flattens the hierarchy. Lead with big-number tiles only when those figures are the point of the page.

**Draw charts to the scale.** One scale places marks, ticks and labels, and every label names a value the chart reaches; chart text takes its color from the theme tokens so it reads in both themes; marks, labels and edges stay clear of one another and inside the drawing's bounds - in SVG, leave room in the viewBox for the outermost labels and give every drawn shape an explicit fill.

**Show the page at rest.** Everything meant to be read is visible once the page has loaded, without scrolling to trigger it - that first still frame is what a thumbnail, a shared link, and a skimming reader all get. A section may animate in, but from a visible resting state, never parked at `opacity: 0` waiting on an observer. Size a hero to what it holds, not to the viewport; a `100vh` opener pushes the page itself out of that first frame. A tool or app opens in a realistic working state - the user's real data where it exists, otherwise example rows, a loaded sample, a form someone plausibly filled, plainly marked as examples and never passed off as the user's own figures - so the first look shows what it does; an empty shell waiting for input shows nothing.

**Avoid AI-generated design** AI-generated design currently clusters around a few looks: warm cream (#F4F1EA) with a serif display and terracotta accent; near-black with a lone acid-green or vermilion pop; broadsheet hairline rules with dense columns; a purple-to-blue gradient hero on white; Inter or Space Grotesk as the "safe" face; emoji as section markers; everything centered; `rounded-lg` everywhere; accent bar/rail on rounded cards. Where the user pins down a visual direction, follow it exactly - their words always win, including when they ask for one of these looks. Where nothing is specified, don't spend that freedom on one of these defaults.

**Build cleanly** Be cognizant of overlapping elements, cascade collisions, silent font fallbacks. Close every non-void element, double-quote attributes, give keyboard focus a visible state, respect `prefers-reduced-motion`. Give every form control a stable `id` (the platform carries form values, focus and scroll across a republish). For generative or decorative graphics, reach for Canvas or WebGL rather than hand-authoring long SVG path data.

**CSS rules** When writing the CSS, watch your selector specificities. It is easy to generate classes that cancel each other out - a type-based selector like `.section` fighting an element-based one like `.cta` over padding and margins between sections. Structure the cascade so it doesn't silently undo your spacing.

**Writing the copy** Words are design material, not decoration. Write from the user's side of the screen - name things by what people recognize, not how the system is built (a person manages *notifications*, not *webhook config*). Active voice; a control says exactly what happens ("Publish", then a toast that says "Published"). Errors explain what went wrong and how to fix it - no apologies, no vagueness. Specific beats clever.

**Name the page like a product, not a caption.** The `<title>` is the artifact's name in the gallery and the browser tab, and it sets the reader's first impression of care. Give the page a real name: a short noun phrase, typically two to four words, specific to the subject - or, for a page that exists to answer one question, that question itself, which is then the page's name. Stop at the name - a title that carries its own explainer after a dash or colon reads as generated filler. The name must also identify the page among many: in the gallery it sits beside dozens of other artifacts, and a generic category label that could sit on any of them fails as a name just as surely as an appended explainer. When a candidate title pairs the name with a generic word - a greeting, a category, a page-type label - the name is the half to keep; a trim that drops the identity and keeps the generic word produces exactly the title that could sit on any page. And the rule removes explainers, it does not impose brevity: a multi-word title that already reads as one specific name is finished, and shortening it further only makes it generic. The one-sentence publish `description` is where the explanation belongs; the gallery shows it right under the title.

**Structure is information** Structural devices, numbering, eyebrows, dividers, labels, should encode something true about the content, not decorate it. Many generic designs use numbered markers (01 / 02 / 03), but that's only appropriate if the content actually is a sequence - like a real process or a typed timeline where order carries information the reader needs. Question if choices like numbered markers actually make sense before incorporating them.

**When it's a UI, not a document** A dashboard or tool is scanned and operated, not read top-to-bottom, so the craft shifts from typography to information design. Surface the summary before the detail; encode state in form as well as number - a pill, a chip, a severity stripe - so what needs attention reads at a glance. Semantic color (good / warning / critical) is separate from the accent hue and doesn't count as your accent. Give sparklines and charts the same care as type: an area fill, a faint grid, an emphasized endpoint. What's interactive should look interactive.



## Process

Start with what the viewer should be able to do on the page, not only what they will read: if it should take input, keep what people change for whoever opens it next, show live data, or ask Claude something, load the `artifact-capabilities` skill now and design around what it makes available to this user; a page that is only read needs none of that.

Before writing code, sketch a short design plan - a compact token system with color, type, and layout:
- **Color**: describe the palette as 4-6 named hex values.
- **Type**: typefaces for 2+ roles - a characterful display face used with restraint, a complementary body face, and a utility face for captions or data if needed.
- **Layout**: a layout concept in one or two sentences.

Then build, following the plan and deriving every color and type decision from it.

**Write, look once, publish.** Before publishing you may look at the rendered page once - one screenshot of the local file, or the Artifact tool's preview where it offers one - then one pass of edits for what it shows, without a second look. For a page that charts real numbers, take that look rather than skip it, and spend it on the chart. Don't build a test loop around your own file: no repeated screenshots, no pulling the script out to run it through node, no scripts that probe the DOM. That loop spends the session re-checking what a careful write already settled, while the user waits for a link. Then publish, check once any `window.claude` call the preview couldn't run, and stop: the live page is the review surface, and further polish is the user's to ask for. If the user reports something visibly broken - a clipped column, unreadable text, a control that does nothing - fix that and republish once.

**Open viewers** You don't need to do anything for viewers who already have the page open - published changes reach them automatically at their next quiet moment, with state carried where possible. If your page holds state a viewer would miss (a game, a long form), register `window.claude?.hot?.snapshot(...)` and boot through `window.claude?.hot?.ready ? window.claude.hot.ready(start) : start(window.claude?.hot?.data ?? {})`.

## When the request is editorial

The stance shifts: the client has already rejected proposals that felt templated, and is paying for a distinctive point of view. Make opinionated calls, and take one real aesthetic risk where it serves the work.

Review the design plan against the subject before building: if any part of it reads like the generic default you would produce for any similar page, revise that part, and note what you changed and why. Only after you've confirmed the plan's uniqueness do you write the code, following the revised plan exactly.

**Principles** 

- The hero is a thesis: open with the most characteristic thing in the subject's world - headline, image, live demo, interactive moment. 
- Typography carries the personality of the page. Pair the display and body faces deliberately, not the same families you would reach for on any other project, and set a clear type scale with intentional weights, widths, and spacing. Make the type treatment itself a memorable part of the design, not a neutral delivery vehicle for the content. 
- Leverage motion deliberately. Think about where and if animation can serve the subject: a page-load sequence, hover micro-interactions, ambient atmosphere. An orchestrated moment usually lands harder than scattered effects; choose what the direction calls for. However, sometimes less is more, and extra animation contributes to the feeling that the design is AI-generated. 
- Match complexity to the vision. Maximalist directions need elaborate execution; minimal directions need precision in spacing, type, and detail. Elegance is executing the chosen vision well.
- Spend your boldness in one place; keep everything around it quiet. If the accent fights the ground, shift it toward analogous or drop saturation rather than replacing it.

# Arise Church — local sample site

A local render of the Velo custom elements in `files2/arise-fixed-2026-08-23/`
(the canonical set), composed the way the published Wix site composes them:
header element + one page element + footer element.

## Run it

```bash
node sample-site/server.js
```

Then open **http://localhost:4173/_sample** — the hub lists every page.

Clean URLs work exactly like the live site (`/about`, `/leaders`, `/creative-arts`,
`/praise-worship` …). `/tithes-and-offerings` and `/podcast` stop at a stand-in page
instead of redirecting off-site. Anything else that would be a Wix app page
(`/events-1/...`, `/classes/...`) shows a stand-in too.

## What feeds the elements

- `fixtures-cms.json` — real rows read from the live Wix CMS on 2026-09-13
  (Leaders, Ministries, PageContent, ServePositions, CreativeDepartments,
  CreativeMembers, HomeSettings, SiteSettings, Studies). Image URLs are exactly
  what the CMS holds, including the `c3b2d0_…` ones the CDN answers 403.
- `fixtures-data.js` — sample data for things the CMS does not have yet
  (connect groups, class rows, gallery photos, news items, past events). Every
  sample string says "Sample" so it cannot be mistaken for real content.
- `make-fixtures.js` merges both (plus `files/PageContent.csv`) into `fixtures.js`.
- `mock-page-code.js` plays the role of the Velo page code: it waits for the
  element, then sets the `data-*` attributes 350 ms later, as production does.

Main routes get **only what the live site's page code would send today**
(no `data-events` because the events backend is not installed, empty galleries
because Portfolio has no items, etc.). Routes under `/_sample/` feed the same
elements sample data so every feature can be seen.

## Forms

The elements POST to `/_functions/ariseForm`. `server.js` mocks that endpoint
with the same validation as the handoff's `http-functions.js` (ALLOWED list,
email regex, required fields). Submissions are printed to the console and
listed at `/_sample/submissions.json`. Nothing is emailed or saved.

## Rebuild after editing

```bash
node sample-site/build.js && node sample-site/make-fixtures.js
```

`assets/audit.js` is a dev helper (`window.__audit()`) used for the render
audit; it is not part of the site.

Escaping

  • All 18 elements with applyContent() write CMS text with innerHTML unescaped, and build a CSS selector from the CMS key. A stray < or quote typed into Page Content breaks the page. Writes are admin-only, so this is robustness, not an attack surface.

# ARISE CHURCH — CODE AUDIT & RENDER TEST REPORT
**Aug 23, 2026 · all 21 current element files · fixed set: `arise-fixed-2026-08-23.zip`**

---

## How it was tested

**Static pass** — every file: syntax (`node --check`), every validation regex extracted
and *executed* against real sample input, every internal link cross-checked against the
canonical slug map, every service time/name/phone cross-checked against the known facts,
listener-cleanup analysis, escaping analysis, and a scan for attribute-text corruption.

**Render pass** — every element loaded in real Chromium at **390px (phone), 768px
(tablet), 1366px (desktop)**, in **normal AND forced dark mode** (your Facebook in-app
browser), with interactions exercised: hamburger menu opened, About popup opened, a
Connect group's "Join" tapped, Service Times opened, the home lightbox opened.
**132 renders**, each automatically checked for JavaScript errors, horizontal overflow,
WCAG contrast on every text node, tap-target sizes, duplicate IDs, and missing alt text
— then key screenshots inspected by eye.

## Verdict

The codebase is **genuinely good**. Zero JavaScript errors in 132 renders. Zero
horizontal overflow at any width. Forced dark mode renders **identically** to light on
every page — the protection you needed for the Facebook browser holds everywhere. The
escaping discipline, focus management, and reduced-motion support are consistent.

But it was **not ship-ready**: one file was corrupted, one link 404'd, and a "TBA" was
about to go live on your homepage. All fixed. **13 files changed, 8 untouched.**

---

## FIXED — ship blockers

### 1. Corrupted headings printing raw code on the homepage  `arise-home.js`
Three `<h2` tag openers were missing — eaten, most likely by a find/replace at some
point. The browser rendered the leftovers as **literal visible text**:

> `data-ck="home.who.h2">Who We Are`

…above every one of these sections: **Who We Are**, **One Church, Two Campuses**,
**What To Expect**. The headings also lost their Anton styling and their H2 semantics.
This is almost certainly one of the mobile glitches you saw. Restored all three,
confirmed on screenshots.

### 2. Alexandria campus link — verified against the live site  `arise-home.js`
**Correction, with thanks to Bradly:** my first pass "fixed" this link to `/alexandria`
because ALEXANDRIA-SETUP.md says that's the page URL — but the live site says
otherwise: **`/arise-alexandria` is the real page (200, in the sitemap) and
`/alexandria` 404s.** The link is restored to `/arise-alexandria`, now verified
against the published site rather than the doc. The setup doc is what's wrong.

### 3. "TBA" shipping on the homepage and Contact  `arise-home.js` `arise-contact.js`
The Alexandria card hardcoded **Pre-Service Prayer: TBA** and **Midweek Service: TBA**
on two pages — while the Alexandria page itself was built on the principle *"no TBA
sitting there for months."* Both rows are now **hidden by default** and appear
automatically the moment you put a time into CMS → Page Content
(`site.times.second.prayer` / `site.times.second.midweek`). Verified both ways in a
live render — including a CSS override that was needed because `display:flex` was
beating the `hidden` attribute (caught on the screenshot, not by the scanner).

---

## FIXED — bugs and robustness

### 4. Brand red failing contrast in Service Times  `arise-service-times-final.js`
"Sunday Service" and "Monday Nights" used **#D6222D on near-black — 3.89:1**, below
the 4.5:1 minimum. This is the *exact* failure your brand system created `#DB3F48`
for. Switched both rules; re-tested at 4.5+. The dashes and buttons keep brand red,
as designed.

### 5. Carousel dots were 9×9px  `arise-home.js`
Practically untappable on a phone. Now a **26×26px hit area** with the same 9px
visual dot — the design is pixel-identical, the target is nearly 9× larger.

### 6. Menu/lightbox die if Wix re-attaches an element  `arise-home.js` `arise-header.js`
Both elements append a panel to `document.body` and remove it on disconnect — but if
Wix detaches and re-attaches the element, the old guard skipped rebuilding, leaving a
hamburger that opens nothing and gallery tiles that open nothing. Both now restore
their body-mounted panels and key handlers on re-attach.

### 7. Unescaped lightbox markup  `arise-home.js`
Thumbnails escaped captions/URLs; the full-size lightbox didn't. An alt like
`Youth "Edge" Night` would have broken the markup. Escaped, matching the rest.

### 8. Listener hygiene  `arise-home.js`
The lightbox's document-level keyboard handler now detaches with the element, and the
carousel's hover pause/resume no longer stacks a new pair of listeners on every data
refresh.

### 9. Insecure social links  `arise-footer.js` `arise-contact.js`
Instagram and X linked as `http://`. Now `https://`.

### 10. Maps links behaved inconsistently  `arise-home.js`
Home opened Google Maps **in the same tab** (navigating people off your site); the
footer opened a new tab. Standardized: all three home maps links now
`target="_blank" rel="noopener"`, matching the footer.

### 11. Required select said "No preference," then errored "Required"  `arise-connect.js`
The host form's required venue dropdown offered *No preference* as its default, then
rejected it. Required selects now read **"Choose…"**; optional ones keep
*No preference* (correct there).

### 12. Mobile autofill  `arise-connect.js` `arise-serve.js` `arise-form.js`
Inputs had `autocomplete="on"` and no `name` — phones couldn't offer name/email/phone
autofill. All form controls now carry `name` plus real tokens (`given-name`,
`family-name`, `email`, `tel`). On a phone this turns the Connect signup into
three taps. (Contact already had proper tokens — untouched.)

### 13. Small tap targets  `arise-home.js` `arise-contact.js` `arise-footer.js` `arise-header.js`
"Get Directions" links were 19px tall; footer links ~28px; the menu's phone number
20px. Padding added (visually invisible): everything now ≥26px, clearing the WCAG
2.1 AA minimum of 24px; footer social icons are 44px on mobile.

### 14. Dead code out  `arise-home.js` `arise-connect.js` `arise-footer.js`
Home's leftover footer CSS (the footer markup was already removed — the footer file's
install note claiming otherwise was stale and is now corrected), and Connect's join
pre-fill writing to a `#connect-join-position` field that doesn't exist.

### 15. The four gallery pages carried home's lightbox bugs, byte-for-byte
`arise-childrens.js` `arise-youth.js` `arise-outreach.js` `arise-leadnetwork.js`
Their lightbox code is an exact copy of home's original — so all three defects came
along: unescaped media markup, a document keyboard handler that never detaches, and a
gallery that goes dead if Wix re-attaches the element. The same fix set (7 edits each)
was applied to all four, then torture-tested on Youth: a hostile alt text
(`Youth "Edge" <Night>`) round-trips intact, and after a forced detach/re-attach the
lightbox still opens and arrow-key navigation still works. Zero errors.

### 16. About's Escape handler leaked  `arise-about.js`
The popups' Escape-to-close listener sat on `document` with no cleanup at all — it
survived the element's removal and would stack another copy on every re-attach. Now

Both attachments are byte-identical to the copies I audited, so there's one fix set. One correction to my report: the Aug 23 pass changed **14** files, not 13 (the earlier report's own table lists 14; its headline miscounted, and I repeated it).

Here is what actually needs code work, in priority order.

**1. No new code — install the 14 files that are already fixed**
Everything visitors can see broken today is fixed in `arise-fixed-2026-08-23.zip`; it just never reached Wix. Pasting these and publishing clears the raw `data-ck` text on Home, the dead Previous Events button, the `http://` socials, the "No preference" required selects, the missing autofill names, and the TBA rows: `arise-home`, `arise-events`, `arise-footer`, `arise-contact`, `arise-connect`, `arise-serve`, `arise-form`, `arise-header`, `arise-about`, `arise-service-times-final`, `arise-childrens`, `arise-youth`, `arise-outreach`, `arise-leadnetwork`.

**2. Real defects in those files that I'd patch before you paste (all small)**
- `arise-outreach.js:251` and `arise-leadnetwork.js:322`: the `fillGallery()`/`applyContent()` calls were pasted inside a `.map()` callback after its `return`, so they never run. Move them below the render, as in the Children's and Youth files.
- `arise-service-times-final.js`: on a Wix re-mount the panel is removed and never rebuilt, so the button opens nothing. Same fix the header got in August.
- `arise-events.js`: "Sold Out" is a live link with `pointer-events:none` (keyboard users can still activate it); the built-in fallback event has no expiry, so it will advertise The Outpour as upcoming after 1 Nov.
- `arise-contact.js`: Directions and social links still open in the same tab (the August fix only covered Home); the file header still tells the installer to keep the native Wix form.
- `arise-connect.js`: the September 2 deadline and season dates are hardcoded, and the tab label has no CMS hook. Needs your new dates.
- `arise-home.js`: ignores the CMS `heading`/`kicker` for the culture video; the news rotation timer is not cleared when the list empties and not restored after a re-mount.
- `arise-form.js`: a failed prayer request tells people to email the general inbox instead of the prayer address.

Recorded and republished (report version 2, same link). Here is where that leaves things.

**What Pastor Sheron's facts settle**
- Alexandria Sunday is **10:00 AM**. The CMS and every element were right; the design brief, build plan, handoff §9 and the Service Times dropdown text ("10:30 AM · Both campuses") are wrong.
- Wednesday **6:00 PM Prayer** and **6:45 PM Bible Study** are already in the CMS rows and already showing on the live Contact page. The only mismatch is the label: the code calls the 6:45 row "Midweek Service" and the 6:00 row "Pre-Service Prayer".
- Her bio is her own text, word for word what is in the CMS. It stands as written.

**Your point about the CMS is right, and the code only half honors it.** The times are CMS-driven. The words around them are not:
- The row labels are typed into three files, so "Midweek Service" cannot become "Bible Study" from the CMS.
- The Service Times dropdown has no CMS hook at all. Its "10:30 AM · Both campuses" line is wrong for Alexandria and can only be changed in the file.
- The header menu and the footer never receive CMS data, because the site-wide code file is empty and the menu panel lives outside the element.
- Seven pages carry a hardcoded "Sunday 10:30 AM in Pineville, 10:00 AM in Alexandria" sentence with no hook.
- The Connect Groups tab label and the culture-video heading are hardcoded too.

The report now has a table of exactly what is CMS-linked and what is not, with file and line for each.

**The code change that closes the gap** is one consistent pattern rather than many patches: add label rows to Page Content (for example a label key beside each time key) with matching hooks in the markup, give the Service Times element a `data-content` attribute like the others, add a few lines of site-wide code so the header and footer receive the same Page Content map, and put hooks on the seven sentences and the footer strip. After that, renaming "Midweek Service" to "Bible Study" or changing any time is a CMS edit with no publish.

If you want that, say so and I'll build it into the new fixed set alongside the other code fixes. The CMS edits you can make today regardless: the two Sunday rows to plain "10:30 AM" and "10:00 AM", and the five image URLs.

# Arise Church — CMS reference
**Read from the live Wix site (ID `5fff0585-70f7-4075-9289-b6e4e3d38059`) on 14 Sept 2026, read-only.**
This is how the site is edited. Every collection, every field, what reads it, and how to change things.

---

## How the CMS drives the site

```
CMS collection  →  backend function (backend/content.web.js etc.)  →  page code ($w.onReady)  →  custom element
                                                                       sets a data-* attribute     reads it and renders
```

A custom element cannot read the CMS itself. The page's Velo code fetches the rows, `JSON.stringify`s them, and sets
them as a `data-*` attribute on the element (`data-leaders`, `data-ministries`, `data-content` …). If a page has no
page code, its element shows the copy that is built into the file. **That is why some pages ignore the CMS today**
(six Creative Arts department pages, Serve, Children's, Youth, Outreach, Lead Network, Sermons — see the audit).

Forms go the other way: the element POSTs to `/_functions/ariseForm`, the backend writes a row into **Form Submissions**.

Permissions on every content collection: **read = Anyone, insert/update/remove = Admin**. The two collections holding
people's details (Form Submissions, ArchivedFormSubmissions) are **Admin-only for everything, including read**. Correct.

---

## The 12 custom collections

### Leaders — `Leaders` · 7 rows · read by `/leaders` via `getLeaders()` → `data-leaders`
| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| name | Text | display field |
| role | Text | e.g. "Apostle · Pastor & Prophet" |
| shortBio | Text | **this is what the page shows** (backend prefers shortBio over bio) |
| bio | Text | long version, kept for reference |
| photo | Image | 3:4 portrait |
| featured | Boolean | ticked = the wide card at the top (only the first featured row is shown) |
| sortOrder | Number | 1 = first |

Rows (sortOrder): 1 Bryant & Vanessa Sanders (featured) · 2 Norman and Margie Youngblood · 3 Chad and Tabitha Kerik · 4 Herbert and Erica Perry · 5 Will Robertson · 6 Ethan Mayes · 16 Kristina Robinson (Creative Arts Director · Minister, added 23 Aug).
Six photos are stored as https URLs (seeded by API); Kristina's is a Wix image upload. Both work live.

### Ministries — `Ministries` · 9 rows · read by `/ministries` via `getMinistries()` → `data-ministries`
| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| title | Text | display field |
| category | Text | small line under the title, e.g. "Birth – 5th Grade" |
| image | Image | 4:5 tile |
| pageLink | Text | `/childrens` etc. Empty when coming soon |
| comingSoon | Boolean | ticked = "Coming Soon" badge, no link |
| sortOrder | Number | |

Rows: 1 Lead Network (/lead-network) · 2 Children's Ministry (/childrens) · 3 Youth Ministry (/youth) · 4 Outreach (/outreach) · **5 Connect Groups (/connect-groups) and 5 Thrive For Young Adults (coming soon) share sortOrder 5** · 6 Mvmt 6:14 (coming soon) · 7 Arise Creative Arts (/creative-arts) · 8 In Edge/ X Edge (coming soon).
The Home page's ministries strip is hardcoded to the first four; it does not read this collection.

### Page Content — `PageContent` · 45 rows · read by most pages via `getPageContent()` → `data-content`
The copy-and-times collection. Each row is one editable thing.

| Field | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| contentKey | Text | the key the code looks for (`data-ck="…"` for text, `data-ci="…"` for images) |
| page | Text | which page it belongs to (filter on this in the CMS) |
| label | Text | human description |
| text | Text | the copy shown. **Plain text only** — a stray `<` breaks the page today |
| imageUrl | Text | the image URL in use today |
| image | Image | optional upload; if set it wins over imageUrl |
| where | Text | where on the page it appears |

**All 45 keys, by page** (✓ = an element reads it today; ✗ = nothing reads it yet)

| Key | ✓ | Current value / note |
|---|---|---|
| site.times.sunday.main | ✓ | "Sunday 10:30 AM" → should be `10:30 AM` (the word Sunday is doubled on Contact/Home) |
| site.times.sunday.second | ✓ | "Sunday 10:00 AM" → should be `10:00 AM` (confirmed 10:00 by Pastor Sheron) |
| site.times.main.glorynight | ✓ | Monday 7:00 PM |

| site.times.main.prayer | ✓ | Mon-Thu 5:00 AM |

| site.times.second.midweek | ✓ | Wednesday 6:45 PM (label in code: "Midweek Service" — Pastor Sheron calls it Bible Study) |
| site.campus.main | ✓ | 501 Ates Road, Pineville, LA 71360 |

| site.email | ✓ footer only | arisenow.church@gmail.com (footer never receives the map today) |
| site.tagline | header only | #YouBelongHere (header never receives the map today) |

| home.hero.body | ✓ | Welcome to our multicultural… |

Not in the CMS but read by the code: nothing — every key the elements look for exists. Not read by any code: `site.times.second.other` is in the old CSV only, not in the live CMS.

### Serve Positions — `ServePositions` · 7 rows · meant for `/serve` via `getServePositions()` → `data-positions` (page code not installed; page shows 5 built-in roles)
Fields: title (Text) · description (Text) · team (Text) · image (Image, unused by the element) · urgent (Boolean = "Most Needed" badge) · active (Boolean) · sortOrder (Number).
Rows: 1 Children's Department (urgent) · 2 Outreach (urgent) · 3 Media / Social Media · 4 Edge / X Edge · 5 Maintenance · 6 Praise & Worship · 7 Production & Sound.

### Connect Groups — `ConnectGroups` · 0 rows · read by `/connect-groups` via `getConnectGroups()` → `data-groups`
Fields: title · hostName · day · time · location · dates · description (Text) · flyer (Image) · audience (Text) · isFull (Boolean = "Full" badge, button disabled) · active (Boolean, untick to hide) · sortOrder (Number).
Empty, so the page shows "Groups are forming". Add a row and it appears.

### Creative Departments — `CreativeDepartments` · 6 rows · read by `/creative-arts` and the six department pages via `getCreatives()` → `data-depts`
Fields: name · slug · tagline · description (Text) · groupPhoto (Image) · pageLink (Text) · active (Boolean) · sortOrder (Number).
Rows: 1 Praise & Worship (/praise-worship) · 2 Musicians (/musicians) · 3 Production (/production) · 4 Sound (/sound) · 5 Media (/media-team) · 6 Social Media & Content (/content). All have taglines; description and groupPhoto are empty.
**The `slug` must equal the `data-dept` attribute set on that page's element, and the `name` must equal each member's `department` text exactly** (case and spacing) or the member is not shown.

### Creative Members — `CreativeMembers` · 14 rows · same backend → `data-members`
Fields: name · department (Text — must match a department `name`) · role · bio (Text) · photo (Image) · isLeader (Boolean, not used by the element yet) · active (Boolean) · sortOrder (Number).
Praise & Worship: Kristina Robinson (Praise Team Leader, isLeader), Ethan Mayes, Linda Lemon, Yolanda Foreman, Brandis Mayes, Cailey Norman, Margie Youngblood · Musicians: Nick Robinson, Geremiah Branch · Production: Darek Foreman, Ronnie Odom, Brandon Sizemore · Sound: Ty Sanders · Media: Bradly Dyer. No photos or bios yet (monogram cards show). CREATIVES-SETUP.md listed Thelma as a fifteenth member; she is not in the collection.

### Home Settings — `HomeSettings` · 1 row (`churchCulture`) · read by `/` via `getHomeSettings()` → `data-culture`
Fields: settingKey · cultureVideo (Video — **uploaded: Arise_This_Is_Our_Culture.mp4**) · posterImage (Image, set) · heading ("This Is Arise") · kicker ("Church Culture") · active (Boolean, **ticked**).
The video is live on the homepage. heading/kicker are in the CMS but the element still prints its built-in text (audit item).

### Site Settings — `SiteSettings` · 1 row (`sermonSeries`) · meant for `/sermons` page code → `data-series-*` (page code not installed)
Fields: settingKey · seriesActive (ticked) · seriesTitle ("The Kingdom") · seriesLine ("Culture of Giving") · seriesLink (YouTube /streams) · seriesButton ("Watch the Full Message").
The live page shows the same words only because they are also the file's built-in fallback.

### Studies — `Studies` · 2 rows · read by nothing yet (Training page never rebuilt; Lead Network lists the same two studies from its own file)
Fields: title · description · speaker (Text) · image (Image) · videoUrl (Text, **both blank**) · sortOrder.
Rows: Guarding the Anointing: Unmasking the Spirit of Delilah (Apostle Bryant Sanders) · Leading with Purpose (Pastors Derrick and Pam Calloway).

### Form Submissions — `FormSubmissions` · 1 row · written by `/_functions/ariseForm` · Admin-only
Fields: formType (contact/serve/prayer/connect-host/connect-join) · name · email · phone · subject · message · position · handled (Boolean).
One contact submission, **unhandled**. Tick `handled` when answered.

### ArchivedFormSubmissions — collection ID `Import1` · 50 rows · Admin-only · read by nothing
The 2019–2025 submissions rescued from the old Wix Forms. Fields: title · source · submitted (Date) · firstName · lastName · email · phone (**Number** — formatting and leading zeros lost) · address · firstTime · sessions · inquiries · originalId.

### What the docs describe that does not exist
- `PastEvents` — never created (the Events page reads Wix Events instead).
- `Import2` — deleted, as PAGECONTENT-SETUP says.
- A "Church Culture" Portfolio project — gone; the video lives in Home Settings now.

---

## Wix app collections that matter

| Collection | Rows | What it is | Used by |
|---|---|---|---|
| Portfolio/Projects | 5 | Children's Ministry `621e6fdb…` · Youth Ministry `c2be296e…` · Outreach `78e5e5f9…` · Lead Network `885f9ceb…` · Exciting News `b2697282…`. All five still wear the same Wix placeholder cover | the gallery page code (GALLERY-SETUP.md) — **not installed on any page yet** |
| Portfolio/ProjectItems | 1 | one video, "Arise Hub", attached to no project | galleries → empty until photos are added to the projects |
| Portfolio/Collections | 1 | "Church Collection" (/photos) | — |
| Events/Events | 20 | 1 scheduled (The Outpour, 30 Oct–1 Nov 2026), 14 ended, 5 canceled (four of them duplicates of "Apostle Joan Hunter Power To Heal") | `/events` page code (installed, working) |
| Events/Categories | 8 | | |
| Bookings/Services | 3 | two classes and one course (Pathway to Discipleship in-person / online, and the 2022 conference per the Aug 17 audit) | /book-online app pages |
| Stores/Products | 2 | #ImpactTioga T-Shirt $25 · Arise Church Yard Sign $10 (store publicly reachable) | store app pages |
| Locations/Locations | 2 | **"Ates Road" and "Ates Rd" — two copies of the Pineville campus, no Alexandria** | Wix business info / Bookings |
| Members/PublicData | 82 | site member accounts | Members Area |
| Forms/contact032, Forms/stripsContact042 | 8 + 8 | legacy Wix Forms submissions (the other five Forms/* are empty) | nothing — candidates for archive and delete |
| WixForms/* (3) | see note | newer Wix Forms app collections | nothing |
| @hanas535/events-calendar/events | 16 | **a third-party Events Calendar app still holding its demo rows** (Yoga by the River, Farmers Market, Pasta-Making Workshop…) | nothing on the rebuilt pages; likely the old /schedule page |
| Marketing/Coupons | 0 | | |

---

## How to change things (today)

| Change a service time | Page Content → the `site.times.*` row → `text`. Home, Contact and the Alexandria page pick it up on next load, no publish. (Header menu, footer strip and the Service Times dropdown do **not** — they are hardcoded; audit item.) |

# Arise Church — CMS reference
**Read from the live Wix site (ID `5fff0585-70f7-4075-9289-b6e4e3d38059`) on 14 Sept 2026, read-only.**
This is how the site is edited. Every collection, every field, what reads it, and how to change things.

---

## How the CMS drives the site

```
CMS collection  →  backend function (backend/content.web.js etc.)  →  page code ($w.onReady)  →  custom element
                                                                       sets a data-* attribute     reads it and renders
```

A custom element cannot read the CMS itself. The page's Velo code fetches the rows, `JSON.stringify`s them, and sets
them as a `data-*` attribute on the element (`data-leaders`, `data-ministries`, `data-content` …). If a page has no
page code, its element shows the copy that is built into the file. **That is why some pages ignore the CMS today**
(six Creative Arts department pages, Serve, Children's, Youth, Outreach, Lead Network, Sermons — see the audit).

Forms go the other way: the element POSTs to `/_functions/ariseForm`, the backend writes a row into **Form Submissions**.

Permissions on every content collection: **read = Anyone, insert/update/remove = Admin**. The two collections holding
people's details (Form Submissions, ArchivedFormSubmissions) are **Admin-only for everything, including read**. Correct.

## How to change things (today)

| I want to… | Do this |
|---|---|
| Change a service time | Page Content → the `site.times.*` row → `text`. Home, Contact and the Alexandria page pick it up on next load, no publish. (Header menu, footer strip and the Service Times dropdown do **not** — they are hardcoded; audit item.) |
| Rename "Midweek Service" to "Bible Study" | Not possible from the CMS yet — the label is in the code. Audit proposes label rows. |
| Fix the doubled "Sunday" | Page Content → `site.times.sunday.main` = `10:30 AM`, `site.times.sunday.second` = `10:00 AM` |
| Add or reorder a leader | Leaders → new row (name, role, shortBio, photo, sortOrder) |
| Launch a ministry page | Ministries → untick comingSoon, set pageLink |
| Add a Connect Group | Connect Groups → new row (active ticked). Mark full with isFull |
| Add a serve role | Serve Positions → new row (needs the Serve page code installed to show) |
| Add a Creative Arts member | Creative Members → new row; `department` must match the department `name` exactly |
| Put photos on a ministry page | Portfolio → the project (Children's Ministry, Youth Ministry, Outreach, Lead Network) → add items. Title becomes alt text, description the caption. Needs the gallery page code installed. |
| Put news in the homepage hero | Portfolio → Exciting News → add an item (needs Home page code that sets `data-news`; none is documented yet) |
| Change the culture video | Home Settings → cultureVideo. Untick active to show the photo collage instead |
| Set the sermon series band | Site Settings → sermonSeries (needs the Sermons page code installed to take effect) |
| Answer a form message | Form Submissions → tick handled |
| Change the Connect season | Page Content → the four `connect.season.*` rows (the tab label is hardcoded; audit item) |
