tools.description:
Mark the start of a new chapter in this session.

Call this when the work shifts to a meaningfully different phase — e.g. after finishing exploration and starting implementation, after a fix lands and you move to verification, or when the user pivots to an unrelated request. The user sees a divider in the transcript and a floating table of contents for jumping between chapters.

Use sparingly: a chapter should cover a coherent stretch of work, not every tool call. A typical session has 3–8 chapters. Do not mark a chapter for the very first message — the session start is implicit.

The title is a short noun phrase ("Codebase exploration", "Auth bug fix", "Test verification"), not a sentence.

Flag an out-of-scope issue for a separate background task.

Call this when you notice something worth fixing that would bloat the current change — dead code, stale docs, missing coverage, a confirmed TODO, or a security issue spotted in passing. Don't flag vague code-smell observations, trivial fixes you can do inline, or low-confidence hunches. A chip appears for the user; one click spins it off into its own session. tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

entries.description:
Execute JavaScript code against the Wix REST API when code is useful for chaining related calls, pagination, loops, branching, or in-memory transformation.

CODE CONTRACT:
- Pass an async function expression: `async function() { ... }` or `async () => { ... }`. Put every declaration, `await`, and `return` inside it, and do not invoke it yourself.
- Use only `wix.request({ method, url, body })` and in-memory JavaScript. Node.js modules, filesystem access, and downloadable-file creation are unavailable.
- Do not minify the code. Put each object property on its own line, with spaces after colons and commas, and declare deep literals (request bodies, filters, patch lists) as a named `const` before use so each `wix.request({ ... })` argument stays short.

CONFIRM API CONTRACTS:
- Do not rely on memory for endpoints, methods, bodies, response paths, filters, enum values, or auth scope. Confirm every method from conversation-provided details, a complete matching docs example, or the schema/docs tools before executing.
- Prefer `method.publicUrl` from SearchWixAPISpec; never use `method.servers[0]`. Pass all supporting documentation URLs through `sourceDocUrls`.
- A response field is not automatically filterable or sortable. Use only capabilities declared for that exact query/search method. If an unsupported filter is unavoidable, fetch a bounded result set and filter it in code.
- Read-only probes may inspect state or resolve IDs. Never use speculative create/update/delete calls to discover request or response shapes, and never repeat a successful mutation merely to obtain more response data.

For query and search endpoints: each endpoint declares which fields it can filter and sort by, and with which operators. That list is closed for fields and their operators and covers that endpoint only, and a field's presence in the response is no evidence it can be filtered on. It lives in the method's declared capabilities, and some resources also publish it as a "Supported Filters and Sorting" page. Logical operators are WQL sy… [truncated]

code.description: JavaScript async function expression to execute against the Wix REST API. The value must be the function itself, for example `async function() { ... }` or `async () => { ... }`, not a script body and not an invoked function. Return the final answer from inside the function. Do not write top-level `const`, top-level `await`, or top-level `return` outside the function body. Do not import Node.js built-ins such as `fs`, `path`, or `node:*`, and do not try to write files from this code; ExecuteWixAPI only returns data from the function. Use `wix.request({ method, url, body })` for Wix API calls. Scope defaults to `site` when a `siteId` is available — either the ExecuteWixAPI `siteId` parameter or a per-request `siteId` on the `wix.request` call — and to `account` when neither is set; set `scope` explicitly when needed. Full Wix API URLs and paths starting with `/` are supported. For MULTIPLE sites, handle them all in this ONE call: map over the site IDs and fan out with `Promise.allSettled`, passing a per-request `siteId` to each `wix.request({ scope: "site", siteId, method, url, body })`; the runtime obtains each site's token automatically. Do NOT invoke ExecuteWixAPI once per site. When `siteId` is omitted, the tool-level `siteId` is used. Wix REST API page size limits vary — use 100 as a safe default unless the method schema (via SearchWixAPISpec) confirms a higher limit is supported. For cursor-based APIs, pass the next cursor as `cursorPaging: { limit: 100, cursor: pagingMetadata.cursors.next }` — not inside `paging`. content.text:
# Workflow authoring reference

A workflow structures work across many agents — to be comprehensive (decompose and cover in parallel), to be confident (independent perspectives and adversarial checks before committing), or to take on scale one context can't hold (migrations, audits, broad sweeps). The script is where you encode that structure: what fans out, what verifies, what synthesizes.

When you do call it, the right move is often **hybrid**: scout inline first (list the files, find the channels, scope the diff) to discover the work-list, then call Workflow to pipeline over it. You don't need to know the shape before the *task* — only before the *orchestration step*.

Common single-phase workflows you can chain across turns:
- **Understand** — parallel readers over relevant subsystems → structured map
- **Design** — judge panel of N independent approaches → scored synthesis
- **Review** — dimensions → find → adversarially verify (the review-changes example)
- **Research** — multi-modal sweep → deep-read → synthesize
- **Migrate** — discover sites → transform each (worktree isolation) → verify

For larger work, run several in sequence — read each result before deciding the next phase. You stay in the loop; each workflow is one well-scoped fan-out.

**Ultracode.** When a system-reminder confirms ultracode is on, that opt-in is standing: author and run a workflow for every substantive task by default. The goal is the most exhaustive, correct answer you can produce — token cost is not a constraint. For multi-phase work (understand → design → implement → review), that often means several workflows in sequence — one per phase — so you stay in the loop between them. The quality patterns below (adversarial verify, multi-modal sweep, completeness critic, loop-until-dry) are the tools; pick what fits the task. Lean toward orchestrating with workflows and adversarially verifying your findings — unless the work is trivial or already verified. Solo only on conversational turns or trivial mechanical edits. When a reminder says ultracode is off, revert to the opt-in rule in the Workflow tool description.

Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first. Every invocation automatically persists its script to a file under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate on a workflow, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with `{scriptPath: "<path>"}` instead of resending the full script.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'find-flaky-tests',
    description: 'Find flaky tests and propose fixes',   // one-line, shown in permission dialog
    phases: [                                            // one entry per phase() call
      { title: 'Scan', detail: 'grep test logs for retries' },
      { title: 'Fix', detail: 'one agent per flaky test' },
    ],
  }
  // script body starts here — use agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase()/log()
  phase('Scan')
  const flaky = await agent('grep CI logs for retry markers', {schema: FLAKY_SCHEMA})
  ...

The `meta` object must be a PURE LITERAL — no variables, function calls, spreads, or template interpolation. Required fields: `name`, `description`. Optional: `whenToUse` (shown in the workflow list), `phases`. Use the SAME phase titles in meta.phases as in phase() calls — titles are matched exactly; a phase() call with no matching meta entry just gets its own progress group. Add `model` to a phase entry when that phase uses a specific model override.

Script body hooks:
- agent(prompt: string, opts?: {label?: string, phase?: string, schema?: object, model?: string, effort?: string, isolation?: 'worktree', agentType?: string}): Promise<any> — spawn a subagent. Without schema, returns its final text as a string. With schema (a JSON Schema), the subagent is forced to call a StructuredOutput tool and agent() returns the validated object — no parsing needed. Returns null if the user skips the agent mid-run or the subagent dies on a terminal API error after retries (filter with .filter(Boolean)). opts.label overrides the display label. opts.phase explicitly assigns this agent to a progress group (use this inside pipeline()/parallel() stages to avoid races on the global phase() state — same phase string → same group box). opts.model overrides the model for this agent call. Default to omitting it — the agent inherits the main-loop model (the resolved session model), which is almost always correct. Only set it when you're highly confident a different tier fits the task; when unsure, omit. opts.effort overrides the reasoning effort for this agent call ('low' | 'medium' | 'high' | 'xhigh' | 'max') — omit to inherit the session effort; use 'low' for cheap mechanical stages and higher tiers only for the hardest verify/judge stages. opts.isolation: 'worktree' runs the agent in a fresh git worktree — EXPENSIVE (~200-500ms setup + disk per agent), use ONLY when agents mutate files in parallel and would otherwise conflict; the worktree is auto-removed if unchanged. opts.agentType uses a custom subagent type (e.g. 'general-purpose', 'code-reviewer') instead of the default workflow subagent — resolved from the same registry as the Agent tool; composes with schema (the custom agent's system prompt gets a StructuredOutput instruction appended).
- pipeline(items, stage1, stage2, ...): Promise<any[]> — run each item through all stages independently, NO barrier between stages. Item A can be in stage 3 while item B is still in stage 1. This is the DEFAULT for multi-stage work. Wall-clock = slowest single-item chain, not sum-of-slowest-per-stage. Every stage callback receives (prevResult, originalItem, index) — use originalItem/index in later stages to label work without threading context through stage 1's return value. A stage that throws drops that item to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- parallel(thunks: Array<() => Promise<any>>): Promise<any[]> — run tasks concurrently. This is a BARRIER: awaits all thunks before returning. A thunk that throws (or whose agent errors) resolves to `null` in the result array — the call itself never rejects, so `.filter(Boolean)` before using the results. Use ONLY when you genuinely need all results together.
- log(message: string): void — emit a progress message to the user (shown as a narrator line above the progress tree)
- phase(title: string): void — start a new phase; subsequent agent() calls are grouped under this title in the progress display
- args: any — the value passed as Workflow's `args` input, verbatim (undefined if not provided). Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values in the tool call, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — `args: ["a.ts", "b.ts"]`, not `args: "[\"a.ts\", ...]"` (a stringified list reaches the script as one string, so `args.filter`/`args.map` throw). Use this to parameterize named workflows — e.g. pass a research question, target path, or config object directly instead of via a side-channel file.
- budget: {total: number|null, spent(): number, remaining(): number} — the turn's token target from the user's "+500k"-style directive. `budget.total` is null if no target was set. `budget.spent()` returns output tokens spent this turn across the main loop and all workflows — the pool is shared, not per-workflow. `budget.remaining()` returns `max(0, total - spent())`, or `Infinity` if no target. The target is a HARD ceiling, not advisory: once `spent()` reaches `total`, further `agent()` calls throw. Use for dynamic loops: `while (budget.total && budget.remaining() > 50_000) { ... }`, or static scaling: `const FLEET = budget.total ? Math.floor(budget.total / 100_000) : 5`.
- workflow(nameOrRef: string | {scriptPath: string}, args?: any): Promise<any> — run another workflow inline as a sub-step and return whatever it returns. Pass a name to invoke a saved workflow (same registry as {name: "..."}), or {scriptPath} to run a script file you Wrote earlier. The child shares this run's concurrency cap, agent counter, abort signal, and token budget — its agents appear under a "▸ name" group in /workflows and its tokens count toward budget.spent(). The args param becomes the child's `args` global. Nesting is one level only: workflow() inside a child throws. Throws on unknown name / unreadable scriptPath / child syntax error; catch to handle gracefully.

Subagents are told their final text IS the return value (not a human-facing message), so they return raw data. For structured output, use the schema option — validation happens at the tool-call layer so the model retries on mismatch.
Schemas need {type: 'object', properties: {...}} at root and required ⊆ properties; unsatisfiable ones throw at agent().

Workflow agents can reach all session-connected MCP tools via ToolSearch — schemas load on demand per agent. Caveat: interactively-authenticated MCP servers (e.g. claude.ai) may be absent in headless/cron runs.

Subagents get the same CLAUDE.md files injected at start that you did (except built-in agent types that omit them, such as Explore and Plan) — don't tell them to re-read those or paste their rules into the prompt; name the specific rule a stage needs, if any.

Scripts are plain JavaScript, NOT TypeScript — type annotations (`: string[]`), interfaces, and generics fail to parse. The script body runs in an async context — use await directly. Standard JS built-ins (JSON, Math, Array, etc.) are available — EXCEPT `Date.now()`/`Math.random()`/argless `new Date()`, which throw (they would break resume); pass timestamps in via `args`, stamp results after the workflow returns, and for randomness vary the agent prompt/label by index. No filesystem or Node.js API access.

DEFAULT TO pipeline(). Only reach for a barrier (parallel between stages) when you genuinely need ALL prior-stage results together.

A barrier is correct ONLY when stage N needs cross-item context from all of stage N-1:
- Dedup/merge across the full result set before expensive downstream work
- Early-exit if the total count is zero ("0 bugs found → skip verification entirely")
- Stage N's prompt references "the other findings" for comparison

A barrier is NOT justified by:
- "I need to flatten/map/filter first" — do it inside a pipeline stage: pipeline(items, stageA, r => transform([r]).flat(), stageB)
- "The stages are conceptually separate" — that's what pipeline() models. Separate stages ≠ synchronized stages.
- "It's cleaner code" — barrier latency is real. If 5 finders run and the slowest takes 3× the fastest, a barrier wastes 2/3 of the fast finders' idle time.

Smell test: if you wrote
  const a = await parallel(...)
  const b = transform(a)        // flatten, map, filter — no cross-item dependency
  const c = await parallel(b.map(...))
that middle transform doesn't need the barrier. Rewrite as a pipeline with the transform inside a stage. When in doubt: pipeline.

Concurrent agent() calls are capped at min(16, available CPUs - 2) per workflow — excess calls queue and run as slots free up. You can still pass 100 items to parallel()/pipeline() and they all complete; only ~10 run at any moment. Total agent count across a workflow's lifetime is capped at 1000 — a runaway-loop backstop set far above any real workflow. A single parallel()/pipeline() call accepts at most 4096 items; passing more is an explicit error, not a silent truncation.

When a barrier IS correct — dedup across all findings before expensive verification:
  const all = await parallel(DIMENSIONS.map(d => () => agent(d.prompt, {schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA})))
  const deduped = dedupeByFileAndLine(all.filter(Boolean).flatMap(r => r.findings))  // <-- genuinely needs ALL at once
  const verified = await parallel(deduped.map(f => () => agent(verifyPrompt(f), {schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})))

Loop-until-count pattern — accumulate to a target:
  const bugs = []
  while (bugs.length < 10) {
    const result = await agent("Find bugs in this codebase.", {schema: BUGS_SCHEMA})
    bugs.push(...result.bugs)
    log(`${bugs.length}/10 found`)
  }

Loop-until-budget pattern — scale depth to the user's "+500k" directive. Guard on budget.total: with no target set, remaining() is Infinity and the loop would run straight to the 1000-agent cap.
  const bugs = []
  while (budget.total && budget.remaining() > 50_000) {
    const result = await agent("Find bugs in this codebase.", {schema: BUGS_SCHEMA})
    bugs.push(...result.bugs)
    log(`${bugs.length} found, ${Math.round(budget.remaining()/1000)}k remaining`)
  }

Composing patterns — exhaustive review (find → dedup vs seen → diverse-lens panel → loop-until-dry):
  const seen = new Set(), confirmed = []
  let dry = 0
  while (dry < 2) {                                              // loop-until-dry
    const found = (await parallel(FINDERS.map(f => () =>          // barrier: collect all finders this round
      agent(f.prompt, {phase: 'Find', schema: BUGS})))).filter(Boolean).flatMap(r => r.bugs)
    const fresh = found.filter(b => !seen.has(key(b)))           // dedup vs ALL seen — plain code, not an agent
    if (!fresh.length) { dry++; continue }
    dry = 0; fresh.forEach(b => seen.add(key(b)))
    const judged = await parallel(fresh.map(b => () =>           // every fresh bug judged concurrently...
      parallel(['correctness','security','repro'].map(lens => () =>   // ...each by 3 distinct lenses
        agent(`Judge "${b.desc}" via the ${lens} lens — real?`, {phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT})))
        .then(vs => ({ b, real: vs.filter(Boolean).filter(v => v.real).length >= 2 }))))
    confirmed.push(...judged.filter(v => v.real).map(v => v.b))
  }
  return confirmed
  // dedup vs `seen`, NOT `confirmed` — else judge-rejected findings reappear every round and it never converges.

Quality patterns — common shapes; pick by task and compose freely:
- Adversarial verify: spawn N independent skeptics per finding, each prompted to REFUTE. Kill if ≥majority refute. Prevents plausible-but-wrong findings from surviving.
    const votes = await parallel(Array.from({length: 3}, () => () =>
      agent(`Try to refute: ${claim}. Default to refuted=true if uncertain.`, {schema: VERDICT})))
    const survives = votes.filter(Boolean).filter(v => !v.refuted).length >= 2
- Perspective-diverse verify: when a finding can fail in more than one way, give each verifier a distinct lens (correctness, security, perf, does-it-reproduce) instead of N identical refuters — diversity catches failure modes redundancy can't.
- Judge panel: generate N independent attempts from different angles (e.g. MVP-first, risk-first, user-first), score with parallel judges, synthesize from the winner while grafting the best ideas from runners-up. Beats one-attempt-iterated when the solution space is wide.
- Loop-until-dry: for unknown-size discovery (bugs, issues, edge cases), keep spawning finders until K consecutive rounds return nothing new. Simple counters (while count < N) miss the tail.
- Multi-modal sweep: parallel agents each searching a different way (by-container, by-content, by-entity, by-time). Each is blind to what the others surface; useful when one search angle won't find everything.
- Completeness critic: a final agent that asks "what's missing — modality not run, claim unverified, source unread?" What it finds becomes the next round of work.
- No silent caps: if a workflow bounds coverage (top-N, no-retry, sampling), `log()` what was dropped — silent truncation reads as "covered everything" when it didn't.

Scale to what the user asked for. "find any bugs" → a few finders, single-vote verify. "thoroughly audit this" or "be comprehensive" → larger finder pool, 3–5 vote adversarial pass, synthesis stage. When unsure, lean toward thoroughness for research/review/audit requests and toward brevity for quick checks.

These patterns aren't exhaustive — compose novel harnesses when the task calls for it (tournament brackets, self-repair loops, staged escalation, whatever fits).

Use this tool for multi-step orchestration where control flow should be deterministic (loops, conditionals, fan-out) rather than model-driven.

## Resume

The tool result includes a runId. To resume after a pause, kill, or script edit, relaunch with Workflow({scriptPath, resumeFromRunId}) — the longest unchanged prefix of agent() calls returns cached results instantly; the first edited/new call and everything after it runs live. Same script + same args → 100% cache hit. Before diagnosing why a completed workflow returned an empty or unexpected result, Read <transcriptDir>/journal.jsonl — it records each agent's actual return value; do not assume cached results are non-empty. Date.now()/Math.random()/new Date() are unavailable in scripts (they would break this) — stamp results after the workflow returns, or pass timestamps via args. Fallback when no journal is available: Read agent-<id>.jsonl files in the transcript directory and hand-author a continuation script.

description: "How arisecenla.church is built on Wix — Velo custom-element architecture, which local files are canonical, CMS collections, backend modules, page slugs, gotchas, and the local sample site"

Wix classic Editor + Velo. Wix has no REST API for layout, so whole pages ship as **Velo custom elements** in `public/custom-elements/`. Pattern: CMS collection → backend web module (`content.web.js` etc.) → page code (`$w.onReady`, retry-until-ready, sets a `data-*` attribute with `JSON.stringify`) → element reads the attribute and renders. Forms in the elements POST to `/_functions/ariseForm` (`backend/http-functions.js` → `FormSubmissions` collection first, then email/automation).

- **Local project:** `D:\projects\Arise Church Website` (not a git repo). `files.zip` = everything to Aug 2026 (75 files: docs, mockups, images, CSVs, element JS); `files2.zip` = `ARISE-HANDOFF.md` (newest, Aug 23 2026), `AUDIT-REPORT.md`, and `arise-fixed-2026-08-23.zip`. Both were extracted on 2026-09-13 into `files/` and `files2/`.
- **CANONICAL element set = `files2/arise-fixed-2026-08-23/*.js` (21 files).** The same-named files in `files/` are older (13 differ). Legacy files that also define the same tags and must not be installed: `arise-pages.js`, `arise-hero.js`, `arise-events-sermons.js`, `arise-service-times.js`, `arise-service-times-v2.js` (canonical is `arise-service-times-final.js`).
- **Backend code exists only as code blocks inside the `*-SETUP.md` docs** (no `.jsw`/`.web.js` files in the zips), and the docs disagree: `events.jsw` (EVENTS-SETUP) vs `events.web.js` (handoff); two different `getPageContent` implementations (PAGECONTENT-SETUP returns `{text,image}`, ALEXANDRIA-SETUP returns string|`{text,imageUrl}`); INSTALL-ORDER still says Serve uses `arise-form.js` while SERVE-SETUP/handoff use `arise-serve.js`; FORMS-SETUP's `http-functions.js` uses `triggeredEmails.emailContact` with an email address instead of a contactId.
- **Elements → pages:** arise-header + arise-footer sitewide; arise-home `/` (+ arise-service-times placed top-right of the hero, 360×80); arise-about `/about`; arise-leaders `/leaders`; arise-ministries `/ministries`; arise-sermons `/sermons`; arise-events `/events`; arise-contact `/contact`; arise-bible `/arise-bible` (calls bible-api.com directly; 16 translations, no NIV/ESV); arise-serve `/serve`; arise-connect `/connect-groups`; arise-creatives `/creative-arts` + `/praise-worship /musicians /production /sound /media-team /content` via `data-dept`; arise-classes `/classes`; galleries arise-childrens `/childrens`, arise-youth `/youth`, arise-outreach `/outreach`, arise-leadnetwork `/lead-network` (Portfolio projects → `data-photos`); arise-alexandria `/arise-alexandria` (NOT `/alexandria`); arise-form reusable (`data-form=contact|serve|prayer`).
- **CMS collections (read in full 2026-09-14; reference at `audit/CMS-REFERENCE-2026-09-14.md`):** 12 custom: Leaders(7 incl. Kristina), Ministries(9 incl. Connect Groups + Arise Creative Arts), PageContent(45 keys), ServePositions(7), ConnectGroups(0), CreativeDepartments(6), CreativeMembers(14, no Thelma), HomeSettings(churchCulture: video uploaded + active), SiteSettings(sermonSeries: "The Kingdom / Culture of Giving"), Studies(2, videoUrl blank), FormSubmissions(1 unhandled, admin-only), `Import1` = ArchivedFormSubmissions(50, admin-only). **PastEvents does NOT exist.** All content collections: read Anyone / write Admin. Image fields are Wix Image type; the live backend converts wix:image → https (undocumented `imgUrl` helper).
- **App collections:** Portfolio/Projects = 5 (Children's `621e6fdb…`, Youth `c2be296e…`, Outreach `78e5e5f9…`, Lead Network `885f9ceb…`, Exciting News `b2697282…`) but ProjectItems has only 1 item (Arise Hub video) → galleries empty; Events/Events 20 (1 scheduled: The Outpour 30 Oct 2026); Bookings/Services 3; Stores/Products 2; Locations/Locations 2 (duplicate Pineville, no Alexandria); Members 82; legacy Forms/contact032 + stripsContact042 hold 8+8 old submissions; third-party `@hanas535/events-calendar/events` holds 16 demo rows.
- **Gotchas:** custom elements render in an iframe in Editor/Preview — only Published is real; `/_functions/` don't work in Preview; element code pasted into page code/masterPage throws "document is not defined"; check the element ID per page (Classes was `#customElement5`); custom-element text is invisible to Google — homepage still has no native H1/meta description (2026-09-13); Wix classic has no text-transform control; header `NAV` array is hardcoded; Wix serves each element file in its own module scope.
- **Local sample site (built 2026-09-13):** `sample-site/` — `node sample-site/server.js` → http://localhost:4173/_sample (hub listing every route); `.claude/launch.json` config `arise-sample`; pages generated by `build.js`, fixtures by `make-fixtures.js` (reads `files/PageContent.csv`, merges `fixtures-cms.json` if present); mock `/_functions/ariseForm` mirrors the handoff backend. ## 4. The three page-code defects

**A. Department pages target the wrong element ID.** The hub page's element is `#customElement5`;
the six department pages were almost certainly duplicated from it, so their element is not
`#customElement1`. `$w('#customElement1')` finds nothing, `typeof el.setAttribute` is never
`'function'`, and the loop gives up after 30 tries without a warning. Settle it by right-clicking the
element on any department page → View Properties. Fix: use the real ID, or select the element by
type so the ID no longer matters.

**B. Past Sermons guards on `.length`.** `$w('#customElement1')` returns a single element, and
the code treats a missing `.length` as "not found". Whether or not the ID is also wrong, the guard
fails first. Fix: the same typeof-setAttribute retry used on Events and Ministries.

**C. masterPage.js never finds the elements.** `$w('*').filter(e => e.type === '$w.CustomElement')`
returns nothing on every page, so the broadcast that was supposed to feed the header, footer and every
page without its own content code is a no-op. That is why the 11 `site.*` keys (tagline, campus
names, service times, email) never reach the header and footer. Fix pending a Velo-docs check
(expected: select with the `CustomElement` type selector).
input.new_string:
## 4. The three page-code defects

Each was checked against the Velo reference and adversarially reviewed (workflow of 14 Sept; verdicts
in the session task output). The Velo `$w()` reference documents exactly three selector forms —
`#id`, a type name such as `CustomElement`, and a comma list — and says an `#id` selection returns
**one Element object**, while a type selection returns **an array, even for zero or one match**.

**A. Department pages target an element ID that is not on the page — confirmed.** Identical code
lands on Home, Events, Ministries and Contact with `#customElement1`, and the hub had to be pointed
at `#customElement5` to work; the six department pages log the successful fetch and then nothing
reaches the element. The exact ID on those pages is still unverified (right-click the element →
View Properties). Fix: select by type — `$w('CustomElement')[0]` — so the ID no longer matters,
and add a final `console.warn` to every retry loop so a miss is never silent again.

**B. Past Sermons dies on `if (!$w(EL).length)` — confirmed, but the cause behind it is not
settled.** A single-element selection has no `.length`, so the guard bails even when the ID is
right; if the ID is also wrong it bails for that reason instead. The typeof-setAttribute retry
alone would NOT fix a wrong ID (Praise & Worship proves that). Fix: the same type selector as A,
which works either way.

**C. masterPage.js never finds any element — confirmed.** `$w('*')` is not a documented selector,
and the loop exits silently after 30 tries; on /contact the page's own code puts `data-content` on
`<arise-contact>` while `<arise-header>` and `<arise-footer>` in the same DOM have no attributes at
all. Consequence: the 11 `site.*` keys (tagline, campus names, service times, email) never reach the
header or footer, and About, Ministries, Events, Leaders, Sermons and the galleries get no CMS text.
Fix: `$w('CustomElement').forEach(el => el.setAttribute('data-content', json))` — documented,
returns an empty array on pages with no element instead of erroring.

# What is actually running in Wix — 14 Sept 2026

Sources: Bradly pasted the live element files, backend files and page code into the chat; the exact
element sources AND every page-code file were then recovered from the published site's bundler source
maps, so everything below is definitive. Live behaviour was checked in the browser console and DOM of
https://www.arisecenla.church on 14 Sept 2026. The page code Bradly pasted from the Editor is
byte-identical to the published code (only a trailing newline differs), so there are no unpublished
code changes.

Where the live code is saved locally:

| What | Where |
|---|---|
| Exact live element sources (19) | `files2/live-elements/src/arise-*.js` (from the `.map` files in `files2/live-elements/maps/`) |
| Minified live bundles (19) | `files2/live-elements/arise-*.js` |
| Live backend files (7, as pasted) | `files2/live-backend/` |
| Live page code (as pasted, 22 files) | `files2/live-page-code/` |
| Published page code (recovered, 20 files incl. Serve, Leaders, the four galleries, Youth) | `files2/live-page-code/recovered/` |

How recovery works: each published element loads from
`https://bundler-velo.parastorage.com/v_metaSiteId_5fff0585-…/gridAppId_c1613cca-…/filePath_public_delimiter_custom-elements_delimiter_arise-<tag>.js/…`
and its source map at `https://bundler.wix-code.com/5fff0585-…/undefined/c1613cca-…/custom-elements/arise-<tag>.js.map`
carries the original file in `sourcesContent`. Page code maps live at `…/pages/<pageId>.js.map`
(entry `public/pages/<pageId>.js`); the page id is printed in the browser console
("Running the code for the … page … open <pageId>.js"). The grid id changes on every Publish.

## 1. Custom elements — which version is live

| Element | Live version | Lines the fixed file would add / remove | Live element observes |
|---|---|---|---|
| arise-alexandria | **= canonical** | — | data-content |
| arise-leaders | = canonical | — | data-leaders, data-content |
| arise-ministries | = canonical | — | data-ministries, data-content |
| arise-sermons | = canonical | — | data-live-video, data-series-*, data-content |
| arise-home | pre-fix original (`files/`) | +42 / −28 | data-photos, data-news, data-culture, data-content |
| arise-header | pre-fix original | +8 / −3 | data-content |
| arise-footer | pre-fix original | +6 / −6 | data-content |
| arise-about | pre-fix original | +13 / −4 | data-content |
| arise-contact | pre-fix original | +12 / −6 | data-content |
| arise-connect | pre-fix original | +10 / −7 | data-groups, data-content |
| arise-events | pre-fix original | +5 / −3 | data-events, data-content |
| arise-bible | **older than files.zip** (no data-content hook, no phone kicker fix) — and now **deleted from Velo** | +37 / −1 | nothing |
| arise-childrens | older than files.zip | +59 / −12 | data-photos |
| arise-youth | older than files.zip | +57 / −10 | data-photos |
| arise-outreach | older than files.zip | +58 / −11 | data-photos |
| arise-leadnetwork | older than files.zip | +61 / −14 | data-photos |
| arise-serve | older than files.zip | +50 / −10 | data-positions |
| arise-classes | older than files.zip | +40 / −4 | data-classes |
| arise-creatives | older than files.zip | +45 / −8 | data-depts, data-members, data-dept |
| arise-service-times(-final) | **not published** | | |
| arise-form | not published | | |

Three generations are live at once. Pasting `files2/arise-fixed-2026-08-23/` replaces all of them with one.
The eight "older than files.zip" elements have no Page Content hooks, so today no CMS text or image
reaches those pages at all — and the five broken `c3b2d0_` image rows are harmless until the fixed
files go in. Fix those five rows first.

## 2. Backend files (`files2/live-backend/`)

| File | What it is | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `content.web.js` | getPageContent, getLeaders, getMinistries, getConnectGroups, getCreatives, getServePositions, getHomeSettings | Defines `imgUrl` and converts every image field. getPageContent returns `{text, image}` (PAGECONTENT-SETUP shape). |
| `http-functions.js` | post_ariseForm | ALLOWED = 5 types. Stores the row, then `contacts.appendOrCreateContact`, then Automations trigger `519d3164-8dae-4448-a362-35ff96ed2068`. Both extras are try/catch — failures show only in the site log. |
| `events.web.js` | getEvents (`@wix/events`) | **This is the one the Events page imports.** Converts mainImage, falls back to `/events-1/<slug>`, still has the TEMPORARY console.log, no upcoming sort. |
| `events.jsw` | getEvents (old `wix-events.v2`) | **Dead code** — nothing imports it. Delete. |
| `classes.web.js` | getPrograms (`@wix/online-programs`) | Links to `/class-detail/<slug>` (correct). Live returns 0 programs — nothing is published in Online Programs. |
| `gallery.web.js` | getProjectPhotos(projectId) (`@wix/portfolio`) | Fine; returns [] until the Portfolio projects have items (they log "Gallery: 0 items" today). |
| `youtube.jsw` | getLiveVideoId, getCurrentSeries | 6-name IGNORE list. |

## 3. Page code — what each page sends, and whether it lands

"Lands" was checked by reading the element's DOM attributes on the published page 8–10 s after load.

| Page (Velo file) | Targets | Sets | Lands? | Live result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Home (qpco5) | #customElement1 | data-content, data-culture, data-news | yes | Works. (Raw `data-ck` text on the page is the pre-fix element's bug, not page code.) |
| Arise Church Alexandria (hgxqe) | #customElement5 | data-content | yes | Works. |
| Connect Groups (zvxz2) | #customElement1 | data-content, data-groups | yes | Works; logs "Connect Groups: 0" because the collection is empty → "Groups are forming". |
| Creative Arts hub (m59gp) | #customElement5 | data-content, data-depts, data-members | yes | 6 department tiles. (data-content ignored by the live element.) |
| Praise & Worship (ps77x), Musicians, Production, Sound (wtsvl), Media (bv9n3), Social Media & Content | **#customElement1** | data-content, data-depts, data-members | **NO** | Logs "Creatives: 6 departments, 14 members", but the element carries only the Editor-set `data-dept`. → slug as H1, no tabs, "Team coming soon". |
| Classes (b4yyk) | #customElement5 | data-content, data-classes | yes | "Classes: 0 programs" → coming-soon panel. |
| Past Sermons (sg492) | #customElement1 | data-series-*, data-live-video | **NO** | Bails at `if (!$w(EL).length)` → console warns "custom element #customElement1 not found"; element has no attributes; badge stays "Latest Service". |
| Ministries (d2xew) | #customElement1 | data-ministries | yes | 9 ministries. |
| Events (c24vq) | #customElement1 | data-events | yes | 1 upcoming, 8 past. |
| Contact (rjf74) | #customElement1 | data-content | yes | Works ("Sunday Sunday" is CMS text). |
| Meet our Leaders (gliws) | #customElement1 | data-leaders | yes | Works. |
| Sign Up to Serve (j9kva) | **#customElement1** | data-content, data-positions | **NO** | Logs "Serve: 7 positions"; element has no attributes → shows the 5 built-in fallback roles instead of the 7 CMS positions. |
| Children's Ministry (ih40z), Youth Ministry (gqfab), Outreach (j03bc), Lead Network (coke9) | **#customElement1** | data-content, data-photos | **NO** | Log "Content: 45 keys" and "Gallery: 0 items"; nothing reaches the element. Project IDs match the Portfolio projects, which are empty anyway. |

## Will break the moment the page code goes in (verified in the sample with the real CMS rows)

12. **Five Page Content image rows 403 on the CDN** — `childrens.kids.photo`, `childrens.superkid.logo`, `outreach.supplies.image`, `leadnetwork.austin.photo`, `leadnetwork.calloway.photo` use a `c3b2d0_` media ID; the working files are `1f9fa2_`. Fix: edit the five `imageUrl` values in CMS → Page Content.
13. **Outreach and Lead Network:** `this.fillGallery(); this.applyContent();` sit inside a `.map()` callback after `return` (arise-outreach.js:251, arise-leadnetwork.js:322) — unreachable on first build; only matters when attributes precede upgrade (Wix re-mount).
14. **Class links** would go to `/classes/{slug}`; the live Online Programs page is `/class-detail`.
15. **Sermons series band** hides only on `data-series-active="false"`; the live page gets no attributes, so the hardcoded "The Kingdom · Culture of Giving" shows (matches today).
16. **Connect flyers / ministry images** depend on the backend converting Wix image fields; the docs' getters pass them raw (the live backend evidently converts — leader portraits load).
17. **Service Times panel dies on a Wix re-mount** (`disconnectedCallback` removes the panel, the `_built` guard never rebuilds it).

## What the CMS can and cannot change today (added 14 Sept after Bradly's note)

Bradly's expectation: every editable fact comes from the CMS. Today that holds for the **times** but not for the words around them, and not for four elements at all.

| Thing | State | Where |
|---|---|---|
| Alexandria times (Sunday, Wed prayer, Wed Bible study) on Home, Contact, Alexandria page | **CMS-linked** (`site.times.second.*`), values already right in the CMS | — |
| Row labels "Pre-Service Prayer" / "Midweek Service" | **Hardcoded.** Pastor Sheron calls them Prayer and Bible Study; cannot be renamed from the CMS | arise-home.js:462–463, arise-contact.js:306–307, arise-alexandria.js:217–218 |
| Service Times dropdown ("10:30 AM · Both campuses") | **Entirely hardcoded**, no `data-content` support; wrong for Alexandria | arise-service-times-final.js:78–80 |
| Header mobile menu times and phone | **Hardcoded**; panel sits outside the element so hooks cannot reach it; header never receives `data-content` (masterPage.js is empty) | arise-header.js:254–259 |
| Footer columns / footer bottom strip | Columns hooked but footer never receives `data-content`; bottom strip hardcoded | arise-footer.js:121–122, 153 |
| "Sunday 10:30 AM in Pineville, 10:00 AM in Alexandria" sentences | **Hardcoded**, no hooks | about:318, leaders:331, ministries:298, events:260, bible:230, childrens:285, youth:247 |
| Connect Groups tab label "Sign up by September 2" | Hardcoded (the card is hooked) | arise-connect.js:388 |
| Culture video heading/kicker | CMS fields exist in Home Settings; element ignores them | arise-home.js:429 |

To make all of it CMS-driven: add label rows to Page Content (e.g. `site.times.second.prayer.label`) with `data-ck` hooks; give `arise-service-times` a `data-content` attribute and bind its rows; add a small `masterPage.js` that fetches Page Content once and sets `data-content` on the header and footer (and scope the header's panel); add hooks to the seven CTA sentences and the footer strip. One Page Content map then feeds every element.

## Decisions — two resolved on 14 Sept
.....
## Code review of the 21 canonical files (static; live impact none today)

- **Escaping:** all 18 elements with `applyContent()` write CMS text via `innerHTML` unescaped and build a CSS selector from the CMS key; Leaders, Ministries, Sermons (series title), Home and the galleries (video IDs/poster) concatenate CMS values raw. Admin-only writes, so robustness rather than security.
- **Accessibility:** About popups, home and gallery lightboxes, mobile menu lack dialog role / focus trap / focus return (menu returns focus); form status never announced, no `aria-required`/`aria-invalid` (contact, serve, connect, form); Connect tabs half-ARIA; Events "Sold Out" is a link with `pointer-events:none`; placeholders at 3.0:1.
- **Brand:** Anton below 18px in contact labels (13), creatives badge/switcher/h3 (13/14/16), events h3 and labels (15/13), header wordmark/panel title (17/15), about popup labels (16).
- **Dead CMS hooks:** header/footer never receive `data-content` (`site.tagline` dead; the mobile panel is outside the element anyway); About, Leaders, Events, Ministries, Bible observe `data-content` with no hooks; Home ignores CMS `heading`/`kicker`; `isLeader` unused; footer bottom strip hardcodes times.
- **Lifecycle:** service-times re-mount (17); home re-attach does not restart the news timer/video observer; news timer not cleared on empty list; header re-attach with the menu open; Bible overlapping requests.
- **Dead weight:** duplicated culture-video CSS in home; Events constants/CSS inside sermons; ~100 lines of unused shared CSS in leaders/ministries; unused `_setOpen` in header; stale file headers ("PAST SERMONS", `events.jsw`, "delete the Bible page code").

One finder claim was refuted on re-check: "sermons iframe reloads every 60 s" — the documented page code only re-sets the attribute when the video ID changes.

## What checked out (rendered, 27 routes × 1366 and 390, plus forced dark)

0 JavaScript errors · 0 horizontal overflow · 0 contrast failures on rendered text · 0 tap targets under 24px · 0 duplicate IDs · 0 images without alt · one H1 per page · dark mode identical to light · every internal link in the 21 files resolves to a live 200/301 · menu, dropdown, popups, lightbox, tabs, join pre-fill all work · contact form validates and saves against the mock backend · Bible Search returns John 3:16 from the live API · live Events images and Leaders portraits all load.

## Suggested order, when you say go

1. CMS edits (five image URLs, two Sunday rows, four season rows) — no publish needed.
2. Paste the 13 fixed files and publish (optionally with the small code fixes above — say which).
3. Page code on the pages that have none (6 department pages, Serve, Children's, Youth, Outreach, Lead Network, Sermons), checking the element ID on each.
4. Place the Service Times element on Home, after settling the Alexandria time.
5. Native H1 + campus addresses on the homepage.
6. Docs cleanup; move the archived-submissions CSV out of the shared zip.

## What the CMS can and cannot change today (added 14 Sept after Bradly's note)

Bradly's expectation: every editable fact comes from the CMS. Today that holds for the **times** but not for the words around them, and not for four elements at all.

| Thing | State | Where |
|---|---|---|
| Alexandria times (Sunday, Wed prayer, Wed Bible study) on Home, Contact, Alexandria page | **CMS-linked** (`site.times.second.*`), values already right in the CMS | — |
| Row labels "Pre-Service Prayer" / "Midweek Service" | **Hardcoded.** Pastor Sheron calls them Prayer and Bible Study; cannot be renamed from the CMS | arise-home.js:462–463, arise-contact.js:306–307, arise-alexandria.js:217–218 |
| Service Times dropdown ("10:30 AM · Both campuses") | **Entirely hardcoded**, no `data-content` support; wrong for Alexandria | arise-service-times-final.js:78–80 |
| Header mobile menu times and phone | **Hardcoded**; panel sits outside the element so hooks cannot reach it; header never receives `data-content` (masterPage.js is empty) | arise-header.js:254–259 |

| "Sunday 10:30 AM in Pineville, 10:00 AM in Alexandria" sentences | **Hardcoded**, no hooks | about:318, leaders:331, ministries:298, events:260, bible:230, childrens:285, youth:247 |
| Connect Groups tab label "Sign up by September 2" | Hardcoded (the card is hooked) | arise-connect.js:388 |
| Culture video heading/kicker | CMS fields exist in Home Settings; element ignores them | arise-home.js:429 |

To make all of it CMS-driven: add label rows to Page Content (e.g. `site.times.second.prayer.label`) with `data-ck` hooks; give `arise-service-times` a `data-content` attribute and bind its rows; add a small `masterPage.js` that fetches Page Content once and sets `data-content` on the header and footer (and scope the header's panel); add hooks to the seven CTA sentences and the footer strip. One Page Content map then feeds every element.

## Decisions — two resolved on 14 Sept
.....
## Code review of the 21 canonical files (static; live impact none today)

- **Escaping:** all 18 elements with `applyContent()` write CMS text via `innerHTML` unescaped and build a CSS selector from the CMS key; Leaders, Ministries, Sermons (series title), Home and the galleries (video IDs/poster) concatenate CMS values raw. Admin-only writes, so robustness rather than security.
- **Accessibility:** About popups, home and gallery lightboxes, mobile menu lack dialog role / focus trap / focus return (menu returns focus); form status never announced, no `aria-required`/`aria-invalid` (contact, serve, connect, form); Connect tabs half-ARIA; Events "Sold Out" is a link with `pointer-events:none`; placeholders at 3.0:1.
- **Brand:** Anton below 18px in contact labels (13), creatives badge/switcher/h3 (13/14/16), events h3 and labels (15/13), header wordmark/panel title (17/15), about popup labels (16).
- **Dead CMS hooks:** header/footer never receive `data-content` (`site.tagline` dead; the mobile panel is outside the element anyway); About, Leaders, Events, Ministries, Bible observe `data-content` with no hooks; Home ignores CMS `heading`/`kicker`; `isLeader` unused; footer bottom strip hardcodes times.
- **Lifecycle:** service-times re-mount (17); home re-attach does not restart the news timer/video observer; news timer not cleared on empty list; header re-attach with the menu open; Bible overlapping requests.
- **Dead weight:** duplicated culture-video CSS in home; Events constants/CSS inside sermons; ~100 lines of unused shared CSS in leaders/ministries; unused `_setOpen` in header; stale file headers ("PAST SERMONS", `events.jsw`, "delete the Bible page code").

One finder claim was refuted on re-check: "sermons iframe reloads every 60 s" — the documented page code only re-sets the attribute when the video ID changes.

## What checked out (rendered, 27 routes × 1366 and 390, plus forced dark)

0 JavaScript errors · 0 horizontal overflow · 0 contrast failures on rendered text · 0 tap targets under 24px · 0 duplicate IDs · 0 images without alt · one H1 per page · dark mode identical to light · every internal link in the 21 files resolves to a live 200/301 · menu, dropdown, popups, lightbox, tabs, join pre-fill all work · contact form validates and saves against the mock backend · Bible Search returns John 3:16 from the live API · live Events images and Leaders portraits all load.

1. CMS edits (five image URLs, two Sunday rows, four season rows) — no publish needed.
2. Paste the 13 fixed files and publish (optionally with the small code fixes above — say which).
3. Page code on the pages that have none (6 department pages, Serve, Children's, Youth, Outreach, Lead Network, Sermons), checking the element ID on each.
4. Place the Service Times element on Home, after settling the Alexandria time.
5. Native H1 + campus addresses on the homepage.
6. Docs cleanup; move the archived-submissions CSV out of the shared zip.

# Arise Church — installing the 14 Sept 2026 fixes in Wix Everything in this folder was tested in the local sample before it came to you (see "What was tested" at the end). Do the steps in order, and **publish only once, at the very end**. Custom elements and page code do not run properly in the Editor or Preview, so check the published site afterwards. The live code as it was before these changes is saved in `files2/live-elements/src/`, `files2/live-backend/` and `files2/live-page-code/`. Pasting those back undoes everything. --- ## Step 1 — CMS (no publish needed) **1a. Five broken images.** These Page Content rows point at image files that no longer exist, so the page would show a blank box once the fixed elements are in. Open CMS → Page Content, find each key, and **clear the `imageUrl` cell** (the page then keeps its built-in photo), or upload the right photo into the `image` field. | contentKey | Page | |---|---| | childrens.kids.photo | Children's Ministry | | childrens.superkid.logo | Children's Ministry | | outreach.supplies.image | Outreach | | leadnetwork.austin.photo | Lead Network | | leadnetwork.calloway.photo | Lead Network | **1b. Add the new editable rows.** CMS → Page Content → More actions → Import → choose `cms/PageContent-new-rows.csv` → **add as new items** (do not replace). Every new row already contains the text the page shows today, so importing changes nothing you can see. From then on, editing a row's `text` (or `image`) changes that spot on the site. `cms/PageContent-all-keys.md` lists every key by page with a plain description of where it appears. Notes for editors: - `text` is shown as written. You may use `
` for a line break. Do not type a lone `<`. - Service times keep the day in the value ("Sunday 10:30 AM"). Rows that already say the day in their label drop the repeated day automatically. - Row labels such as "Prayer" and "Bible Study" have their own keys ending in `.label`. ## Step 2 — Backend (Velo sidebar → Backend) | File | Action | |---|---| | `backend/events.web.js` | Replace the whole file with `backend/events.web.js` from this folder | | `backend/classes.web.js` | Replace the whole file with `backend/classes.web.js` from this folder | | `backend/events.jsw` | **Delete** — nothing uses it (the Events page imports `events.web.js`) | | `content.web.js`, `http-functions.js`, `gallery.web.js`, `youtube.jsw` | Leave as they are — identical to what is live | ## Step 3 — Custom elements (Velo sidebar → Public → custom-elements) **First, re-create the Bible file you deleted:** New file → `arise-bible.js` → paste `custom-elements/arise-bible.js` from this folder. Then open the Bible Search page in the Editor, click the custom element → Choose Source and make sure it points at `arise-bible.js`. Then, for each file below, open the file of the same name in Velo, select all, and paste the new file over it: arise-about.js · arise-alexandria.js · arise-childrens.js · arise-classes.js · arise-connect.js · arise-contact.js · arise-creatives.js · arise-events.js · arise-footer.js · arise-header.js · arise-home.js · arise-leaders.js · arise-leadnetwork.js · arise-ministries.js · arise-outreach.js · arise-sermons.js · arise-serve.js · arise-youth.js Optional, not installed today: `arise-service-times-final.js` (the Service Times dropdown for the homepage hero) and `arise-form.js` (reusable form). # Arise Church — local sample site

A local render of the Velo custom elements in `files2/arise-fixed-2026-08-23/`
(the canonical set), composed the way the published Wix site composes them:
header element + one page element + footer element.

## Run it

```bash
node sample-site/server.js
```

Then open **http://localhost:4173/_sample** — the hub lists every page.

Clean URLs work exactly like the live site (`/about`, `/leaders`, `/creative-arts`,
`/praise-worship` …). `/tithes-and-offerings` and `/podcast` stop at a stand-in page
instead of redirecting off-site. Anything else that would be a Wix app page
(`/events-1/...`, `/classes/...`) shows a stand-in too.

## What feeds the elements

- `fixtures-cms.json` — real rows read from the live Wix CMS on 2026-09-13
  (Leaders, Ministries, PageContent, ServePositions, CreativeDepartments,
  CreativeMembers, HomeSettings, SiteSettings, Studies). Image URLs are exactly
  what the CMS holds, including the `c3b2d0_…` ones the CDN answers 403.
- `fixtures-data.js` — sample data for things the CMS does not have yet
  (connect groups, class rows, gallery photos, news items, past events). Every
  sample string says "Sample" so it cannot be mistaken for real content.
- `make-fixtures.js` merges both (plus `files/PageContent.csv`) into `fixtures.js`.
- `mock-page-code.js` plays the role of the Velo page code: it waits for the
  element, then sets the `data-*` attributes 350 ms later, as production does.

Main routes get **only what the live site's page code would send today**
(no `data-events` because the events backend is not installed, empty galleries
because Portfolio has no items, etc.). Routes under `/_sample/` feed the same
elements sample data so every feature can be seen.

## Forms

The elements POST to `/_functions/ariseForm`. `server.js` mocks that endpoint
with the same validation as the handoff's `http-functions.js` (ALLOWED list,
email regex, required fields). Submissions are printed to the console and
listed at `/_sample/submissions.json`. Nothing is emailed or saved.

## Rebuild after editing

```bash
node sample-site/build.js && node sample-site/make-fixtures.js
```

`assets/audit.js` is a dev helper (`window.__audit()`) used for the render
audit; it is not part of the site.

# Arise Church — local sample site

A local render of the Velo custom elements in `files2/arise-fixed-2026-08-23/`
(the canonical set), composed the way the published Wix site composes them:
header element + one page element + footer element.

## Run it

```bash
node sample-site/server.js
```

Then open **http://localhost:4173/_sample** — the hub lists every page.

Clean URLs work exactly like the live site (`/about`, `/leaders`, `/creative-arts`,
`/praise-worship` …). `/tithes-and-offerings` and `/podcast` stop at a stand-in page
instead of redirecting off-site. Anything else that would be a Wix app page
(`/events-1/...`, `/classes/...`) shows a stand-in too.

## What feeds the elements

- `fixtures-cms.json` — real rows read from the live Wix CMS on 2026-09-13
  (Leaders, Ministries, PageContent, ServePositions, CreativeDepartments,
  CreativeMembers, HomeSettings, SiteSettings, Studies). Image URLs are exactly
  what the CMS holds, including the `c3b2d0_…` ones the CDN answers 403.
- `fixtures-data.js` — sample data for things the CMS does not have yet
  (connect groups, class rows, gallery photos, news items, past events). Every
  sample string says "Sample" so it cannot be mistaken for real content.
- `make-fixtures.js` merges both (plus `files/PageContent.csv`) into `fixtures.js`.
- `mock-page-code.js` plays the role of the Velo page code: it waits for the
  element, then sets the `data-*` attributes 350 ms later, as production does.

Main routes get **only what the live site's page code would send today**
(no `data-events` because the events backend is not installed, empty galleries
because Portfolio has no items, etc.). Routes under `/_sample/` feed the same
elements sample data so every feature can be seen.

## Forms

The elements POST to `/_functions/ariseForm`. `server.js` mocks that endpoint
with the same validation as the handoff's `http-functions.js` (ALLOWED list,
email regex, required fields). Submissions are printed to the console and
listed at `/_sample/submissions.json`. Nothing is emailed or saved.

## Rebuild after editing

```bash
node sample-site/build.js && node sample-site/make-fixtures.js
```

`assets/audit.js` is a dev helper (`window.__audit()`) used for the render
audit; it is not part of the site.

# Arise Church — installing the 14 Sept 2026 fixes in Wix Everything in this folder was tested in the local sample before it came to you (see "What was tested" at the end). Do the steps in order, and **publish only once, at the very end**. Custom elements and page code do not run properly in the Editor or Preview, so check the published site afterwards. The live code as it was before these changes is saved in `files2/live-elements/src/`, `files2/live-backend/` and `files2/live-page-code/`. Pasting those back undoes everything. | Folder | What it holds | |---|---| | `custom-elements/` | 21 element files (bug fixes + CMS hooks on every text block and image) | | `page-code/` | 22 page-code files, one per page, plus `masterPage.js` | | `backend/` | the backend files; only two change | | `cms/` | `PageContent-new-rows.csv` to import, `PageContent-all-keys.md` listing every editable spot by page | --- ## Step 1 — CMS (no publish needed) **1a. Five broken images.** These Page Content rows point at image addresses that start `c3b2d0_`, which return "forbidden". The same photos exist under `1f9fa2_` (each address below was checked and loads). Without this edit those spots would show a blank box once the fixed elements are in. Open CMS → Page Content, find each key, and replace the `imageUrl` cell with the address shown: | contentKey | Page | New imageUrl | |---|---|---| | childrens.kids.photo | Children's Ministry | https://static.wixstatic.com/media/1f9fa2_a5448e514cc14ea08cb657e4f1a9cec4~mv2.jpg | | childrens.superkid.logo | Children's Ministry | https://static.wixstatic.com/media/1f9fa2_8c21ef4200d44594bcec41ac5680c2c0~mv2.jpg | | outreach.supplies.image | Outreach | https://static.wixstatic.com/media/1f9fa2_ef28ad94288a4068ac9c2974b4d4d545~mv2.jpg | | leadnetwork.austin.photo | Lead Network | https://static.wixstatic.com/media/1f9fa2_0118a2141a564a909b5c493b2f55211d~mv2.png | | leadnetwork.calloway.photo | Lead Network | https://static.wixstatic.com/media/1f9fa2_1331547403e94f94a08912f08d45d1de~mv2.png | If a row also has a file in its `image` field, that file wins over `imageUrl`; clear it if it shows the wrong photo. **1b. Two copy corrections in existing rows.** | contentKey | Change | |---|---| | alexandria.pastor.bio2 | "Apostle Bryant and **Prophet** Vanessa Sanders" → "Apostle Bryant and **Pastor** Vanessa Sanders" (the rest of Pastor Sheron's paragraph stays as she wrote it) | | connect.season.hostby | The page is host registration only for now. Put the real host sign-up deadline here, or **clear the text** to hide the deadline wherever it appears | **1c. Add the new editable rows.** CMS → Page Content → More actions → Import → choose `cms/PageContent-new-rows.csv` → **add as new items** (do not replace existing items). The file has **558 rows**: one for every heading, paragraph, button label, card label and photo that did not have a CMS row yet. Each row already holds the text the page shows today, so importing changes nothing you can see. From then on, editing a row's `text` (or `image`) changes that spot on the site. `cms/PageContent-all-keys.md` lists all 610 keys by page, with where each one appears. Notes for editors: - `text` is shown as written. You may use `
` for a line break. Do not type a lone `<`. - Service times keep the day in the value ("Sunday 10:30 AM"). Rows whose label already names the day drop the repeated day automatically. - Seven row labels are shared by several pages and differ between them (for example "Sunday Service" on Home and "Sunday" on Contact). They are **not** in the CSV, because one row sets that label on every page at once. Add one only if you want the same wording everywhere. They are listed at the end of `PageContent-all-keys.md`. - The footer year updates itself and has no row. ## Step 2 — Backend (Velo sidebar → Backend) | File | Action | |---|---| | `backend/events.web.js` | Replace the whole file with `backend/events.web.js` from this folder | | `backend/classes.web.js` | Replace the whole file with `backend/classes.web.js` from this folder | | `backend/events.jsw` | **Delete** — nothing uses it (the Events page imports `events.web.js`) | | `content.web.js`, `http-functions.js`, `gallery.web.js`, `youtube.jsw` | Leave as they are — identical to what is live | ## Step 3 — Custom elements (Velo sidebar → Public → custom-elements) **First, re-create the Bible file you deleted:** New file → `arise-bible.js` → paste `custom-elements/arise-bible.js` from this folder. Then open the Bible Search page in the Editor, click the custom element → Choose Source and make sure it points at `arise-bible.js`. Then, for each file below, open the file of the same name in Velo, select all, and paste the new file over it: arise-about.js · arise-alexandria.js · arise-childrens.js · arise-classes.js · arise-connect.js · arise-contact.js · arise-creatives.js · arise-events.js · arise-footer.js · arise-header.js · arise-home.js · arise-leaders.js · arise-leadnetwork.js · arise-ministries.js · arise-outreach.js · arise-sermons.js · arise-serve.js · arise-youth.js Optional, not installed today: `arise-service-times-final.js` (the Service Times dropdown for the homepage hero) and `arise-form.js` (reusable form). Both are fixed, CMS-hooked and tested, but placing them is a design decision. ## Step 4 — Page code Open each page in the Editor, open its code panel, select all, and paste the file of the same name from `page-code/`. For the site-wide file use Code panel → Site Code → `masterPage.js`. Home · Arise Church Alexandria · Connect Groups · Creative Arts · Praise and Worship · Musicians · Production · Sound · Media · Social Media and Content · Classes · Past Sermons · Ministries · Events · Contact · Sign Up to Serve! · Meet our Leaders · Children's Ministry · Youth Ministry · Outreach · Lead Network · masterPage.js Pages that need no code: About, Bible Search, Give, Job Board, Information Desk Registration, Podcast, Training. (About and Bible Search still get their CMS text, from `masterPage.js`.) Every page file finds its element even if the element ID is not the one written at the top, so you do not need to look up IDs. Each file writes a line in the browser console when data arrives, and a warning if it cannot find the element. ## Step 5 — Publish and check Publish, then open each page on the live site. On a computer, press F12 → Console to see the log lines. - [ ] Home — no stray code text under "Who We Are"; campus rows read "Sunday Service 10:30 AM" (no doubled day); Alexandria shows Prayer 6:00 PM and Bible Study 6:45 PM - [ ] Header menu on a phone — Sunday times, Glory Night, phone number; footer bottom line shows both campuses - [ ] Contact — "Sunday 10:30 AM" not "Sunday Sunday"; Directions open in a new tab - [ ] Praise & Worship, Musicians, Production, Sound, Media, Social Media & Content — department name as the heading, department tabs underneath, team cards - [ ] Serve — 7 positions (Praise & Worship and Production & Sound included) - [ ] Sermons — series band "The Kingdom · Culture of Giving" - [ ] Events — "Previous Events" button no longer goes to a 404 - [ ] Bible Search — search "John 3:16" returns the verse - [ ] Children's, Youth, Outreach, Lead Network — page renders, photos show - [ ] Connect Groups — only "Host a Group" shows; a host sign-up submits (a row appears in CMS → Form Submissions) - [ ] Alexandria — Pastor Sheron's second paragraph says "Pastor Vanessa Sanders" - [ ] Change one Page Content row's text, publish, and see it change on the page ## Small wording changes you may notice These places now show the CMS value instead of text that was typed into the code, so wording matches the rest of the site: - Bible Search, bottom box: "Sunday 10:30 AM in Pineville, Sunday 10:00 AM in Alexandria. Glory Nights Monday 7:00 PM." - Sermons, Glory Nights box: "Monday 7:00 PM" (was "Mondays 7:00 PM") - Contact, main campus rows: the Glory Night, Wednesday and Corporate Prayer times come from the CMS - Alexandria and Home: the two Wednesday rows are labelled "Prayer" and "Bible Study" ## Settled on 14 Sept - Titles are **Pastor Vanessa Sanders** and **Pastor Sheron Turner** (code fallback corrected; one CMS row in step 1b). - **Connect Groups is host registration only.** The "Join a Group" tab, the join form and the "Join This Group" buttons stay hidden. When groups are scheduled, open joining with one CMS row: add `connect.join.open` with the text `yes`, and publish. - There is no Thelma; the 14 Creative Members are complete. ## Still open (not changed in the code) - "Tioga, Louisiana" in Pastor Sheron's second paragraph (the main campus address is Pineville) - The Leaders collection row for Bryant & Vanessa Sanders still reads "Apostle · Pastor & Prophet" and "serves as Prophet" — edit in CMS → Leaders if that should change - Two dated sermon clips (Aug 22 baby shower, "Upcoming at Arise Church") — now editable in Page Content - Portfolio projects for the galleries and the homepage news panel are empty; Online Programs has no published class ## What was tested | Test | Result | |---|---| | Backend files under node with Wix mocked (`node sample-site/tests/backend.test.mjs`) | 12 of 12 pass | | Every page-code file, right element ID and wrong element ID, plus masterPage and Sermons (`node sample-site/tests/page-code.test.mjs`) | 44 of 44 pass | | Every sample page at desktop width: no script errors, no blank elements, Wix remove-and-re-add leaves the page unchanged, every CMS hook shows a changed CMS value, importing the CSV leaves the page unchanged, nothing worse than today's code (overflow, missing alt text, broken images, contrast, tap targets, heading count) | 34 of 34 pages pass | | The same checks at phone width (390 px) | 20 of 20 pages pass | | Connect Groups: default, with groups listed, joining opened from the CMS, deadline cleared | all 4 behave as described above | | All 21 element files parse; no syntax older iPhones reject; every observed attribute kept | pass | Run the sample yourself with `node sample-site/server.js` and open http://localhost:4173/_sample.
