input.content:
# Arise Church — installing the 14 Sept 2026 fixes in Wix Everything in this folder was tested in the local sample before it came to you (see "What was tested" at the end). Do the steps in order, and **publish only once, at the very end**. Custom elements and page code do not run properly in the Editor or Preview, so check the published site afterwards. The live code as it was before these changes is saved in `files2/live-elements/src/`, `files2/live-backend/` and `files2/live-page-code/`. Pasting those back undoes everything. | Folder | What it holds | |---|---| | `custom-elements/` | 21 element files (bug fixes + CMS hooks on every text block and image) | | `page-code/` | 22 page-code files, one per page, plus `masterPage.js` | | `backend/` | the backend files; three change | | `cms/` | `PageContent-new-rows.csv` to import, `PageContent-all-keys.md` listing every editable spot by page | --- ## Step 1 — CMS (no publish needed) **1a. Five broken images.** These Page Content rows point at image addresses that start `c3b2d0_`, which return "forbidden". The same photos exist under `1f9fa2_` (each address below was checked and loads). Without this edit those spots would show a blank box once the fixed elements are in. Open CMS → Page Content, find each key, and replace the `imageUrl` cell with the address shown: | contentKey | Page | New imageUrl | |---|---|---| | childrens.kids.photo | Children's Ministry | https://static.wixstatic.com/media/1f9fa2_a5448e514cc14ea08cb657e4f1a9cec4~mv2.jpg | | childrens.superkid.logo | Children's Ministry | https://static.wixstatic.com/media/1f9fa2_8c21ef4200d44594bcec41ac5680c2c0~mv2.jpg | | outreach.supplies.image | Outreach | https://static.wixstatic.com/media/1f9fa2_ef28ad94288a4068ac9c2974b4d4d545~mv2.jpg | | leadnetwork.austin.photo | Lead Network | https://static.wixstatic.com/media/1f9fa2_0118a2141a564a909b5c493b2f55211d~mv2.png | | leadnetwork.calloway.photo | Lead Network | https://static.wixstatic.com/media/1f9fa2_1331547403e94f94a08912f08d45d1de~mv2.png | If a row also has a file in its `image` field, that file wins over `imageUrl`; clear it if it shows the wrong photo. **1b. Two copy corrections in existing rows.** | contentKey | Change | |---|---| | alexandria.pastor.bio2 | "Apostle Bryant and **Prophet** Vanessa Sanders" → "Apostle Bryant and **Pastor** Vanessa Sanders" (the rest of Pastor Sheron's paragraph stays as she wrote it). Pastor Vanessa is both Pastor and Prophet, so skip this row if you prefer Pastor Sheron's original wording | | connect.season.hostby | The page is host registration only for now. Put the real host sign-up deadline here, or **clear the text** to hide the deadline wherever it appears | **1c. Add the new editable rows.** CMS → Page Content → More actions → Import → choose `cms/PageContent-new-rows.csv` → **add as new items** (do not replace existing items). The file has **526 rows**: one for every heading, paragraph, button label, card label and photo that did not have a CMS row yet. Each row already holds the text the page shows today, so importing changes nothing you can see. From then on, editing a row's `text` (or `image`) changes that spot on the site. `cms/PageContent-all-keys.md` lists all 578 keys by page, with where each one appears. Notes for editors: - `text` is shown as written. You may use `
` for a line break. Do not type a lone `<`. - Service times keep the day in the value ("Sunday 10:30 AM"). Rows whose label already names the day drop the repeated day automatically. - Seven row labels are shared by several pages and differ between them (for example "Sunday Service" on Home and "Sunday" on Contact). They are **not** in the CSV, because one row sets that label on every page at once. Add one only if you want the same wording everywhere. They are listed at the end of `PageContent-all-keys.md`. - The footer year updates itself and has no row. The Sermons Shorts come from YouTube and have no rows. ## Step 2 — Backend (Velo sidebar → Backend) | File | Action | |---|---| | `backend/youtube.jsw` | Replace the whole file with `backend/youtube.jsw` from this folder | | `backend/events.web.js` | Replace the whole file with `backend/events.web.js` from this folder | | `backend/classes.web.js` | Replace the whole file with `backend/classes.web.js` from this folder | | `backend/events.jsw` | **Delete** — nothing uses it (the Events page imports `events.web.js`) | | `content.web.js`, `http-functions.js`, `gallery.web.js` | Leave as they are — identical to what is live | What the new `youtube.jsw` fixes: - It reads the newest Shorts for the Sermons page. - It asks YouTube for the desktop page. The old file got YouTube's mobile page, so the automatic series detection never worked. - An upcoming scheduled stream no longer counts as live. Without this, the Sermons page would say "Live Now" over a "waiting to start" screen whenever a stream is scheduled. ## Step 3 — Custom elements (Velo sidebar → Public → custom-elements) **First, re-create the Bible file you deleted:** New file → `arise-bible.js` → paste `custom-elements/arise-bible.js` from this folder. Then open the Bible Search page in the Editor, click the custom element → Choose Source and make sure it points at `arise-bible.js`. Then, for each file below, open the file of the same name in Velo, select all, and paste the new file over it: arise-about.js · arise-alexandria.js · arise-childrens.js · arise-classes.js · arise-connect.js · arise-contact.js · arise-creatives.js · arise-events.js · arise-footer.js · arise-header.js · arise-home.js · arise-leaders.js · arise-leadnetwork.js · arise-ministries.js · arise-outreach.js · arise-sermons.js · arise-serve.js · arise-youth.js Optional, not installed today: `arise-service-times-final.js` (the Service Times dropdown for the homepage hero) and `arise-form.js` (reusable form). Both are fixed, CMS-hooked and tested, but placing them is a design decision. ## Step 4 — Page code Open each page in the Editor, open its code panel, select all, and paste the file of the same name from `page-code/`. For the site-wide file use Code panel → Site Code → `masterPage.js`. Home · Arise Church Alexandria · Connect Groups · Creative Arts · Praise and Worship · Musicians · Production · Sound · Media · Social Media and Content · Classes · Past Sermons · Ministries · Events · Contact · Sign Up to Serve! · Meet our Leaders · Children's Ministry · Youth Ministry · Outreach · Lead Network · masterPage.js Pages that need no code: About, Bible Search, Give, Job Board, Information Desk Registration, Podcast, Training. ## Resource: About Git Integration & Wix CLI for Sites ## Article: About Git Integration & Wix CLI ## Article Link: https://dev.wix.com/docs/develop-websites/articles/workspace-tools/developer-tools/git-integration-wix-cli-for-sites/about-git-integration-wix-cli-for-sites ## Article Content: # About Git Integration & Wix CLI for Sites Git Integration & Wix CLI for Sites is a set of tools that allows you to write, test, preview, and publish code for your Wix site using your preferred IDE. Your site code is stored in a GitHub repository, giving you version control and making collaboration easy.
## Code in your preferred IDE Git Integration & Wix CLI for Sites allows you to connect your site to GitHub and develop using your preferred IDE. Wix sets up a repository for your project, which you can clone to your computer or cloud workspace and write code in as you would in any other non-Wix project. Read how to [set up Git integration & Wix CLI for Sites](https://dev.wix.com/docs/develop-websites/articles/workspace-tools/developer-tools/git-integration-wix-cli/setting-up-git-integration-wix-cli). ## Test your code with the Local Editor The [Local Editor](https://dev.wix.com/docs/develop-websites/articles/workspace-tools/developer-tools/git-integration-wix-cli-for-sites/about-the-local-editor) allows you to test changes made to your site in real time. The code in your IDE is synced with the Local Editor so you can test your changes before committing them to your repo. You can also change your site's design in the Local Editor and sync it with your IDE. ## Preview and publish with the Wix CLI for Sites The [Wix CLI for Sites](https://dev.wix.com/docs/develop-websites/articles/workspace-tools/developer-tools/git-integration-wix-cli-for-sites/wix-cli-for-sites-commands) is a tool that allows you to work with your site locally from the terminal. You can use it to build a preview version of your site and publish it. You can also use the CLI to install [npm packages](https://dev.wix.com/docs/develop-websites/articles/coding-with-velo/packages/about-npm-packages) to your site. ## Work with multiple collaborators at once Git Integration & Wix CLI for Sites extends Wix Studio's [concurrent editing](https://support.wix.com/en/article/studio-editor-collaborating-on-a-site) capabilities. Invite other developers as collaborators on your [site](https://support.wix.com/en/article/inviting-people-to-contribute-to-your-site) and your [GitHub repo](https://docs.github.com/en/account-and-profile/setting-up-and-managing-your-personal-account-on-github/managing-access-to-your-personal-repositories/inviting-collaborators-to-a-personal-repository). Multiple developers can work on a site's code at once. ## Version control With Git integration, every change to your site's code is tracked in your GitHub repository, giving you a clear history of edits and the ability to revert to previous versions when needed. This makes it easy to manage updates, resolve conflicts, and maintain a stable development workflow—even when working with multiple collaborators. ## Get started - To get started, read how to [Set Up Git Integration & Wix CLI for Sites](https://dev.wix.com/docs/develop-websites/articles/workspace-tools/developer-tools/git-integration-wix-cli/setting-up-git-integration-wix-cli).

## Resource: Setting Up Git Integration & Wix CLI for Sites ## Article: Setting Up Git Integration & Wix CLI ## Article Link: https://dev.wix.com/docs/develop-websites/articles/workspace-tools/developer-tools/git-integration-wix-cli-for-sites/setting-up-git-integration-wix-cli-for-sites ## Article Content: # Set Up Git Integration & Wix CLI for Sites [Git Integration & Wix CLI for Sites](https://dev.wix.com/docs/develop-websites/articles/workspace-tools/developer-tools/git-integration-wix-cli-for-sites/about-git-integration-wix-cli-for-sites) allows you to write, test, preview, and publish code for your Wix site from your preferred IDE. This article explains how to set up Git Integration & Wix CLI for Sites by connecting your site to GitHub, cloning your site's GitHub repository to your computer, and installing the Wix CLI for Sites. > **Note:** You can also clone the repo to a cloud IDE workspace, then install and use the Wix CLI for Sites there. ### Before you begin Make sure you have the following tools installed before you start: * [Git](https://git-scm.com/download) * [Node](https://nodejs.org/en/download/), version 20.11 or later. * [npm](https://docs.npmjs.com/downloading-and-installing-node-js-and-npm) or [yarn](https://yarnpkg.com/getting-started/install) * An SSH key [added to your GitHub account](https://docs.github.com/en/authentication/connecting-to-github-with-ssh/adding-a-new-ssh-key-to-your-github-account). ## Step 1 | Connect your site to GitHub To write your site's code locally from your computer, first create a GitHub repo to store your site's code and connect it to your site.
**Important:** * You can't connect your site to GitHub if you have [Velo Packages](https://dev.wix.com/docs/develop-websites/articles/coding-with-velo/packages/working-with-velo-packages) set up on your site. This feature isn't supported when using Git Integration & Wix CLI for Sites. However, you can connect your site to GitHub if you have [npm packages](https://dev.wix.com/docs/develop-websites/articles/coding-with-velo/packages/about-npm-packages) installed on your site. * Once you connect your site to GitHub be careful not to delete your site's repo or revoke the Velo app's access to this repo. These actions may cause your site's GitHub connection to stop working even if you restore the repo or reinstall the app.
If you haven't already done so, click ![Code icon](https://github.com/wix-incubator/wix-code-docs/assets/50321691/2c41d3df-930f-4e0f-966f-038742adceed) and then **Start Coding** (Wix Studio), or enable [Velo Dev Mode](https://support.wix.com/en/article/about-velo-by-wix#to-enable-velo-on-your-site) (Wix Editor). 1. Go to the GitHub Integration section of your editor: + **Wix Studio:** In the Code sidebar, click **GitHub** then **Connect to GitHub**. ![Connect to GitHub](https://wixmp-833713b177cebf373f611808.wixmp.com/images/2975acc2f04e09b584d7445e64fb1107.png) + **Wix Editor:** Click the **GitHub Integration** ![](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/89579857/184818043-6a791df6-9f83-4183-ba2f-63d8c32a6cf7.png) icon in the Code sidebar and then **Connect to GitHub**. 3. Click **Continue**. ![](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/89579857/188311147-436ecd17-c717-440c-93ae-feb7685eddeb.png) 4. Click **Sign In**. Follow the prompts to sign in to your GitHub account and authorize Velo to create a new repo for you. 5. Choose an owner and enter a name for the new repo to connect to your site. Optionally, you can add a custom description as well. Click **Create**. ![](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/89579857/188311195-229312f8-3fd5-4c6d-902d-b746f0c9915d.png) 6. Click **Install** to start installing the Velo GitHub app on your new repo. This app allows your site to communicate with GitHub. You may need to authenticate your identity in GitHub before continuing. 7. Make sure that both **Only select repositories** and your new repo are selected. You're welcome. The Wix API itself can't publish code, but Wix has a route that would let me do nearly all of the install for you. It's called Git Integration and it works with your Wix Editor site.

What it takes:
1. **You connect the site.** In the Editor, turn on Velo Dev Mode, open the GitHub Integration icon in the Code sidebar, and choose Connect to GitHub. That involves signing in to GitHub, which only you can do.
2. **I place the code.** Once the site's code lives in a GitHub repository, I can clone it here and put every fixed file in its exact place: elements, backend and page code. I already know each page's internal file name from the live site.
3. **I test it in Wix's own Local Editor.** That runs on the real site before anything goes live, which is closer to reality than my sample site.
4. **You approve, then it publishes.** The Wix command-line tool publishes from here once you've logged it in to your Wix account. I'd still wait for your go-ahead before publishing.

Two things to know first:
- **The Editor's code panel becomes read-only** while the site is connected, because GitHub becomes the source of the code. You can disconnect at any time.
- **Velo Packages block the connection.** Regular npm packages are fine. I haven't checked whether your site uses Velo Packages.

The CMS steps would still happen in the CMS: the five image URLs, the deadline row and the CSV import. The GitHub connection only carries code.

Everything the code imports is one of two kinds:

- **Wix SDK packages starting with `@wix/`**, like `@wix/events`, `@wix/portfolio` and `@wix/automations`. These are npm packages, and Wix's docs say npm packages don't block the GitHub connection.

125	Wix classic Editor + Velo. Wix has no REST API for layout, so whole pages ship as **Velo custom elements** in `public/custom-elements/`. Pattern: CMS collection → backend web module (`content.web.js` etc.) → page code (`$w.onReady`, retry-until-ready, sets a `data-*` attribute with `JSON.stringify`) → element reads the attribute and renders. Forms in the elements POST to `/_functions/ariseForm` (`backend/http-functions.js` → `FormSubmissions` collection first, then Contacts + an Automations custom trigger).

## Viewing and Editing Memory

You can see exactly what Claude remembers in Settings > Memory. Everything Claude remembers is listed under Topics. Select any topic to read it, then use the edit icon to change it or select "Delete" to remove it.

Fix something in one topic and the change applies to every conversation from then on.

To add specific information into Claude's memory, go to Settings > Capabilities, click "View and edit your memory," and add that information as an edit. Additionally, you can update memory directly from a chat by telling Claude what you'd like it to remember, change, or forget, and the update applies to your next conversation.

## Importing Memory

From the home screen, click "Get started" on the "Import memory to Claude" card. The import flow will display a prompt along with a text box where you can paste the results. Paste the exported text from your previous AI provider into the text box and click the "Add to memory" button to submit it. Claude will extract key information and store it as individual memory edits.

Publishes a site.

This method does not require any direct arguments. When using an API key, a `wix-site-id` header with the site's GUID must be included. The method returns an empty object upon successful execution. A possible error is `SITE_IS_NOT_DEFINED_AS_PUBLISHABLE` (HTTP 428), which occurs if the site is not a template or headless structure.

1.  **Q: What does the `publishSite` method do?**
    A: It makes saved changes to a Wix site available on the internet.
2.  **Q: Does `publishSite` require any parameters in the request body?**
    A: No, the `publishSite` method does not require any direct arguments.
3.  **Q: How do I specify which site to publish when using an API key?**
    A: You must include a `wix-site-id` header with the site's GUID.
4.  **Q: What is the URL for the `publishSite` method?**
    A: The URL is `https://www.wixapis.com/site-publisher/v1/site/publish`.
5.  **Q: What error might I encounter if my site cannot be published?**
    A: You might receive a `SITE_IS_NOT_DEFINED_AS_PUBLISHABLE` error if the site isn't a template or headless structure.

# About Extending Wix Sites          

[Extending websites on Wix](https://dev.wix.com/docs/develop-websites) combines regular Wix site creation with the ability to add custom code to extend out-of-the-box functionality. You can build your site using Wix's visual editor and then enhance it with custom JavaScript code to add specific features, integrate with external services, or create unique user experiences.

## Which APIs to use

Extend Wix sites using the [Wix JavaScript SDK](https://dev.wix.com/docs/sdk) and [Velo APIs](https://dev.wix.com/docs/velo). These tools allow you to add custom functionality, integrate with Wix business solutions, and build rich, interactive experiences directly in your Wix site.

> **Note:** [Wix REST APIs](https://dev.wix.com/docs/rest) aren't intended for use when extending Wix sites.

## Transition from Velo to the Wix JavaScript SDK

Until recently, custom code on Wix sites was written using Velo APIs. You can now also use the Wix JavaScript SDK for both extending sites and app building with Blocks. If you have sites with existing Velo code, you might want to [migrate](https://dev.wix.com/docs/develop-websites/articles/coding-with-velo/develop-with-the-sdk/migrate-from-velo-to-the-sdk) them to use the SDK instead.

Wix's transition to the SDK is a gradual process. At this stage, the SDK doesn't currently support the functionality of all Velo APIs for extending sites or for app creation with Blocks. For functionality that isn't yet supported in the SDK, use Velo APIs alongside the SDK.

The Velo APIs that you should still use at this stage fall into 2 categories:

- APIs that are imported from Velo modules.
- APIs that work by file and method name conventions.

>   - For files with public URLs, you can call [Import File](https://dev.wix.com/docs/rest/assets/media/media-manager/files/import-file).
>   - For files without public URLs, you can call [Generate File Upload URL](https://dev.wix.com/docs/rest/assets/media/media-manager/files/generate-file-upload-url).

## Upload flow

The code for generating an upload URL and sending it an upload request varies depending on your context. For example, the code for a dashboard page of a self-hosted app differs slightly from the code for a headless site.

However, in all scenarios, you need to perform the following steps:

1. Get the file to upload.
1. Get the name of the file.
1. Get the MIME type of the file.
1. Generate an upload URL and upload token using the [Generate File Resumable Upload URL](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/assets/media/media-manager/files/generate-file-resumable-upload-url) method.
1. Create a new [tus](https://tus.io/) upload using the generated upload URL.
1. Start the tus upload.

# About Extending Wix Sites          

[Extending websites on Wix](https://dev.wix.com/docs/develop-websites) combines regular Wix site creation with the ability to add custom code to extend out-of-the-box functionality. You can build your site using Wix's visual editor and then enhance it with custom JavaScript code to add specific features, integrate with external services, or create unique user experiences.

## Which APIs to use

Extend Wix sites using the [Wix JavaScript SDK](https://dev.wix.com/docs/sdk) and [Velo APIs](https://dev.wix.com/docs/velo). These tools allow you to add custom functionality, integrate with Wix business solutions, and build rich, interactive experiences directly in your Wix site.

> **Note:** [Wix REST APIs](https://dev.wix.com/docs/rest) aren't intended for use when extending Wix sites.

## Transition from Velo to the Wix JavaScript SDK

Until recently, custom code on Wix sites was written using Velo APIs. You can now also use the Wix JavaScript SDK for both extending sites and app building with Blocks. If you have sites with existing Velo code, you might want to [migrate](https://dev.wix.com/docs/develop-websites/articles/coding-with-velo/develop-with-the-sdk/migrate-from-velo-to-the-sdk) them to use the SDK instead.

Wix's transition to the SDK is a gradual process. At this stage, the SDK doesn't currently support the functionality of all Velo APIs for extending sites or for app creation with Blocks. For functionality that isn't yet supported in the SDK, use Velo APIs alongside the SDK.

The Velo APIs that you should still use at this stage fall into 2 categories:

- APIs that are imported from Velo modules.
- APIs that work by file and method name conventions.

## Article Content:

# Upload a File with a Generated Resumable File Upload URL

To upload a file to a site's Media Manager with a URL that allows you to pause and resume an upload, you can call [Generate File Resumable Upload URL](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/assets/media/media-manager/files/generate-file-resumable-upload-url). This call returns a signed `uploadUrl` and `uploadToken` that you can then use to upload a file.

> **Notes:**
>
> - If you don't specifically need a resumable upload experience, you can call one of the following options instead of calling Generate File Resumable Upload URL:
>   - For files with public URLs, you can call [Import File](https://dev.wix.com/docs/rest/assets/media/media-manager/files/import-file).
>   - For files without public URLs, you can call [Generate File Upload URL](https://dev.wix.com/docs/rest/assets/media/media-manager/files/generate-file-upload-url).

## Upload flow

The code for generating an upload URL and sending it an upload request varies depending on your context. For example, the code for a dashboard page of a self-hosted app differs slightly from the code for a headless site.

However, in all scenarios, you need to perform the following steps:

1. Get the file to upload.
1. Get the name of the file.
1. Get the MIME type of the file.
1. Generate an upload URL and upload token using the [Generate File Resumable Upload URL](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/assets/media/media-manager/files/generate-file-resumable-upload-url) method.
1. Create a new [tus](https://tus.io/) upload using the generated upload URL.
1. Start the tus upload.

# Arise Church — installing the 14 Sept 2026 fixes in Wix Everything in this folder was tested in the local sample before it came to you (see "What was tested" at the end). Do the steps in order. **Publish once, at step 5, and import the new CMS rows only after that publish.** Custom elements and page code do not run properly in the Editor or Preview, so check the published site. The live code as it was before these changes is saved in `files2/live-elements/src/`, `files2/live-backend/` and `files2/live-page-code/`. Pasting those back undoes everything. | Folder | What it holds | |---|---| | `custom-elements/` | 21 element files (bug fixes + CMS hooks on every text block and image) | | `page-code/` | 22 page-code files, one per page, plus `masterPage.js` | | `backend/` | the backend files; four change | | `cms/` | `PageContent-new-rows.csv` to import in step 6, `PageContent-all-keys.md` listing every editable spot by page | --- ## Step 1 — CMS fixes (no publish needed) **1a. Five broken images.** These Page Content rows point at image addresses that start `c3b2d0_`, which return "forbidden". The same photos exist under `1f9fa2_` (each address below was checked and loads). Without this edit those spots would show a blank box once the fixed elements are in. Open CMS → Page Content, find each key, and replace the `imageUrl` cell with the address shown: | contentKey | Page | New imageUrl | |---|---|---| | childrens.kids.photo | Children's Ministry | https://static.wixstatic.com/media/1f9fa2_a5448e514cc14ea08cb657e4f1a9cec4~mv2.jpg | | childrens.superkid.logo | Children's Ministry | https://static.wixstatic.com/media/1f9fa2_8c21ef4200d44594bcec41ac5680c2c0~mv2.jpg | | outreach.supplies.image | Outreach | https://static.wixstatic.com/media/1f9fa2_ef28ad94288a4068ac9c2974b4d4d545~mv2.jpg | | leadnetwork.austin.photo | Lead Network | https://static.wixstatic.com/media/1f9fa2_0118a2141a564a909b5c493b2f55211d~mv2.png | | leadnetwork.calloway.photo | Lead Network | https://static.wixstatic.com/media/1f9fa2_1331547403e94f94a08912f08d45d1de~mv2.png | **1b. Two copy decisions in existing rows.** | contentKey | Change | |---|---| | alexandria.pastor.bio2 | Optional. This paragraph mentions **Pastor Vanessa Sanders** as "Apostle Bryant and Prophet Vanessa Sanders". Pastor Vanessa is both Pastor and Prophet, so the sentence is accurate as written; change "Prophet Vanessa Sanders" to "Pastor Vanessa Sanders" only if you want her pastor title there. Nothing on the site calls Pastor Sheron a prophet | | connect.season.hostby | The page is host registration only for now. Put the real host sign-up deadline here, or **clear the text** to hide the deadline wherever it appears | ## Step 2 — Backend (Velo sidebar → Backend) | File | Action | |---|---| | `backend/content.web.js` | Replace the whole file with `backend/content.web.js` from this folder | | `backend/youtube.jsw` | Replace the whole file with `backend/youtube.jsw` from this folder | | `backend/events.web.js` | Replace the whole file with `backend/events.web.js` from this folder | | `backend/classes.web.js` | Replace the whole file with `backend/classes.web.js` from this folder | | `backend/events.jsw` | **Delete** — nothing uses it (the Events page imports `events.web.js`) | | `http-functions.js`, `gallery.web.js` | Leave as they are — identical to what is live | What the changed backend files fix: - `content.web.js` now reads every Page Content row. The old file stopped at 500 rows. Step 6 brings the collection to 571 rows, so on the old file some rows, possibly the service times, would silently disappear. - `youtube.jsw` reads the newest Shorts for the Sermons page, asks YouTube for the desktop page (the old file got the mobile page, so automatic series detection never worked), and no longer treats an upcoming scheduled stream as live. Without that last fix the Sermons page would say "Live Now" over a "waiting to start" screen. - `events.web.js` sorts events by real date; `classes.web.js` shows a price of 0 as Free. ## Step 3 — Custom elements (Velo sidebar → Public → custom-elements) **First, re-create the Bible file you deleted:** New file → `arise-bible.js` → paste `custom-elements/arise-bible.js` from this folder. Then open the Bible Search page in the Editor, click the custom element → Choose Source and make sure it points at `arise-bible.js`. Then, for each file below, open the file of the same name in Velo, select all, and paste the new file over it: arise-about.js · arise-alexandria.js · arise-childrens.js · arise-classes.js · arise-connect.js · arise-contact.js · arise-creatives.js · arise-events.js · arise-footer.js · arise-header.js · arise-home.js · arise-leaders.js · arise-leadnetwork.js · arise-ministries.js · arise-outreach.js · arise-sermons.js · arise-serve.js · arise-youth.js Optional, not installed today: `arise-service-times-final.js` (the Service Times dropdown for the homepage hero) and `arise-form.js` (reusable form). Both are fixed, CMS-hooked and tested, but placing them is a design decision. ## Step 4 — Page code Open each page in the Editor, open its code panel, select all, and paste the file of the same name from `page-code/`. For the site-wide file use Code panel → Site Code → `masterPage.js`. Home · Arise Church Alexandria · Connect Groups · Creative Arts · Praise and Worship · Musicians · Production · Sound · Media · Social Media and Content · Classes · Past Sermons · Ministries · Events · Contact · Sign Up to Serve! · Meet our Leaders · Children's Ministry · Youth Ministry · Outreach · Lead Network · masterPage.js Pages that need no code: About, Bible Search, Give, Job Board, Information Desk Registration, Podcast, Training. (About and Bible Search still get their CMS text, from `masterPage.js`.) Every page file finds its element even if the element ID is not the one written at the top, so you do not need to look up IDs. Each file writes a line in the browser console when data arrives, and a warning if it cannot find the element. ## Step 5 — Publish and check Publish, then open each page on the live site. On a computer, press F12 → Console to see the log lines. - [ ] Home — no stray code text under "Who We Are"; campus rows read "Sunday Service 10:30 AM" (no doubled day); Alexandria shows Prayer 6:00 PM and Bible Study 6:45 PM - [ ] Header menu on a phone — Sunday times, Glory Night, phone number; footer bottom line shows both campuses - [ ] Contact — "Sunday 10:30 AM" not "Sunday Sunday"; Directions open in a new tab - [ ] Praise & Worship, Musicians, Production, Sound, Media, Social Media & Content — department name as the heading, department tabs underneath, team cards - [ ] Serve — 7 positions (Praise & Worship and Production & Sound included) - [ ] Sermons — series band "The Kingdom · Culture of Giving"; the clips section shows the newest Shorts from YouTube (the console says "8 newest Shorts"); the badge says "Latest Service" unless a stream is actually playing - [ ] Events — "Previous Events" button no longer goes to a 404 - [ ] Bible Search — search "John 3:16" returns the verse - [ ] Children's, Youth, Outreach, Lead Network — page renders, photos show - [ ] Connect Groups — only "Host a Group" shows; a host sign-up submits (a row appears in CMS → Form Submissions) ## Step 6 — After publishing: add the new editable rows CMS → Page Content → More actions → Import → choose `cms/PageContent-new-rows.csv` → **add as new items** (do not replace existing items). The file has **526 rows**: one for every heading, paragraph, button label, card label and photo that did not have a CMS row yet. Each row already holds the text the page shows today, so importing changes nothing you can see. From then on, editing a row's `text`, or `imageUrl` for a photo, changes that spot on the site. `cms/PageContent-all-keys.md` lists all 578 keys by page, with where each one appears. The CSV's empty `image` column can be skipped when Wix asks how to map columns; the collection uses `imageUrl`. Do this only after step 5, so the new `content.web.js` that reads every row is already live. Then check: change one Page Content row's text, and see it change on the page after a refresh. Notes for editors: - `text` is shown as written. You may use `
` for a line break. Do not type a lone `<`. - To change a photo, paste the Wix media address of the new image into `imageUrl`. - Service times keep the day in the value ("Sunday 10:30 AM"). Rows whose label already names the day drop the repeated day automatically. - Seven row labels are shared by several pages and differ between them (for example "Sunday Service" on Home and "Sunday" on Contact). They are **not** in the CSV, because one row sets that label on every page at once. Add one only if you want the same wording everywhere. ## Method Description:
Patches an item in a collection.

Call this method when you need a partial update and want fields that aren't mentioned in the request to stay unchanged. Patch requests are also the right place to use `fieldModifications` actions such as `SET_FIELD` for a direct replacement and `INCREMENT_FIELD` for arithmetic changes. For different behavior, you can call:

- [Update Data Item](https://dev.wix.com/docs/rest/business-solutions/cms/data-items/update-data-item) to replace the full payload rather than patch part of it.
- [Save Data Item](https://dev.wix.com/docs/rest/business-solutions/cms/data-items/save-data-item) for upsert behavior, meaning to create if the item doesn't exist and update if it does.

This method modifies the specified item's existing data. Unlike [`Update Data Item`](https://dev.wix.com/docs/rest/business-solutions/cms/data-items/update-data-item), only the fields specified in the request are modified. Data that isn't explicitly modified remains unchanged.

To patch an item, specify its ID, the ID of the collection that contains it, and the modifications you want to apply. If an item is found in the specified collection with the specified ID, that item is patched. If the collection doesn't contain an item with that ID, the request fails.

> **Notes**:
> - When an item is patched, its `data._updatedDate` property is updated to the current date and time.
> - You can only patch items in [collections created by Wix users](https://support.wix.com/en/article/cms-formerly-content-manager-creating-a-collection). Items in [Wix app collections](https://dev.wix.com/docs/develop-websites/articles/databases/wix-data/collections/working-with-wix-app-collections-and-code) cannot be patched.
## Method Permissions:
WIX_DATA.PATCH
## Method Permissions Scopes:
Write Data Items: SCOPE.DC-DATA.WRITE

## Method Schema Summary:
The `patchDataItem` method allows for partial updates to an existing item within a collection. It modifies only the specified fields, leaving other fields unchanged.

**Method Parameters:**

*   **`dataCollectionId`**: (String, required) The GUID of the collection containing the item to be patched.
*   **`patch`**: (Object, required) Contains the details of the patch operation.
    *   **`dataItemId`**: (String, required) The GUID of the item to patch.
    *   **`fieldModifications`**: (Array of `FieldModification` objects, required) A list of modifications to apply to the item's fields. Each `FieldModification` object must include:
        *   **`fieldPath`**: (String, required) The path to the field to modify (e.g., `title` or `address.street`).

## Method Description:
Patches one or more items in a collection.

Call this method when you need to apply partial changes to many items and want each item to keep fields that aren't mentioned in the request. This is also the right bulk surface for `fieldModifications` actions such as `SET_FIELD` and `INCREMENT_FIELD`: increments and decrements apply atomically on the server, so concurrent writers don't have to read the current value first or coordinate to avoid lost updates. For different behavior, you can call:

- [Bulk Update Data Items](https://dev.wix.com/docs/rest/business-solutions/cms/data-items/bulk-update-data-items) to replace each item's full payload rather than patch part of it.
- [Save Data Item](https://dev.wix.com/docs/rest/business-solutions/cms/data-items/save-data-item) per item for upsert behavior, meaning to create the item if its ID doesn't exist yet and update it if it does.

This method modifies the existing data of one or more items. Unlike [`Bulk Update Data Item`](https://dev.wix.com/docs/rest/business-solutions/cms/data-items/bulk-update-data-items), only the fields specified in the request are modified. Data that isn't explicitly modified remains unchanged.

To patch items, specify the ID of the collection that contains them. For each item, specify its ID and the modifications you want to apply. If the item is found in the specified collection with the specified ID, that item is patched. If no such item is found, the response's `results` array contains a corresponding item whose `itemMetadata.error` property contains details about the error.

Learn more about [Wix Data error codes](https://dev.wix.com/docs/rest/business-solutions/cms/wix-data-error-codes).

> **Notes**:
> - When an item is patched, its `data._updatedDate` property is updated to the current date and time.
> - You can only patch items in [collections created by Wix users](https://support.wix.com/en/article/cms-formerly-content-manager-creating-a-collection). Items in [Wix app collections](https://dev.wix.com/docs/develop-websites/articles/databases/wix-data/collections/working-with-wix-app-collections-and-code) cannot be patched.
> - Calling this method triggers the [`Data Item Updated`](https://dev.wix.com/docs/rest/business-solutions/cms/data-items/data-item-updated) event for each patched item.

# About the Data Items API

> **Note for app developers:** Wix Data APIs require the site's [code editor](https://dev.wix.com/docs/develop-websites/articles/get-started/development-environments) to be enabled. If you are building a Wix app, add a [data collections extension](https://dev.wix.com/docs/build-apps/develop-your-app/extensions/backend-extensions/data-collections/about-data-collections-extensions) to automatically enable the code editor and create data collections when your app is installed on a site.


The Data Items API allows you to access and manage items in a Wix site's data collections.

With the Data Items API, you can:

- Create and manage data items in a site's collections.
- Publish and unpublish data items through an editorial draft lifecycle.
- Retrieve data items from a collection individually or with filtering and sorting queries.
- Create and manage reference fields.
- Update or remove many items asynchronously by filter.
- Perform aggregations and calculations on data in collections.
- Run advanced aggregation pipelines for complex data transformations.
- Truncate a data collection, removing all its contents.

The Data Items API only works with existing collections. To create and manage data collections, use the [Data Collections API](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/business-solutions/cms/collection-management/data-collections).

The Background Tasks API allows you to create and manage tasks that process [data items](https://dev.wix.com/docs/rest/business-solutions/cms/data-items/introduction). Tasks run in the background, so they don't block the user's ability to work on their site while items are processed.

Each task has a different type, which determines the kind of processing the task performs on the items of the specified collection. You can create tasks to:

- Copy data from one field to another for all items in a collection.
- Update field data for items that match a specified filter.
- Delete all items in a collection that match a specified filter.
- Update the publish status for items that match a specified filter.

## Method Description:
Patches one or more items in a collection.

Call this method when you need to apply partial changes to many items and want each item to keep fields that aren't mentioned in the request. This is also the right bulk surface for `fieldModifications` actions such as `SET_FIELD` and `INCREMENT_FIELD`: increments and decrements apply atomically on the server, so concurrent writers don't have to read the current value first or coordinate to avoid lost updates. For different behavior, you can call:

- [Bulk Update Data Items](https://dev.wix.com/docs/rest/business-solutions/cms/data-items/bulk-update-data-items) to replace each item's full payload rather than patch part of it.
- [Save Data Item](https://dev.wix.com/docs/rest/business-solutions/cms/data-items/save-data-item) per item for upsert behavior, meaning to create the item if its ID doesn't exist yet and update it if it does.

To patch items, specify the ID of the collection that contains them. For each item, specify its ID and the modifications you want to apply. If the item is found in the specified collection with the specified ID, that item is patched. If no such item is found, the response's `results` array contains a corresponding item whose `itemMetadata.error` property contains details about the error.

# About the Data Items API

> **Note for app developers:** Wix Data APIs require the site's [code editor](https://dev.wix.com/docs/develop-websites/articles/get-started/development-environments) to be enabled. If you are building a Wix app, add a [data collections extension](https://dev.wix.com/docs/build-apps/develop-your-app/extensions/backend-extensions/data-collections/about-data-collections-extensions) to automatically enable the code editor and create data collections when your app is installed on a site.


The Data Items API allows you to access and manage items in a Wix site's data collections.

With the Data Items API, you can:

- Create and manage data items in a site's collections.
- Publish and unpublish data items through an editorial draft lifecycle.
- Retrieve data items from a collection individually or with filtering and sorting queries.
- Create and manage reference fields.
- Update or remove many items asynchronously by filter.
- Perform aggregations and calculations on data in collections.
- Run advanced aggregation pipelines for complex data transformations.
- Truncate a data collection, removing all its contents.

The Data Items API only works with existing collections. To create and manage data collections, use the [Data Collections API](https://dev.wix.com/docs/api-reference/business-solutions/cms/collection-management/data-collections).

> **Note for app developers:** Wix Data APIs require the site's [code editor](https://dev.wix.com/docs/develop-websites/articles/get-started/development-environments) to be enabled. The Background Tasks API allows you to create and manage tasks that process [data items](https://dev.wix.com/docs/rest/business-solutions/cms/data-items/introduction). Tasks run in the background, so they don't block the user's ability to work on their site while items are processed.

Each task has a different type, which determines the kind of processing the task performs on the items of the specified collection. You can create tasks to:

- Copy data from one field to another for all items in a collection.
- Update field data for items that match a specified filter.
- Delete all items in a collection that match a specified filter.
- Update the publish status for items that match a specified filter.

## Before you begin

It's important to note the following points before starting to code:

- To run a task of the type `UPDATE_PUBLISH_STATUS`, the collection must have the Publish plugin to [control item visibility](https://support.wix.com/en/article/cms-controlling-live-site-item-visibility-from-your-collection).

message.content:
This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation.

Summary:
1. Primary Request and Intent:
   - **Who and where.** Bradly (dyerbradly2@gmail.com) maintains arisecenla.church (Wix classic Editor + Velo custom elements) for Arise Church. The project folder is `D:\projects\Arise Church Website`.
   - **Session arc.** Full audit, then saving the live code, then "fix any issues in the existing codes, don't break them, and test them before finalizing". After that: "do a code test to make sure it works before I add the new files to Wix" and "it should use CMS to update text, images, etc."
   - **Content decisions:**
     - Pastor Vanessa Sanders is Pastor and Prophet.
     - Pastor Sheron Turner is NOT a prophet.
     - Connect Groups is currently host registration only; joining comes later.
     - There is no Thelma.
     - The Sermons page must show the newest YouTube Shorts.
   - **Access and memory.** Save everything to memory, both Claude Code memory and Claude account Settings memory. View the sample site on his phone.
   - **Wix access.** He "Gave you full Wix access". His most recent instruction, "Yes fix them!", approved fixing the five broken Page Content image URLs.
   - **Standing constraints (preserve verbatim intent):**
     - No design or code change without explicit permission.
     - Nothing goes onto the live Wix site without Bradly's go-ahead, and publishing is his call. Never call the Wix Publish Site API without his explicit go-ahead: the saved Editor state lacks arise-bible.js, which he deleted, so publishing would break Bible Search.
     - Always write "Arise Church".
     - Use the live copy; don't invent copy.
     - Never quote the ArchivedFormSubmissions/Import1 rows (PII).
     - Test before handing over.
     - Every editable fact comes from the CMS.
     - Phrase titles so they can't be misread: Pastor Sheron is not a prophet.

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - **Element architecture.** Wix Velo custom elements live in `public/custom-elements`. Page code sets `data-*` JSON attributes. Elements `applyContent()` for `data-ck` (text via innerHTML), `data-ci` (images) and `data-ckrow`. Containers marked `data-cms-source` are exempt from the CMS coverage check.
   - **Velo selectors.** `$w('#id')` returns a single element with no `.length`. `$w('*')` is not a valid selector; `$w('CustomElement')` returns an array. Header and footer types are `$w.Header` / `$w.Footer`.
   - **Recovering live code.** Wix bundler source maps: `bundler.wix-code.com/<metaSiteId>/undefined/<gridAppId>/custom-elements/arise-<tag>.js.map` and `.../pages/<pageId>.js.map`, with the original code in `sourcesContent`.
   - **Wix Data REST:**
     - query: `POST /wix-data/v2/items/query`
     - get: `GET /wix-data/v2/items/{id}?dataCollectionId=`
     - bulk insert: `POST /wix-data/v2/bulk/items/insert`, max 1000 items
     - bulk patch: `POST /wix-data/v2/bulk/items/patch` with `patches[{dataItemId, fieldModifications[{fieldPath, action:'SET_FIELD', setFieldOptions:{value}}]}]`
     - publish: `POST /site-publisher/v1/site/publish` (don't use)
     - There is no API for uploading Velo code.
   - **Deploying code.** Git Integration & Wix CLI for Sites works on Wix Editor sites and is blocked only by `@velo/*` Velo Packages. The site's packages are all `@wix/*`.
   - **YouTube scraping:**
     - A desktop Chrome UA is required; a generic UA gets m.youtube.com.
     - RSS feeds return 404.
     - The Shorts tab uses `shortsLockupViewModel`, `shorts-shelf-item-<id>` and `primaryText.content`, with thumbnail `i.ytimg.com/vi/<id>/frame0.jpg`.
     - Playlists use `lockupViewModel` with `contentId` and `lockupMetadataViewModel.title.content`.
     - The `/live` page points at upcoming streams too. Treat it as live only when playabilityStatus is OK, isLive is true, and it is not isUpcoming.
   - **Sample site.** A zero-dependency Node server serves the fixed set with the real page code via `velo-shim.js` and backend mocks, and the old render at `/_before/`. Browser helpers: `__audit`, `__cmsTest`, `__remountTest`, `__roundTrip`, `__snapshot`, `__errors`.
   - **Scripting lessons:**
     - A dollar-apostrophe sequence in a String.replace replacement inserts the rest of the string; use split/join.
     - Write scripts that contain backticks with the Write tool, not bash heredocs.
     - Workflows that hit usage limits leave files half-edited; snapshot first and reset.
     - Headless Edge clips pages narrower than about 500px.

3. Files and Code Sections:
   - **`files2/arise-fixed-2026-09-14/`** is the deliverable. The zip `files2/arise-fixed-2026-09-14.zip` was rebuilt at 4:44 AM on 9/15.
     - **`INSTALL.md`** was fully rewritten.
       - Step 1: CMS fixes. 1a is marked DONE on 15 Sept, with the backup path. 1b covers the bio2 optional wording and the hostby date or clear.
       - Step 2: backend. Replace content.web.js, youtube.jsw, events.web.js and classes.web.js; delete events.jsw; leave http-functions.js and gallery.web.js.
       - Step 3: re-create arise-bible.js, then paste the 18 elements.
       - Step 4: page code, 22 files including masterPage.
       - Step 5: publish and checklist.
       - Step 6: AFTER publishing, import the 526-row CSV, because the new content.web.js reads every row.
       - Also: notes for editors (change photos via imageUrl; there is no image field), small wording changes, settled items, still open (Tioga), and the tests table (19/19, 44/44, 35/35, 20/20).
     - **`backend/content.web.js`** — getPageContent is now paged:
       ```js
       export const getPageContent = webMethod(Permissions.Anyone, async () => {
         const items = [];
         try {
           let res = await q('PageContent').limit(1000).find(opts);
           items.push.apply(items, res.items);
           let pages = 0;
           while (res.hasNext() && pages++ < 20) {
             res = await res.next();
             items.push.apply(items, res.items);
           }
         } catch (e) {
           console.error('getPageContent:', e);
         }
         const out = {};
         items.forEach((r) => { ... { text: r.text || '', image: imgUrl(r.image) || r.imageUrl || '' } });
       ```
     - **`backend/youtube.jsw`** was rewritten:
       - `YT_HEADERS` with a desktop Chrome UA and Accept-Language en-US; shared `getPage(path)`.
       - `getLiveVideoId` requires `status === 'OK' && liveNow && !upcoming`, checked within the videoDetails slice.
       - `listPlaylists(html)` supports lockupViewModel plus the legacy layout; `getCurrentSeries` keeps the IGNORE list and the "series" rule.
       - `parseShorts(html)` plus `getLatestShorts(limit)`: max 24, 10-minute cache, keeps the last good list.
     - **`backend/events.web.js`** has the real-date sort, `startsAt`, registrationDisabled, and no debug log. **`backend/classes.web.js`** has no debug log and `amount > 0 ? '$'+value : 'Free'`.
     - **`custom-elements/`** has 21 files with fixes and CMS hooks. Key additions:

# Arise Church — installing the 14 Sept 2026 fixes in Wix Everything in this folder was tested in the local sample before it came to you (see "What was tested" at the end). Do the steps in order. **Publish once, at step 5, and import the new CMS rows only after that publish.** Custom elements and page code do not run properly in the Editor or Preview, so check the published site. The live code as it was before these changes is saved in `files2/live-elements/src/`, `files2/live-backend/` and `files2/live-page-code/`. Pasting those back undoes everything. | Folder | What it holds | |---|---| | `custom-elements/` | 21 element files (bug fixes + CMS hooks on every text block and image) | | `page-code/` | 22 page-code files, one per page, plus `masterPage.js` | | `backend/` | the backend files; four change | | `cms/` | `PageContent-new-rows.csv` to import in step 6, `PageContent-all-keys.md` listing every editable spot by page | --- ## Step 1 — CMS fixes (no publish needed) **1a. Five broken images — DONE on 15 Sept 2026.** Claude updated these rows through the Wix connector with Bradly's go-ahead and read them back to confirm; nothing else in the rows changed. The old values are saved in `audit/cms-backups/PageContent-image-rows-before-2026-09-15.json`. Skip this step. For the record: the rows pointed at image addresses starting `c3b2d0_`, which return "forbidden"; the same photos exist under `1f9fa2_`, and each new address below was checked and loads. | contentKey | Page | New imageUrl | |---|---|---| | childrens.kids.photo | Children's Ministry | https://static.wixstatic.com/media/1f9fa2_a5448e514cc14ea08cb657e4f1a9cec4~mv2.jpg | | childrens.superkid.logo | Children's Ministry | https://static.wixstatic.com/media/1f9fa2_8c21ef4200d44594bcec41ac5680c2c0~mv2.jpg | | outreach.supplies.image | Outreach | https://static.wixstatic.com/media/1f9fa2_ef28ad94288a4068ac9c2974b4d4d545~mv2.jpg | | leadnetwork.austin.photo | Lead Network | https://static.wixstatic.com/media/1f9fa2_0118a2141a564a909b5c493b2f55211d~mv2.png | | leadnetwork.calloway.photo | Lead Network | https://static.wixstatic.com/media/1f9fa2_1331547403e94f94a08912f08d45d1de~mv2.png | **1b. Two copy decisions in existing rows.** | contentKey | Change | |---|---| | alexandria.pastor.bio2 | Optional. This paragraph mentions **Pastor Vanessa Sanders** as "Apostle Bryant and Prophet Vanessa Sanders". Pastor Vanessa is both Pastor and Prophet, so the sentence is accurate as written; change "Prophet Vanessa Sanders" to "Pastor Vanessa Sanders" only if you want her pastor title there. Nothing on the site calls Pastor Sheron a prophet | | connect.season.hostby | The page is host registration only for now. Put the real host sign-up deadline here, or **clear the text** to hide the deadline wherever it appears | ## Step 2 — Backend (Velo sidebar → Backend) | File | Action | |---|---| | `backend/content.web.js` | Replace the whole file with `backend/content.web.js` from this folder | | `backend/youtube.jsw` | Replace the whole file with `backend/youtube.jsw` from this folder | | `backend/events.web.js` | Replace the whole file with `backend/events.web.js` from this folder | | `backend/classes.web.js` | Replace the whole file with `backend/classes.web.js` from this folder | | `backend/events.jsw` | **Delete** — nothing uses it (the Events page imports `events.web.js`) | | `http-functions.js`, `gallery.web.js` | Leave as they are — identical to what is live | What the changed backend files fix: - `content.web.js` now reads every Page Content row. The old file stopped at 500 rows. Step 6 brings the collection to 571 rows, so on the old file some rows, possibly the service times, would silently disappear. - `youtube.jsw` reads the newest Shorts for the Sermons page, asks YouTube for the desktop page (the old file got the mobile page, so automatic series detection never worked), and no longer treats an upcoming scheduled stream as live. Without that last fix the Sermons page would say "Live Now" over a "waiting to start" screen. - `events.web.js` sorts events by real date; `classes.web.js` shows a price of 0 as Free. ## Step 3 — Custom elements (Velo sidebar → Public → custom-elements) **First, re-create the Bible file you deleted:** New file → `arise-bible.js` → paste `custom-elements/arise-bible.js` from this folder. Then open the Bible Search page in the Editor, click the custom element → Choose Source and make sure it points at `arise-bible.js`. Then, for each file below, open the file of the same name in Velo, select all, and paste the new file over it: arise-about.js · arise-alexandria.js · arise-childrens.js · arise-classes.js · arise-connect.js · arise-contact.js · arise-creatives.js · arise-events.js · arise-footer.js · arise-header.js · arise-home.js · arise-leaders.js · arise-leadnetwork.js · arise-ministries.js · arise-outreach.js · arise-sermons.js · arise-serve.js · arise-youth.js Optional, not installed today: `arise-service-times-final.js` (the Service Times dropdown for the homepage hero) and `arise-form.js` (reusable form). Both are fixed, CMS-hooked and tested, but placing them is a design decision. ## Step 4 — Page code Open each page in the Editor, open its code panel, select all, and paste the file of the same name from `page-code/`. For the site-wide file use Code panel → Site Code → `masterPage.js`. Home · Arise Church Alexandria · Connect Groups · Creative Arts · Praise and Worship · Musicians · Production · Sound · Media · Social Media and Content · Classes · Past Sermons · Ministries · Events · Contact · Sign Up to Serve! · Meet our Leaders · Children's Ministry · Youth Ministry · Outreach · Lead Network · masterPage.js Pages that need no code: About, Bible Search, Give, Job Board, Information Desk Registration, Podcast, Training. (About and Bible Search still get their CMS text, from `masterPage.js`.) Every page file finds its element even if the element ID is not the one written at the top, so you do not need to look up IDs. Each file writes a line in the browser console when data arrives, and a warning if it cannot find the element. ## Step 5 — Publish and check Publish, then open each page on the live site. On a computer, press F12 → Console to see the log lines. - [ ] Home — no stray code text under "Who We Are"; campus rows read "Sunday Service 10:30 AM" (no doubled day); Alexandria shows Prayer 6:00 PM and Bible Study 6:45 PM - [ ] Header menu on a phone — Sunday times, Glory Night, phone number; footer bottom line shows both campuses - [ ] Contact — "Sunday 10:30 AM" not "Sunday Sunday"; Directions open in a new tab - [ ] Praise & Worship, Musicians, Production, Sound, Media, Social Media & Content — department name as the heading, department tabs underneath, team cards - [ ] Serve — 7 positions (Praise & Worship and Production & Sound included) - [ ] Sermons — series band "The Kingdom · Culture of Giving"; the clips section shows the newest Shorts from YouTube (the console says "8 newest Shorts"); the badge says "Latest Service" unless a stream is actually playing - [ ] Events — "Previous Events" button no longer goes to a 404 - [ ] Bible Search — search "John 3:16" returns the verse - [ ] Children's, Youth, Outreach, Lead Network — page renders, photos show - [ ] Connect Groups — only "Host a Group" shows; a host sign-up submits (a row appears in CMS → Form Submissions) ## Step 6 — After publishing: add the new editable rows CMS → Page Content → More actions → Import → choose `cms/PageContent-new-rows.csv` → **add as new items** (do not replace existing items). The file has **526 rows**: one for every heading, paragraph, button label, card label and photo that did not have a CMS row yet. Each row already holds the text the page shows today, so importing changes nothing you can see. From then on, editing a row's `text`, or `imageUrl` for a photo, changes that spot on the site. `cms/PageContent-all-keys.md` lists all 578 keys by page, with where each one appears. The CSV's empty `image` column can be skipped when Wix asks how to map columns; the collection uses `imageUrl`. Do this only after step 5, so the new `content.web.js` that reads every row is already live. Then check: change one Page Content row's text, and see it change on the page after a refresh. Notes for editors: - `text` is shown as written. You may use `
` for a line break. Do not type a lone `<`. - To change a photo, paste the Wix media address of the new image into `imageUrl`. - Service times keep the day in the value ("Sunday 10:30 AM"). Rows whose label already names the day drop the repeated day automatically. - Seven row labels are shared by several pages and differ between them (for example "Sunday Service" on Home and "Sunday" on Contact). They are **not** in the CSV, because one row sets that label on every page at once. Add one only if you want the same wording everywhere. They are listed at the end of `PageContent-all-keys.md`. - The footer year updates itself and has no row. The Sermons Shorts come from YouTube and have no rows. ## Small wording changes you may notice These places now show the CMS value instead of text that was typed into the code, so wording matches the rest of the site: - Bible Search, bottom box: "Sunday 10:30 AM in Pineville, Sunday 10:00 AM in Alexandria. Glory Nights Monday 7:00 PM." - Sermons, Glory Nights box: "Monday 7:00 PM" (was "Mondays 7:00 PM") - Contact, main campus rows: the Glory Night, Wednesday and Corporate Prayer times come from the CMS - Alexandria and Home: the two Wednesday rows are labelled "Prayer" and "Bible Study" - Sermons, clips section: tall Short-shaped cards with the Short's title, in place of the eight hand-picked clips with descriptions. The section heading "Clips & Announcements" can be renamed in the CMS (`sermons.clips.heading`) ## Settled on 14–15 Sept - **Pastor Vanessa Sanders is Pastor and Prophet.** The Leaders entry ("Apostle · Pastor & Prophet") is correct as it is. - **Pastor Sheron Turner is not a prophet**, and nothing on the site calls her one. - **Sermons shows the newest Shorts automatically.** Upload a Short to the Arise Church channel and it appears on the Sermons page within about 10 minutes. The built-in list, used only if YouTube cannot be reached, is the 8 newest Shorts as of 14 Sept. - **Connect Groups is host registration only.** The "Join a Group" tab, the join form and the "Join This Group" buttons stay hidden. When groups are scheduled, open joining with one CMS row: add `connect.join.open` with the text `yes`, and publish. - There is no Thelma; the 14 Creative Members are complete. ## Still open (not changed in the code) - "Tioga, Louisiana" in Pastor Sheron's second paragraph (the main campus address is Pineville) - Portfolio projects for the galleries and the homepage news panel are empty; Online Programs has no published class ## What was tested | Test | Result | |---|---| | Backend files under node with Wix mocked: Page Content reads every row past 1000; image conversion; event sorting and buttons; forms; and the YouTube readers against real channel pages saved on 14 Sept (newest Shorts, series detection, an upcoming stream not counted as live, a live stream counted) (`node sample-site/tests/backend.test.mjs`) | 19 of 19 pass | | Every page-code file, right element ID and wrong element ID, plus masterPage and Sermons with and without Shorts (`node sample-site/tests/page-code.test.mjs`) | 44 of 44 pass | | Every sample page at desktop width: no script errors, no blank elements, Wix remove-and-re-add leaves the page unchanged, every CMS hook shows a changed CMS value, importing the CSV leaves the page unchanged, nothing worse than today's code (overflow, missing alt text, broken images, contrast, tap targets, heading count) | 35 of 35 pages pass | | The same checks at phone width (390 px) | 20 of 20 pages pass | | Connect Groups: default, with groups listed, joining opened from the CMS, deadline cleared | all 4 behave as described above | | Sermons Shorts: 8 cards from YouTube, 4 columns on desktop and 2 on a phone, links open the Short, all 8 thumbnails load, built-in list shows when YouTube is unreachable | pass | | All 21 element files parse; no syntax older iPhones reject; every observed attribute kept | pass | Run the sample yourself with `node sample-site/server.js` and open http://localhost:4173/_sample.

- I install code myself by pasting Velo files in the Wix Editor. Nothing goes on the live site without my go-ahead.
